Questioned spending extensive time on a deliverable memo and presentation when council already sets spending priorities.
conflicts.side_b_position: Support the five-month engagement to design targeting under 60% AMI and long-term compliance
side_b_arguments: Designing monitoring for rental and homeownership subsidies across multiple properties requires careful planning, justifying five months rather than rushing in three.
Council previously adopted a transit corridor resolution targeting 15% affordable units at 60% AMI or below, making careful target-demographic analysis essential.
conflicts.resolution: Final vote omitted in transcript digest gap after 00:39:00

conflicts.issue: Stonehill Estates and Ravenstone Infrastructure Cost Split ($1,134,000 City Contribution)
conflicts.summary: Following an adverse federal court ruling on subdivision performance bonds, Council split 6-1 over approving an option placing $1,134,000 (slightly over 50 percent) of street and stormwater completion costs on the City while assessing remaining costs against homeowners.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the $1,134,000 City contribution option and move forward to a formal public hearing.
side_a_arguments: City Attorney defended the original bonds as standard when issued despite the judge's ruling and tightened future bond language.
The $1,134,000 option covered slightly more than half the completion burden while advancing a resolution before the public hearing.
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed the $1,134,000 cost-split motion (lone dissenter; residents sought full credit for tax/roadway funds already paid).
side_b_arguments: Public speakers contended the City held sufficient face-value bond coverage and homeowners should receive full credit rather than assessment liens.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 6-1 by show of hands (individual Aye and Nay voters not named in the audio transcript); staff directed to schedule a public hearing in August or September.

conflicts.issue: NC Highway 54 Traffic Saturation, Tree Loss, and Lack of Affordable Housing in Highway 54 Residential (A14-00005 & Z14-00018)
conflicts.summary: The 21.72-acre plan amendment and rezoning for 320 market-rate multifamily units at NC Highway 54 and Revere Road passed on split 4-2 voice votes after sharp questioning over corridor traffic congestion, wooded land clearing, and zero affordable housing units.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve changing 21.72 acres from Office to Medium-High Density Residential / RS-M(D) for 320 multifamily units.
side_a_arguments: Multifamily residential has strong market demand and generates slightly fewer peak-hour trips than existing Office zoning.

The applicant's traffic impact analysis showed adequate peak-hour intersection service and provided NC 54 right-of-way dedication, a bike lane, center turn-lane continuity, and a $21,500 donation to Durham Public Schools.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose adding 320 market-rate multifamily units along an un-widened NC 54 corridor without affordable housing commitments.
side_b_arguments: Mayor Bill Bell warned that approving more developments on NC 54 before state widening risks severe cumulative traffic gridlock and removes wooded areas.
Council Member Steve Schewel objected that all 320 units were market-rate with zero affordable housing units, urging stronger local affordable housing tools.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-2 on voice votes (with two audible nays out of six members present; individual vote names not called).

conflicts.issue: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Erwin Terrace at LaSalle Street (A130010)
conflicts.summary: Pat Young and Aaron Cain presented A130010 to reclassify 19.64 acres at Erwin Road and LaSalle Street to the Compact Neighborhood Tier near a planned light rail station, noting a 9-1 Planning Commission recommendation and ongoing SASI/affordable housing toolbox work due January 7. Applicant team members Patrick Byker, Dan Jewell, Robinson Everett Jr., and lender Keith Wells argued the density was essential for transit and job growth, explained that lenders would not finance an air-rights wrapped parking deck project with a 15% below-market set-aside, and offered $25,000 toward the city's affordable housing toolbox plus a one-year pause on redeveloping Poplar Manor. Seven speakers from Durham People's Alliance, Durham CAN, and Durham Community Land Trustees urged Council to defer approval to negotiate permanent affordable units, arguing market-rate affordability at Duke Manor was already eroding. Mayor Bell, Eugene Brown, and Cora Cole-McFadden supported approval because 79.5% of existing units within a half-mile were already affordable and state law prohibited mandatory inclusionary zoning, whereas Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel voted no to favor holistic station-area planning and stronger affordability commitments.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 5-2)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (5-2)

conflicts.issue: Durham City-County Planning Commission Appointment
conflicts.summary: Council cast a 5-1 split ballot on the Durham City-County Planning Commission appointment, with five votes for the winning appointee (transcribed as 'admin') and one vote for Eric Milman.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support the winning nominee (5 votes)
side_a_arguments: Majority of five Council members selected the winning Planning Commission nominee on the appointment ballot.
conflicts.side_b_position: Support Eric Milman (1 vote)
side_b_arguments: One Council member cast a ballot for Eric Milman.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 5-1 on ballot; individual council members' ballot selections were not read aloud in the transcript.

conflicts.issue: Item 38: Zoning Map Change — Harmony Road II Revisions (Z1400008)
conflicts.summary: Planner Steve Medlin and Standard Pacific attorney Patrick Byker presented Z1400008 to remove 2006 committed elements requiring an off-site asphalt trail connecting the 185-unit Chamberlain/Harmony Road II subdivision to the Woodcroft trail network and an on-site southern mulch trail, after Woodcroft's Community Association refused all proposed easements over a year of talks. Instead, Standard Pacific signed a private agreement with seven Chamberlain residents to spend the $75,000 trail budget (less rezoning/legal/consulting costs) on Chamberlain common-area recreation improvements. Council Member Don Moffitt reluctantly supported the change on grounds that off-site commitments should not be required, and Mayor Bell and Eugene Brown cited Woodcroft's refusal and Chamberlain neighbors' support. Council Members Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel dissented (5-2), arguing that decommitting the trail sacrificed a vital off-road Safe Route to Southwest Elementary School and future Third Fork Creek Trail connection.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 5-2)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (5-2)

conflicts.issue: Durham Cultural Advisory Board Appointment Tie-Breaker (Item 3)
conflicts.summary: In a tie-breaker runoff ballot between two candidates who had tied with three votes each, Council split 3-2 with three votes for Dale and two votes for Diane Standart.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support Dale for Cultural Advisory Board (3 votes)
side_a_arguments: Three Council members cast tie-breaker ballots for Dale.
conflicts.side_b_position: Support Diane Standart for Cultural Advisory Board (2 votes)
side_b_arguments: Two Council members cast tie-breaker ballots for Diane Standart.
conflicts.resolution: Dale received 3 votes to Diane Standart's 2 votes among the five participating Council members (with Cora Cole-McFadden and Don Moffitt absent); individual ballot choices were not announced in the transcript.

conflicts.issue: Item 25: Zoning Map Change — Hope Valley Farms Pod BB Revisions (Z13-0012 / Murphy USA) (Initial Vote)
conflicts.summary: Planning staff presented Murphy USA's request on 6.77 acres at 1051 Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway to remove 2009 proffers barring fuel sales and convenience stores and to remove redundant roadway commitments already built by others. Attorneys Patrick Byker and Lewis Cheek emphasized a 0.8 opacity landscape buffer, 500-foot separation from the nearest townhomes, and $2 million in new tax base. Elm Grove Townhouse Association representative Aida Len O'Tougou requested a continuance because HOA board elections delayed neighborhood review, though Planning staff verified that first-class mail notices were sent to 45 nearby owners and the Elm Grove HOA in April. Following debate over notice and neighborhood compatibility, Council initially approved the rezoning 5-2 with Diane Catotti and Don Moffitt voting no.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 5-2)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (5-2)

conflicts.issue: Item 28: Resolution Approving Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS) Recommendations
conflicts.summary: Dan Jewell, president of Durham Area Designers (DAD), addressed Item 28, urging Council to emphasize that the Durham Traffic Separation Study's limited scenarios were conceptual rather than recommended solutions and warning that some proposals could harm city livability unless subjected to immediate project-specific studies and public engagement. Council Member Steve Schewel argued against adopting the resolution—even with caveats—because accepting recommendations such as closing Dillard Street creates public expectations that those closures are settled policy, urging Council to merely receive the report instead. The motion to approve the resolution failed on a 3-3 tie vote with Diane Catotti absent.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 3-3)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (3-3)

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bill Bell excused and outgoing Council Member Eugene Brown absent), the Durham City Council honored departing members, heard community testimony on marijuana policing disparities, and reviewed greenway and financial reports. Triangle J Council of Governments Executive Director Lee Worsley recognized Eugene Brown for a decade of regional leadership and acknowledged Diane Catotti's final work session. During Citizens Matters, Self-Help Credit Union President Randy Chambers and advocates cited data showing 80% of misdemeanor marijuana charges involved African Americans versus 10% whites and urged a citation-only policy, while Council members noted new state legislative limits on local directives regarding immigration and police enforcement. Council also heard Part 2 of the Minority Report to the Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative, reviewed the Alta five-trail greenway study, heard the FY 2015-16 Q1 financial report, approved Consent Items 1-9 (5-0), and entered closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Mayor Bill Bell
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council called the roll with five members present (Cora Cole-McFadden presiding, Diane Catotti, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel; Eugene Brown absent) and voted unanimously to grant Mayor Bill Bell an excused absence.

agenda_items.title: Triangle J Council of Governments Recognition of Eugene Brown & Diane Catotti
agenda_items.discussion_summary: TJCOG Executive Director Lee Worsley honored outgoing Council Member Eugene Brown (in his absence) for his service since 2005 as delegate, Secretary/Treasurer, Vice Chair, Chair in 2012, and budget/search committee member, while also recognizing outgoing Council Member Diane Catotti at her final work session.

agenda_items.title: Racial Disparities in Misdemeanor Marijuana Enforcement & State Sanctuary Preemption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Randy Chambers (Self-Help Credit Union) and coalition speakers presented dataset findings indicating 80% of misdemeanor marijuana charges targeted African Americans compared to 10% whites, urging Council to require 100% citation enforcement rather than arrests. Council discussion also clarified Durham had never designated itself a 'sanctuary city' and noted the General Assembly's recent action restricting local governments from directing police on state law enforcement.

agenda_items.title: Minority Report to the Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative (Part 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A presenter delivered Part 2 of the minority report to the Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative, reviewing post-1965 family structure trends, single-parent household rates (citing Durham at 27%, highest among major North Carolina cities), and fatherhood engagement work. Council members reflected on systemic 'isms' and the experiences of single mothers raising families.

agenda_items.title: Alta Greenway Trails Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the Alta greenway study funded at the end of the budget cycle to evaluate five priority trails identified by Open Space and Trails and city staff, providing cost estimates needed to incorporate greenways alongside the Beltline Trail in future Capital Improvement Plans.

agenda_items.title: FY 2015-16 First Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson, joined by Jim Reingruber and David Boyd, presented the Q1 financial report showing projected fund balance usage reduced from $3.2M to $1.5M, General Fund spending $870,000 below budget due partly to 17 Public Works vacancies, ~$500,000 in Stormwater savings, Transit on budget, and an upcoming House Bill 255 amendment creating a special revenue fund for inspections. Council suggested illustrating annual household tax costs per $200,000 home value for transit and solid waste at the February budget retreat.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved setting the regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1 through 9 by unanimous voice vote and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Mayor Bill Bell
votes.notes: Eugene Brown was also absent, as noted at 00:12:02.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved excused absence for Mayor Bill Bell from the work session.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-9)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('Aye, without reservation').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved placing Items 1 through 9 on the Consent Agenda for the next regular Council meeting.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for the stated statutory purpose.

meetings.title: Durham City Council November 16, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council approved City Manager Tom Bonfield's priority revisions (7-0) and the consent agenda (7-0), including the 2016 meeting schedule, hydrant meter fee updates, and a HUD Fair Housing contract. Police Chief Jose Lopez presented the 2015 Third Quarter Crime Report—noting a 29% rise in Priority 1 calls, slower response times (6:06 average vs. 5:48 target), and 37 operational vacancies—and faced pointed council questioning over data showing Black residents comprised over 80% of misdemeanor marijuana arrests despite council reforms. Council also held a public hearing on HOPWA funding barriers for shelter and housing providers and approved economic development incentive agreements for Frontier Communications of the Carolinas LLC (7-0) and WillowTree, Inc. (up to $70,500 for 98 jobs, passed by voice/electronic vote without opposition).

agenda_items.title: Schewel Challenge Report, Priority Items, and Boy Scout Troop 424 Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel reported on the fourth annual 5-mile Schewel Challenge race along the American Tobacco Trail with 47 city employees and 14 family members and commended the city's Desk to 5K wellness initiative. City Manager Tom Bonfield presented priority revisions to Item 4 (fire facilities mowing contract), Items 10 and 11 (revealing the company names for Project Ironman and Project Cavalier), and supplemental Item 14 (Q3 crime report plus updates on Civilian Police Review Board and Human Relations Commission recommendations), which passed 7-0. Mayor Bell also recognized Boy Scouts from Troop 424.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously adopted the consent agenda covering Tourism Development Authority reappointments, the 2016 City Council meeting schedule, a hydrant meter deposit fee schedule ordinance, the fire facilities mowing contract, easement sales to 101 West Chapel Hill Street Partners LLC, and the FY 2015-16 HUD Fair Housing contract.

agenda_items.title: 2015 Third Quarter Crime Report and Marijuana Arrest Disparity Questioning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez presented the January–September 2015 crime report, reporting a 29% surge in Priority 1 calls, an average Priority 1 response time of 6 minutes 6 seconds (missing the 5:48 target and the 57% under-5-minute benchmark), 37 operational vacancies due to recruits in training, patrol district staffing ranging from 42% to 72%, and his October White House discussion with President Obama on DPD diversion programs. During questioning, a council member cited a report showing Black residents accounted for over 80% of misdemeanor marijuana charges (and 46% among those under 25 despite being 15% of the population) even after council reforms; Lopez stated he had not read the report, denied marijuana arrests were a DPD priority, and suggested concerned individuals should not smoke marijuana.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on HOPWA Funding Allocation and Administrative Barriers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle-section omission in the transcript digest, Council concluded a public hearing on Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA) funding where a speaker urged Council to remove administrative funding barriers preventing specialized emergency shelter and affordable housing organizations from participating fully. Council questioned Community Development staff regarding the transition from state administration to City of Durham entitlement jurisdiction and whether upcoming one-year funds could support housing rather than solely services, noting policy barriers affecting agencies such as the Durham Crisis Response Center.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Frontier Communications of the Carolinas LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Daryl Solomon of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development presented a job creation incentive agreement with Frontier Communications of the Carolinas LLC, noting that media coverage had prematurely reported the deal prior to Council action. Durham Chamber of Commerce Vice President of Economic Development Ted Conner spoke in support of the project during the public hearing, and Council approved the agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: WillowTree, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Daryl Solomon presented an incentive agreement not to exceed $70,500 with mobile strategy and software firm WillowTree, Inc. (represented by Tobias Dengel) projected to create 98 jobs by the end of 2018 at an average annual salary of $84,118 with full benefits and use of the NCWorks Career Center. Ted Conner of the Chamber of Commerce highlighted that roughly 40% of WillowTree's hires come from coding schools rather than computer science degrees, creating workforce opportunities with Durham Public Schools and Durham Tech, and Council approved the agreement after closing the vote without dissent.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (tally not announced aloud in transcript)

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Items 4, 10, 11, and Supplemental Item 14)
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented priority revisions correcting exhibit numbering on Item 4, inserting company names into Items 10 and 11, and adding the Q3 crime report and Civilian Police Review Board / Human Relations Commission updates as Item 14. Council approved the priority items 7-0.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Frontier Communications of the Carolinas LLC (Item 10)

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell shortly after the November 3 municipal election, the Durham City Council hosted a sister-city delegation from Kostroma, Russia, heard a developer's appeal over a speed-hump driveway conflict, and debated housing mix options for city-owned land near Durham Station. On Item 13 (the FY 2016 Durham Station / Jackson Street RFP), Council members disagreed over whether to leave the RFP open to market-rate and mixed-income proposals until the affordable housing consultant's February report or require an 80% affordable / 20% market-rate housing split. Council also reviewed Human Relations Commission recommendations on city employee grievance finality and random drug testing, heard updates from the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority and the Poverty Reduction Initiative, and approved priority items, the regular meeting agenda, and a closed session by unopposed voice votes (4-0 among members recorded at roll call).

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items & Post-Election Congratulations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members congratulated newly elected Council Members Jillian Johnson and Charlie Reece following the election. The City Manager presented priority items—allowing 15 minutes for Sister Cities of Durham (Item 15) and noting Scott Bunt (Item 17) would not attend—which Council approved unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Sister Cities Presentation: Kostroma, Russia Delegation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives from Durham's sister city Kostroma, Russia—including tourism officials and the 'Snow Maiden' cultural ambassador—addressed Council on fairy-tale tourism, festival organization, minority/diaspora engagement, and charitable work with disadvantaged children.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: 2016 Schedule, Meter Fees, Fire Landscaping & HUD Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including the DCVB Tourism Development Authority appointment (Item 1), the 2016 Council meeting schedule (Item 2), a water meter deposit fee schedule ordinance (Item 3), a Fire Department landscaping contract awarded to a minority firm (Item 4), easements for 101 West Chapel Hill Street Partners LLC (Item 5), and a FY 2015-16 HUD Fair Housing contract (Item 6).

agenda_items.title: Driveway Permit Denial & Speed Hump Conflict (16 K.A. Street / 122 Hillside)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A residential builder appealed Public Works' July 6, 2015 denial of a driveway permit and hold on a Certificate of Occupancy tied to a conflict with an existing speed hump. Public Works staff cited City Code Sec. 62-97 barring driveway approaches from interfering with municipal traffic-control facilities and stated the approved plot plans omitted the speed hump.

agenda_items.title: Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority (RDU) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: RDU representative Mike Silver briefed Council on airport traffic and air service expansion, highlighting 9.5 million passengers in 2014 (including 1.5 million international travelers), roughly 400 daily operations, and new Delta nonstop flights to Salt Lake City and Paris.

agenda_items.title: Human Relations Commission & Employee Recommendations on Grievances and Drug Testing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers and HRC representatives reviewed recommendations on city employee grievance procedures—criticizing the City Manager's final authority even when a second-tier review panel rules in an employee's favor—and called for neutral outside arbitrators, ending mandatory/random drug testing alleged to be applied disparately, and tracking race, gender, and age in disciplinary and promotion logs.

agenda_items.title: FY 2016 Durham Station / Jackson Street Excess Land RFP Options
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD's Kevin Dick outlined three RFP options for excess land near Durham Station pairing civic/office space with either affordable housing, mixed-income housing, or market-rate housing. Council members disagreed over whether to keep all options open until the affordable housing consultant reports in February versus insisting on an 80% affordable / 20% market-rate residential ratio without office space.

agenda_items.title: Poverty Reduction Initiative: Father Absence Data
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A presenter discussed statistics indicating 27%-30% of local families lack an involved father in the home (12th highest in the nation) and urged addressing root family support factors alongside youth assistance programs.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1-8; GBA Item 14; GBA Public Hearing Items 9-11) and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items (Item 15 Sister Cities 15-Minute Slot; Item 17 Removal)
votes.notes: Four members (Bell, Catotti, Davis, Schewel) recorded responses at roll call; an excused absence was noted at 00:00:30 while Eugene Brown, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Don Moffitt did not record responses at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved adjusting time for Sister Cities presentation (Item 15) and noting Scott Bunt's absence (Item 17).

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-8; GBA 14; Public Hearings 9-11)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote among members recorded at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Set the agenda for the upcoming regular City Council meeting.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for the stated statutory purpose.

disagreements.issue: Durham Station / Jackson Street Excess Land RFP Housing Ratio and Flexibility
disagreements.summary: Council members split over whether the Durham Station / Jackson Street RFP should invite flexible market-rate and mixed-income proposals pending the February affordable housing consultant report or mandate an 80% affordable / 20% market-rate housing ratio.
disagreements.side_a_position: Keep all three RFP options open—including mixed-income and market-rate options—and avoid arbitrary ratios before receiving the February affordable housing consultant report.
side_a_arguments: Setting strict income breakdowns (e.g., 30%/60%/80% AMI) prematurely without financing data would be arbitrary.
An open RFP lets developers show feasible financing stacks and wait for the consultant's recommendations before Council evaluates proposals.
disagreements.side_b_position: Commit to an 80% affordable / 20% market-rate target and prioritize maximizing affordable housing units without office space.
side_b_arguments: Prior direction sought to skew heavily toward low- and moderate-income housing with no more than 20% market-rate units.
Following through on the 80/20 commitment avoids drifting away from affordable housing goals.
disagreements.resolution: Staff noted Council could weight scoring points toward desired housing ratios and requested Council direction before finalizing the RFP.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session (Technical Issues - First 5 minutes missing)
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell in a broadcast missing its first five minutes due to technical issues, the Durham City Council reviewed utility right-of-way permit fees, Water Management facility plans, and code enforcement priorities. A coalition of regulated utility and telecom companies requested additional time to review Kimley-Horn's $1.6 million budget breakdown and statutory cost-pass-through concerns before Council adopted a proposed 100% cost-recovery utility-cut fee schedule ($357,400 vs. $114,000 existing revenue). Council also reviewed designs for a two-story Water Management operations facility, heard Council Member Eugene Brown urge action on a neglected property across from NC Central University, granted excused absences to Cora Cole-McFadden and Don Moffitt for the remainder of the session, and set the regular meeting agenda by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Consent Items Review: Downtown Waterline & Durham Bulls Athletic Park Events

agenda_items.title: Right-of-Way / Utility Cut Permit Fee Schedule & Utility Coalition Request

meetings.title: Durham City Council October 19, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council presented proclamations for National Lead Poisoning Prevention Week and Conflict Resolution Day, added two supplemental economic development incentive agreements (Projects Cavalier and Ironman) as priority items (7-0), and approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 11 (7-0), including a resolution supporting Syrian refugee resettlement in Durham and a report on child sex trafficking. Council unanimously approved the Denfield Street annexation for True Covenant Baptist Church (7-0) after hearing an adjacent owner's runoff concerns, removed local historic landmark designation from West Village Complex Parcel L (LD1500001, 7-0) after weighing its 50% property tax deferral against redevelopment plans, approved preliminary incentive agreements for Project Cavalier (unanimous) and Project Ironman (7-0), and approved acquiring the former Duke Diet and Fitness Center property (7-0) as an urban wetland/stormwater site with potential future park amenities.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations (Lead Poisoning Prevention & Conflict Resolution) and Council Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented a National Lead Poisoning Prevention Week proclamation to PEACH program director Lenore Smith, noting a Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative survey finding that about 70% of Northeast Central Durham residents in older housing needed interior repairs, and a Conflict Resolution Day proclamation to the Elna B. Spaulding Conflict Resolution Center for peer mediation in eight Durham schools and truancy court. Council Member Eddie Davis reported on volunteer brush clearing at Geer Cemetery ahead of the 150th anniversary of the 13th Amendment, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden thanked the City Manager for assisting students at Lakeview School.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (26 & 27) and Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield added supplemental Items 26 and 27 (preliminary economic development incentive agreements for Project Cavalier and Project Ironman), which Council approved 7-0. Council then adopted the consent agenda 7-0—pulling Item 11 (Duke Diet & Fitness Center acquisition) for discussion—covering FY 2015-16 budget carryovers, temporary special-event street closing rules, Jordan Lake Partnership support, Lake Michie advance land acquisition, Achievement Academy lease/services, a report on child sex trafficking, and a resolution supporting Syrian refugee resettlement in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Denfield Street / True Covenant Baptist Church
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following an omitted middle segment in the digest, Council heard public testimony on the Denfield Street annexation for True Covenant Baptist Church. Diane King spoke in favor of the church's plans, while adjoining landowner Samuel Mebane stated he did not oppose the church itself but raised concerns about 50 years of tires, motor parts, and contaminated runoff draining from 4512–4516 Denfield Street into a nearby creek. Council approved the annexation and its consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: West Village Complex Parcel L Local Historic Landmark Designation Removal (LD1500001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Pat Young presented an application to remove local historic landmark status from West Village Complex Parcel L, noting a 6-0 recommendation from the Historic Preservation Commission and preliminary redevelopment discussions by the owner. Council Member Diane Catotti asked about the consequences of removing Certificate of Appropriateness oversight, and another council member pointed out that retaining landmark designation on redeveloped property would entitle the owner to a 50% property tax reduction compared to 100% taxation if removed. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval, which passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Preliminary Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Project Cavalier
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office of Economic and Workforce Development Director Kevin Dick presented a preliminary incentive agreement for Project Cavalier within the community redevelopment area. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval and a council member praised the incentives as a bargain while urging future agreements to offer stronger incentives for hiring city residents. The item passed without opposition.

agenda_items.title: Preliminary Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Project Ironman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the preliminary economic development incentive agreement for Project Ironman. A council member requested separating custom-eligibility on-the-job training grant funds from the city incentive in the final agreement, to which staff agreed. Council approved the preliminary agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Acquisition of Former Duke Diet and Fitness Center Property

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation: Denfield Street Property (True Covenant Baptist Church)

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Denfield Street Property

votes.item_title: Local Historic Landmark Designation Removal: West Village Complex Parcel L (LD1500001)

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden after Council excused Mayor Bill Bell's absence, the Durham City Council recognized juvenile justice progress, heard school crossing guard pay concerns, and reviewed long-term capital needs. Cole-McFadden presented a proclamation to Juvenile Crime Prevention Council chair Warren Langley noting an 84% reduction in Durham County juvenile detention admissions, while Council Member Steve Schewel highlighted E.K. Powe Elementary's Walk and Roll to School event and added supplemental Item 25 supporting Syrian refugee resettlement in Durham. Following a crossing guard pay appeal during Citizens Matters, Budget Director Bertha Johnson presented long-term Capital Improvement Program (CIP) projections showing a $17.7 million General Fund surplus above the $20 million minimum reserve, prompting discussion of park restrooms, failed developments, the athletic tournament site, greenway trails, Fire Station 18 timing, and ADA elevator upgrades at the Durham Armory. All procedural motions—excusing Mayor Bell, setting the agenda, and entering closed session—passed by unopposed voice votes.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Mayor Bill Bell & Juvenile Crime Prevention Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved an excused absence for Mayor Bill Bell by voice vote and conducted roll call. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden then presented a proclamation to Warren Langley honoring the Durham County Juvenile Crime Prevention Council and citing an 84% decline in juvenile detention admissions, asking that copies be shared with the County and School Board.

agenda_items.title: Walk and Roll to School, Election Costs & Supplemental Item 25 (Syrian Refugees)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel shared photos of roughly 100 E.K. Powe Elementary students participating in the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission's Walk and Roll to School event. Members also noted municipal election costs rising to ~$200,000, and the Clerk announced supplemental Item 25—a resolution supporting Syrian refugee resettlement in Durham requested by Schewel.

agenda_items.title: Road Reconfiguration Update & Consent/Public Hearing Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated Council on the NCDOT University Drive/Chapel Hill Road resurfacing reconfiguration (converting five lanes to three lanes with a center turn lane, bike lanes, and parking). Council reviewed consent items including FY 2014-15 carryovers (Item 4), Lake Michie land acquisition (Item 10), acquisition of the former Duke Diet & Fitness Center at 808 West Trinity Avenue (Item 11), Achievement Academy lease (Item 12), child sex trafficking resolution (Item 15), and planning public hearings (Items 16-19).

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: School Crossing Guards Compensation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Millicent Rogers spoke on behalf of Durham school crossing guards regarding long-standing lack of pay raises and concern for student safety. Staff referenced an HR memo evaluating pay competitiveness for consideration during the upcoming budget cycle.

agenda_items.title: Long-Term Capital Needs & CIP Priorities Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff presented long-term capital needs and reported a projected $17.7 million General Fund surplus above the 12% ($20 million) minimum fund balance. Council members highlighted priorities including park restroom replacements, failed and struggling developments ($2.8M funded plus $1M+ unfunded), organics recycling and scale house replacement, advancing the athletic tournament site into the first five years, Alta-studied greenway trails, Fire Station 17 vs. future Fire Station 18, and Durham Armory ADA elevator upgrades.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointment Ballots, Setting the Agenda & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council announced ballot tallies for appointments to the Workforce Development Board (6 votes) and Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners (6 votes and 5 votes). Council then voted by voice vote to set the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1-13, 15, and 25; GBA Public Hearing Items 16-19) and to enter closed session.

votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition; Eugene Brown and Steve Schewel joined after initial roll call and participated in the session.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Passed by unopposed voice vote with Bill Bell excused.

meetings.title: Durham City Council October 5, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council presented proclamations for Imagine a Day Without Water, National Arts and Humanities Month (featuring Piedmont Laureate James Maxey), and Long-Term Care Residents' Rights, and unanimously approved the consent agenda (7-0) including making the Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee an official committee and selling property interests for Parkside at Morris Street. Council opened Item 4 regarding a letter to GoTriangle endorsing the recommended preferred alternative for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Draft EIS (modified per Council Member Eddie Davis's input) before an omitted middle portion of the transcript digest. Council subsequently unanimously approved the Hanover Point Subdivision rezoning (7-0) removing an unbuildable East Horseshoe Road widening commitment, adopted UDO Text Amendment TC1500005 on accessory structures and home occupations (7-0), and approved a $6 million, 15-year economic development incentive agreement with Wexford Chesterfield Parking LLC (7-0) to redevelop 701 West Main Street into downtown life-science lab and Class A office space.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Southside Parade of Homes Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented proclamations for Imagine a Day Without Water (Oct. 6) to Water Management Assistant Director Vicki Westbrook, National Arts and Humanities Month to Durham Arts Council Executive Director Sherry DeVries and Piedmont Laureate James Maxey, and Long-Term Care Residents' Rights to local care home committees. Council also congratulated those involved in Southside revitalization on featuring a new South Street home in the regional Parade of Homes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items from the City Attorney or City Clerk, Council unanimously approved the consent agenda covering minutes, street and infrastructure acceptances, generator maintenance, the August 2015 bid report, an easement with Impress Development LLC at 112 West Main Street, an upset-bid sale at 110 Chestnut Street, property sales to Lambert Development Hunt Street LLC for Parkside at Morris Street, DOT Sign and Signal Shop design services, and granting official committee status to the Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit Project Draft EIS Endorsement Letter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff member Wesley Carroll presented a revised letter to GoTriangle endorsing the recommended preferred alternative in the Durham-Orange Light Rail Draft Environmental Impact Statement, incorporating edits requested by Council Member Eddie Davis following its September 21 deferral and public hearings held September 29 and October 1. Mayor Bell noted council members had additional proposed edits and called public speakers Mark Iwinski and Dan Jewell, while discussion touched on engineering and cost constraints against relocating the Alston Avenue transit station east of Alston Avenue; the vote occurred in an omitted segment of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Hanover Point Subdivision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Patrick Byker (Morningstar Law Group), representing Lennar Carolinas, requested rezoning to remove a 2006 commitment requiring 33-foot curb-and-gutter improvements on East Horseshoe Road because Public Works determined existing structures, drainage, and topography prevented meeting stormwater standards. NCDOT approved alternative neighborhood access improvements already under construction, Planning Commission unanimously recommended approval, and Council approved the rezoning (7-0) and consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Accessory Structures and Home Occupations (TC1500005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Michael Stock presented a text amendment to UDO Section 5.4 requested by Parker Poe on behalf of Travis Feltz to allow accessory structures beside a primary structure in RS-20 lots of at least two acres in suburban/rural tiers and to explicitly permit accessory structures for all home occupations. The amendment had been recommended 14-0 by the Planning Commission and approved 5-0 by the Board of County Commissioners. Council passed the text amendment (7-0) and its consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Wexford Chesterfield Parking LLC (701 W. Main Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD Director Kevin Dick, joined by Dan Kramer and Justin Parker of Wexford Science and Technology, presented an incentive agreement providing $6 million over 15 years to adaptively reuse the historic Chesterfield Building at 701 West Main Street into life-science laboratory and Class A office space (amid a 6% downtown office vacancy rate) with structured parking, a 40-year public-use reservation, and funded youth internships. Council members praised the private investment, job creation, and positive property tax cash flow while requesting efforts to preserve George Roesch's blue-circle stairwell painting, and approved the agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: Hanover Point Subdivision
votes.discussion_detail: Patrick Byker on behalf of Lennar Carolinas presented the rezoning to remove an unbuildable 2006 commitment for East Horseshoe Road curb-and-gutter widening, noting NCDOT-approved alternate access under construction and unanimous Planning Commission support. No public opposition appeared, and Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Hanover Point Subdivision Rezoning
votes.notes: Clerk closed the vote without speaking the numerical tally aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted to adopt the statutory consistency statement for the Hanover Point rezoning immediately after the 7-0 rezoning vote, closing the vote without dissent before moving to the final planning item.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment: Accessory Structures and Home Occupations (TC1500005)
votes.discussion_detail: Michael Stock presented UDO Section 5.4 amendments regarding RS-20 side-yard accessory structures on 2+ acre suburban/rural lots and allowing accessory structures for all home occupations, noting 14-0 Planning Commission and 5-0 BOCC approval. Council passed the amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for UDO Text Amendment (TC1500005)
votes.notes: Clerk closed the vote without speaking the numerical tally aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted on the statutory consistency statement for TC1500005 immediately after the 7-0 ordinance vote; the clerk closed the vote without dissent.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Wexford Chesterfield Parking LLC (Item 19)
votes.discussion_detail: OEWD Director Kevin Dick presented the $6 million, 15-year city incentive for Wexford's adaptive reuse of the 701 West Main Street Chesterfield Building into life-science labs, Class A office space, and structured parking, alongside county incentives, tax credits, youth internships, and a 40-year public-use parking agreement. Council praised the positive cash flow and tax base growth and approved the agreement 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, the Durham City Council reviewed health and arts oversight reports, special-event street closure procedures, and competing site layouts for the new Police Headquarters. On the Police Headquarters design, Council and architects weighed Schemes 4 and 5—pulling the building to Main Street without retaining the historic Carpenter Chevrolet building to maintain design control and avoid ~$1.8 million to $2 million in compression and enclosure costs—against a Durham Area Designers (DAD) scheme proposing to preserve Carpenter Chevrolet alongside future private development. Council also heard a second quarterly report from the Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative Health Task Force on community health worker funding, received the DPAC annual compliance report, referred Item 3 (street closures) back to administration, and unanimously approved priority items, two closed-session requests (including an update on Rodriguez v. City), and the regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: City Manager & City Attorney Priority Items (Closed Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items covering presentations on Item 3 (temporary street closing procedures), the DPAC annual report, and the Poverty Reduction Initiative Health Task Force. Council also unanimously approved the City Attorney's request for two closed-session items under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Consent & Public Hearing Review: Riverside on the Eno, Property Sales & Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council commended Public Works on street acceptance for Riverside on the Eno, one of the city's 'failed and struggling developments' (Item 2), and pulled Items 8 (upset-bid sale of 110 Chestnut Street) and 9 (property sale to Lambert Development Hunt Street LLC for Parkside at Morris Ridge). Members also previewed public hearings on O'Moss Street improvements (Item 15), zoning map changes (Items 16-17), a UDO text amendment on accessory structures/home occupations (Item 18), and a Wexford economic development incentive agreement (Item 19).

agenda_items.title: Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative: Health Task Force Quarterly Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Co-chair Latanya Gilchrist presented the Health Task Force's second quarterly report on deploying community health workers rooted in target block groups, building training and credentialing pathways with Durham Tech and the Board of Health, and seeking city, county, and private funding for two 20-hour-per-week positions.

agenda_items.title: Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Annual Oversight Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The DPAC Oversight Committee reported on five meetings reviewing General Manager Bob Klaus's operating and capital budgets, conducting on-site facility inspections, evaluating audience and programming diversity, and confirming full operator compliance with the operating agreement.

agenda_items.title: Temporary Street Closing Procedures for Special Events
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and staff discussed outreach and notification procedures for road races and parades—including advance meetings with affected churches, flyers, and road signs—and requested that staff notify past permit applicants of proposed changes; Item 3 was referred back to administration.

agenda_items.title: New Police Headquarters Design Schemes & Carpenter Chevrolet Retention Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Architects and staff compared updated site schemes with and without the historic Carpenter Chevrolet building, including the Durham Area Designers (DAD) retention scheme carrying ~$1.8M-$2M in added cost, parking deck enclosure ventilation requirements, and facade glass-to-budget tradeoffs (~50% glass). Speakers leaned toward Schemes 4 or 5 to pull the headquarters to Main Street without Carpenter Chevrolet, while staff requested preferred layout direction by October 8 to begin schematic design.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1-2, 5-10, 12; GBA Item 4; GBA Public Hearing Items 15-19; Disposed 11, 13, 14; Referred back Item 3) and unanimously approved entering closed session after the City Attorney added a brief update on Rodriguez v. City.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden presided throughout; Mayor Bill Bell was not recorded presiding or answering roll call, and individual roll-call responses for the six council seats were partially garbled in ASR.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved City Manager priority items regarding presentations and sequencing.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Items (Two Closed Session Items under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Passed without opposition by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the City Attorney's request for two attorney-client privilege closed-session items.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-2, 5-10, 12; GBA 4; Public Hearings 15-19; Referred Back 3)
votes.notes: Passed without opposition by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set the agenda placing Items 1-2, 5-10, and 12 on consent, Item 4 on GBA, Items 15-19 on GBA public hearing, disposing 11, 13, and 14, and referring Item 3 back.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Including Rodriguez v. City Update)
votes.notes: Passed without opposition by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for attorney-client items plus a brief update on Rodriguez v. City.

disagreements.issue: Police Headquarters Site Design and Retention of Carpenter Chevrolet Building
disagreements.summary: Council and design stakeholders weighed whether to adopt Schemes 4 or 5—removing the Carpenter Chevrolet building and pulling the Police Headquarters to Main Street—or pursue the Durham Area Designers (DAD) proposal retaining Carpenter Chevrolet for future private development.
disagreements.side_a_position: Proceed with Scheme 4 or Scheme 5 without retaining Carpenter Chevrolet.
side_a_arguments: Avoids roughly $1.8 million to $2 million in site-compression and additional capital costs.
Retains full city design control along Main Street rather than relying on uncertain future private development.

side_b_arguments: Preserves the historic Carpenter Chevrolet structure while creating future private development opportunities on the parcel.
Addresses concerns about police headquarters buildings appearing as glassless fortresses.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; staff requested Council's preferred site layout by October 8 to advance to schematic design.

meetings.title: Durham City Council September 21, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council proclaimed October 2015 as National Disability Employment Awareness Month, heard an update on Southside homeownership underwriting hurdles, and unanimously approved the consent agenda (7-0) including a Disparity Study follow-up, an open data platform contract, and Alston Avenue widening property conveyances. On the general business agenda, Council unanimously approved the 729 Lawson Drive consolidated annexation (7-0), an unidentified planning/SPU item and its consistency statement (7-0), and the Beaman Street closing for Southside Phase 2 (7-0). On an economic development incentive agreement for the Morris Street Phase 1 office/lab and structured parking project (C1, C2, P1), Council passed the deal in a 6-1 split vote—with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt voting Aye and Diane Catotti voting Nay over the size of the incentive percentage—before hearing closing remarks on policing from Steve Schewel and Durham Police Officers Association President Mike Evans.

agenda_items.title: National Disability Employment Awareness Month, Southside Update, and CAC Oath
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented the October 2015 National Disability Employment Awareness Month proclamation to Jason Jones, Mars Clemens, and Deborah Giles. A brief staff snippet noted strong family interest in Phase 1 Southside homeownership alongside underwriting barriers at initial mortgage application, and a Citizens Advisory Committee appointee took the oath of office.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously adopted the consent agenda covering minutes, the June 2015 inventory audit, Ridgeway Road street renamings (SN1500002/SN1500003), a North Parking Garage lease amendment with American Campus LLC, stream relocation maintenance contracts, Water Management roof replacements, the Disparity Study follow-up report, insurance broker and harm-reduction service contracts, NCDOT property conveyances for the Alston Avenue widening project, and an open data platform contract.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: 729 Lawson Drive (BDG1500003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Pat Young presented a consolidated annexation, initial zoning, and utility extension agreement for 729 Lawson Road in the Jordan Lake B watershed, noting unanimous April 14 Planning Commission support, adequate utility capacity, and positive fiscal impact. The applicant explained he sought annexation to connect to an existing city water line (with county sewer already available), and staff confirmed adjacent properties were expected to annex by year-end to establish contiguity. Council approved the annexation (7-0) and its consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Harris Beverage, 1035 Junction Road (BDG1500009)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented a consolidated annexation for 21.5 acres at 1035 Junction Road with adequate utility capacity and positive fiscal impact, explaining in response to Council Member Steve Schewel that a standing 10-year Planning Commission policy automatically endorses current zoning translations. Attorney Patrick Byker spoke for Harris Beverage; the vote occurred in an omitted middle segment of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Planning/Zoning Item Involving Special Use / SPU Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a digest gap, Council concluded discussion referencing continuing staff concerns regarding a special use / SPU matter and voted 7-0 to approve the item and 7-0 to adopt its consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing: Beaman Street (SC1500004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented a request by Mike Tarrant of Stewart Engineering to close all 422 linear feet of Beaman Street, bordered by a place of worship and vacant land for Southside Phase 2 residential redevelopment, dividing the right-of-way evenly among adjoining owners with no negative agency impacts. Tarrant appeared for questions and asked for support for Southside Phase 2, and Council approved the street closing 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: Morris Street Phase 1 Development (C1, C2, P1)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic development staff presented a multi-phase downtown development along Morris Street terminating at Duke Street near the Carmichael Building, focusing Phase 1 on office/lab buildings C1 and C2, structured parking P1, and the Morris Green open space amid a 6% downtown Class A office vacancy rate, with a roughly seven-year overall buildout. During debate following Vince Taylor's public remarks, a supporting council member agreed with Diane Catotti that the city's incentive percentage was high and urged pushing future deals toward 50-50 parity, while still voting yes; Council passed the agreement 6-1 with Catotti voting no.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-1 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Schewel, Davis, Moffitt; Nay: Catotti)

agenda_items.title: Police Staffing Remarks and Public Comment Supporting Chief Jose Lopez
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel addressed active and former police officers in the gallery to thank them and invite them to discuss their concerns over pizza after the meeting, prompting Mayor Bell to interject that he was presiding over the meeting. Durham Police Officers Association President Mike Evans then addressed Council on behalf of roughly 500 members in support of Police Chief Jose Lopez, disputing claims of low morale and rising crime and urging greater unity between city leadership and the department.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation: 729 Lawson Drive (BDG1500003)

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members participating, the Durham City Council unanimously approved compensation and contract actions for its appointed officials, reviewed the Durham-Orange Light Rail Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS), and examined year-end finances. Following closed-session performance evaluations, Council voted 7-0 to grant the City Manager and City Clerk a 3.5% salary increase effective July 1, voted 7-0 to extend the City Manager's contract by five years, and voted 7-0 on the City Attorney's contract. Council heard detailed questions on the light rail Rail Operations and Maintenance Facility (Farrington Road preferred site vs. Cornwallis) ahead of September 24 and October 1 public hearings, reviewed the FY 2014-15 Q4 financial report showing a $39 million unassigned General Fund balance ($19 million above the 12% policy floor), and saw Mayor Bell and another council member differ over conducting a joint city-county resident survey before setting the regular meeting agenda (7-0).

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney & City Clerk Performance Raises and Contract Extensions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following closed-session performance evaluations of Council's three direct appointees, Council unanimously approved a 3.5% salary increase effective July 1 for the City Manager and City Clerk, unanimously approved extending the City Manager's contract for another five years under existing terms, and unanimously approved the City Attorney's contract action.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Light Rail, Citizens Matter & Durham Station Land)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items scheduling the Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit presentation (Item 5) for 2:00 p.m. and adding supplemental Item 28 (Alois Johnson Citizens Matter) and Item 29 (disposition and development alternatives for excess land adjacent to Durham Station).

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Youth Energy Drinks, Beer/Wine Permits & Noise Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen speaker Wanda Boney urged Council to bar convenience store sales of 24-ounce, 250mg-caffeine energy drinks to minors under 18 and asked about alcohol permit renewals and the Loud and Unruly Noise Ordinance. Finance Director David Boyd explained the 2012 administrative review process for beer and wine permits involving PACs and police, while the City Attorney noted formal Council direction was needed to review noise ordinance amendments.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Transit DEIS & Rail Operations Facility (Farrington Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transit staff answered Council questions on the Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS), clarifying the selection of the Farrington Road site as the preferred Rail Operations and Maintenance Facility (ROMF) over four other sites including Cornwallis, potential rezoning requirements, neighborhood access impacts, and public hearings set for September 24 in Chapel Hill and October 1 in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Pulls: McAdams Company Workforce Statistics & Broker Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Item 6 regarding workforce statistics on the McAdams Company contract and requested adding maps to future agenda items. A member also asked to place a broker contract on the General Business Agenda to allow time to contact prospective vendors.

agenda_items.title: FY 2014-15 Q4 Financial Report & Joint City-County Resident Survey Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff presented FY 2014-15 Q4 financial results showing an unassigned General Fund balance of $39 million (24%), representing a $19 million surplus above the 12% ($20 million) policy minimum. Mayor Bill Bell then questioned combining city and county questions in a joint resident survey, arguing it confuses respondents about county versus city services, while another member cited staff's argument that a joint survey strengthens the community assessment.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the regular meeting agenda by voice vote: Consent Items 1-4 and 6-16; GBA Public Hearing Items 20-26; Referring back Items 5 and 29; and Disposing of Items 17-19, 27, and 28.

votes.item_title: 3.5% Salary Increase Effective July 1 for City Manager and City Clerk
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; Eugene Brown had arrived by 00:00:23.
votes.discussion_detail: Granted a 3.5% performance-based salary increase effective July 1 to the City Manager and City Clerk following closed-session evaluations.

votes.item_title: Five-Year Contract Extension for the City Manager
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Extended the City Manager's employment contract for an additional five years under the same conditions, subject to formal documents from the City Attorney.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items (Item 5 Time Certain; Supplemental Items 28 & 29)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set Item 5 (Light Rail) for 2:00 p.m. and added supplemental Items 28 and 29.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Contract Action
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the contract motion relative to the City Attorney following evaluation.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-4, 6-16; GBA Public Hearings 20-26; Referred Back 5 & 29)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set the regular meeting agenda placing Items 1-4 and 6-16 on consent, Items 20-26 on GBA public hearing, referring Items 5 and 29 back, and disposing of Items 17-19, 27, and 28.

disagreements.issue: Conducting a Joint City-County Resident Survey
disagreements.summary: Mayor Bill Bell questioned the value of combining city and county service questions into a single joint resident survey, while another Council member defended staff's rationale that a joint survey strengthened the community assessment.
disagreements.side_a_position: Limit the city resident survey to city residents and city services rather than combining with county questions.
side_a_arguments: Asking residents outside city limits or across jurisdictions about both county and city operations (such as sheriff protection vs. city services) creates confusion.
The survey is already long and gains little value from mixing distinct city and county responsibilities.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support staff's joint city-county community survey approach.
side_b_arguments: Staff (Josh Edwards) made a strong case that surveying the broader community strengthens the survey and works well across both governments.
disagreements.resolution: Discussion concluded without altering the survey or taking a separate vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council September 8, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present, the Durham City Council inducted the 2015–2016 Durham Youth Commission, issued proclamations for Constitution Week, Life Insurance Awareness Month, and National Recovery Month, and heard Mayor Bill Bell's reminder that public comments on the Durham-Orange Light Rail Draft EIS must go directly to GoTriangle by October 13. Following an omitted middle portion of the transcript digest, Council debated architectural alternatives for the new police headquarters—specifically weighing whether spending $4 million to preserve the historic Carpenter Chevrolet building was justified—and reached consensus to defer the design for additional apples-to-apples review at an upcoming work session. On Item 15, the US 70 Self Storage Center rezoning (Z1400020) that the Planning Commission had recommended denying 1-10, Council passed the rezoning in a 5-2 split vote (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, and Don Moffitt; Nays: Diane Catotti and Eddie Davis) after the applicant proffered a permanent access easement covenant, before unanimously adopting the consistency statement (7-0) and concluding with a Council Member Eddie Davis-led reflection on community violence.

agenda_items.title: Durham Youth Commission Induction, Proclamations, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council inducted the 2015–2016 Durham Youth Commission after hearing a report on 2014–2015 committee projects (including Black Wall Street web episodes, Week of No Barriers, and safe-dating workshops), and presented proclamations for Constitution Week, Life Insurance Awareness Month, and National Recovery Month. Council Member Eddie Davis announced December 5–6 Geer Cemetery events honoring the 150th anniversary of the 13th Amendment and noted the death of former Council Member George Nixon, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden praised DYC and asked staff to investigate an employee benefit roadblock, and Mayor Bill Bell announced public hearings and the October 13 comment deadline for the Durham-Orange Light Rail Draft EIS.

agenda_items.title: New Police Headquarters Site Alternatives and Carpenter Chevrolet Building Preservation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after an omitted digest segment, Council debated architectural schemes for the new police station site and whether to spend roughly $4 million preserving the Carpenter Chevrolet building. One member opposed investing $4 million given no private developer had offered to buy the building, while another speaker emphasized balancing historical context against competing capital needs and ensuring active, walkable street-front uses along Main Street. Council reached consensus for staff to perform an apples-to-apples comparison and return to the September 24 or early October work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Consensus referral to work session

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: US 70 Self Storage Center (Z1400020)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Pat Young presented a rezoning of 7.55 acres on US 70 Highway to Light Industrial with a Development Plan (IL(D)) for a self-storage center, including US 70 right-of-way dedication, land reservation for a future Page Road extension, a >4-foot fence, and a newly proffered commitment requiring a recorded permanent access easement prior to building permit or certificate of occupancy; the Planning Commission had recommended denial 1-10 on April 14 while staff recommended approval. Council Member Don Moffitt noted that the recorded easement resolved his primary access concern despite hesitation over splitting an existing development plan, and Council approved the rezoning 5-2 with Diane Catotti and Eddie Davis voting no, followed by a 7-0 consistency statement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 5-2 (Ayes: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Schewel, Moffitt; Nays: Catotti, Davis); Consistency Statement 7-0

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closing Discussion on Community Violence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk reported ballot appointment results: Barry Burch (7 votes) and Matthew McCarrihan (5 votes) to the Citizens Advisory Committee, and Andrew Hudson (4 votes) to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission. Council Member Eddie Davis then initiated a closing discussion on local violence, emphasizing that addressing gun violence requires broader societal, family, and community engagement beyond policing alone.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Clerk reported ballot appointments (Burch: 7, McCarrihan: 5, Hudson: 4)

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change: US 70 Self Storage Center (Z1400020)
votes.notes: Planning Commission recommended denial 1-10 on April 14, 2015; staff recommended approval with proffered access easement commitment.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Z1400020 to rezone 7.55 acres on US 70 to IL(D) for a self-storage center despite a 1-10 denial recommendation from the Planning Commission. After the applicant added a commitment to record a permanent access easement prior to building permit or certificate of occupancy, Council Member Don Moffitt seconded the approval motion and voiced reluctant support, and Council passed the rezoning 5-2 with Diane Catotti and Eddie Davis voting no.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for US 70 Self Storage Center (Z1400020)
votes.discussion_detail: Following the 5-2 approval of the US 70 Self Storage Center rezoning, Council voted unanimously 7-0 to adopt the statutory consistency statement.

disagreements.issue: US 70 Self Storage Center Rezoning (Z1400020)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 5-2 to approve rezoning 7.55 acres on US 70 Highway to IL(D) for a self-storage facility despite a 1-10 Planning Commission denial recommendation. Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, and Don Moffitt voted in favor after the applicant proffered a permanent access easement covenant, while Diane Catotti and Eddie Davis voted no.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the US 70 Self Storage Center rezoning with the revised access easement commitment
side_a_arguments: Staff determined the proposal complied with UDO and policy provisions, including US 70 right-of-way dedication and Page Road reservation.
The applicant's newly proffered covenant requiring a recorded permanent access easement prior to building permit or certificate of occupancy addressed key access concerns (cited by Don Moffitt).
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose rezoning 7.55 acres to IL(D) for a self-storage facility
side_b_arguments: Voted no on the rezoning following a 1-10 Planning Commission denial recommendation (Don Moffitt also noted discomfort with severing half of an existing site development plan before ultimately voting yes).
disagreements.resolution: Passed 5-2

disagreements.issue: Carpenter Chevrolet Building Preservation at New Police Headquarters Site
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to spend an estimated $4 million to preserve the historic Carpenter Chevrolet building as part of the new police headquarters design along Fayetteville/Main Street, weighing historic preservation against capital budget constraints and street-level activation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Oppose spending $4 million to preserve the Carpenter Chevrolet building
side_a_arguments: Spending $4 million on the structure was not justified relative to the building's assessed value and other capital needs.
No private developer had ever offered to purchase the building alone prior to city acquisition.
disagreements.side_b_position: Explore cost-effective preservation or active pedestrian-oriented alternatives
side_b_arguments: Historical context helps define Durham's identity rather than 'anywhere USA,' and at least one developer had expressed prior interest in the site.
Any preserved or redeveloped frontage should provide active uses residents want to walk to, rather than blank landscaping, if achievable without a $4 million cost.
disagreements.resolution: Deferred by consensus for apples-to-apples staff comparison at the September 24 or first October work session
