meetings.title: Durham City Council May 4, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met with all seven members present and approved the consent agenda, referred a joint City-County Workforce Development Board interlocal agreement back to staff, and passed all seven land-use and planning items unanimously, including Guglhupf Bakery's parking expansion, Laxmi's Plaza neighborhood grocery rezoning, the Herndon Road consolidated annexation, Willow Street closing and renaming, and a multi-year Wireless Communications Facilities (cell tower) text amendment. Council also received the Durham Police Department's 2015 First Quarter Crime Report showing a 22% rise in Part 1 violent crime and discussed community conversations on policing following peaceful local demonstrations.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Student Poster Contest Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented proclamations for Children's Mental Health Awareness Month, the Week of No Barriers (with the Durham Youth Commission), National Prevention Week (with Together for a Resilient Youth), Older Americans Month, National Police Week, and National Drinking Water Week. Department of Water Management staff also recognized local elementary and middle school winners of the NC AWWA water conservation poster contest from Holt Elementary, Durham Academy, and Voyager Academy.

agenda_items.title: Peaceful Demonstrations and Community Policing Dialogue
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eddie Davis commended peaceful demonstrators who marched from Durham Police headquarters to the Durham Detention Center regarding national policing concerns and thanked DPD for protecting their First Amendment rights. Davis, Mayor Bell, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden agreed to organize and lead facilitated community conversations bringing together city, county, school board, and community stakeholders.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Workforce Development Board Referral & Q1 Crime Report)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested referring Item 11, the interlocal agreement establishing the Durham Workforce Development Board under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, back to administration after the Board of County Commissioners suggested modifications earlier that morning. He also added supplemental Item 24, the 2015 First Quarter Summary Crime Report presentation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-8, 10, 12-14, 16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council adopted the unpulled consent agenda covering minutes, Planning Commission appointments, street acceptances, an Emergency Solutions Grant contract with the Durham Crisis Response Center, up to $3.8 million in conditional subordinate financing for Lofts at Southside Phase II and Southside infrastructure, reclaimed water master planning, sanitary sewer root control, the March 2015 bid report, a Liberty Arts sculpture donation, budget amendments, a parks grant, police special revenue funds, and the Recreation Advisory Commission report.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Guglhupf (A14-00007)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a Future Land Use Map amendment for 0.4 acres at 2706 Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard from Medium Density Residential to Commercial to enable additional parking for Guglhupf Bakery. Applicant Howard Partin and Tuscaloosa-Lakewood Neighborhood Association President David Stevenson testified in favor based on a negotiated development plan, restrictive covenant, and private side agreement, while resident Susan Sewell opposed crossing the Francis Street residential boundary.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Guglhupf Parking Expansion (Z14-00007)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: This companion rezoning changed 2706 Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard from RS-8 to Commercial General with a Development Plan prohibiting buildings, preserving mature trees, and installing a 22.5-foot vegetated buffer and decorative fence over four feet tall along Francis Street. Council Member Don Moffitt confirmed that private side agreements are enforced privately rather than by Planning staff, and Council Member Steve Schewel questioned the omission of BPAC-recommended bicycle racks on the parent restaurant parcel.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Laxmi's Plaza (Z14-00005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a public hearing to rezone 0.82 acres at 4823 Hopson Road from Office and Institutional to Commercial Neighborhood with a Development Plan allowing up to 7,078 square feet of commercial uses while prohibiting drive-through restaurants, banks, and fuel sales. Engineer Cliff Craddle and prospective tenant Vijay explained the plan to open a neighborhood produce and grocery store inside the existing vacant building.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Herndon Partners LLC (Herndon Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a utility extension agreement, voluntary contiguous annexation, and initial Rural Residential (RR) zoning for approximately 26 acres on Herndon Road in southwest Durham, supporting up to 48 residential units. Council Members Steve Schewel, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt asked about utility-driven density differences in RR zoning, neighborhood outreach, and why identical initial zonings bypass Planning Commission review.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Wireless Communications Facilities (TC12-00013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented multi-year revisions to UDO wireless communication facility standards expanding 600-foot special use permit notice, requiring balloon tests, adding natural gas line setbacks, regulating unipoles, and requiring minor special use permits via the Board of Adjustment for taller or non-concealed towers near residences. Six residents and neighborhood advocates urged further protections—including an 85-foot height cap in suburban RR zones recommended 8-4 by the Planning Commission, public hearings for towers under 60 feet due to FCC height-expansion rules, and stricter structural safety text—but Council voted to adopt the ordinance now and review remaining items in future technical amendments.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing: Willow Street (SC14-00018)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered closing a 7,251-square-foot unimproved portion of Willow Street right-of-way requested by Edens Land Corp for B. Wallace Design & Construction to serve seven residential lots. Council Member Don Moffitt expressed reluctance about creating a cul-de-sac instead of connecting to Huron Street, while Planning staff and applicant Jared Edens explained that the right-of-way had long been unimproved and connecting to Huron or south Willow would require crossing a buffered stream.

agenda_items.title: Street Renaming: Willow Street to Anchor Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a request to rename the northern segment of Willow Street to Anchor Way following the street closure to avoid emergency response conflicts. Neighbor Elizabeth Shearer and Susan Sewell raised concerns about severe slope drainage, creek protection, and public notice for the seven by-right residential lots; staff and applicant Jared Edens assured Council that stormwater detention ponds, vegetative filter strips, and stream buffer rules would be enforced during site plan review.

agenda_items.title: Durham Police Department 2015 First Quarter Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez reported that Part 1 violent crime rose 22% in Q1 2015 (including 10 homicides compared to 6 in Q1 2014) and property crime rose 2%, while highlighting a 90-day enforcement initiative in the Cornwallis Road and Weaver Street areas that yielded over two dozen arrests and 39 seized firearms. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden pressed Chief Lopez to compile public data on drive-by shootings and pursue ShotSpotter acoustic detection technology.

votes.item_title: Approve City Manager's Priority Items (Refer Item 11 Workforce Development Board Interlocal to Administration; Add Item 24 Q1 Crime Report)
votes.notes: Referred Item 11 back to administration after BOCC requested modifications; added supplemental Item 24.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield informed Council that the Board of County Commissioners had reviewed the Workforce Development Board interlocal agreement earlier that morning and proposed several revisions. He recommended referring Item 11 back to administration for review and follow-up at Thursday's work session, and adding the 2015 First Quarter Summary Crime Report as supplemental Item 24. No council members objected, and the priority items motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Guglhupf (A14-00007)
votes.notes: Amended Future Land Use Map for 0.4 acres at 2706 Durham-Chapel Hill Blvd from Medium Density Residential to Commercial.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the FLUM change for 2706 Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard, noting unanimous 12-0 Planning Commission support. Applicant Howard Partin and Tuscaloosa-Lakewood Neighborhood Association President David Stevenson testified that months of arduous negotiations produced a restrictive covenant, private side agreement, and development plan barring buildings and buffering Francis Street to relieve neighborhood overflow parking. Resident Susan Sewell opposed crossing Francis Street into a residential area, urging Council to protect commercial-residential boundaries, while Council Member Diane Catotti moved approval citing the stringent negotiated protections. Council approved the amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Zoning Map Change: Guglhupf Parking Expansion (Z14-00007)
votes.notes: Rezones 0.4 acres at 2706 Durham-Chapel Hill Blvd from RS-8 to CG(D) with parking-only, tree-preservation, buffer, and >4-ft fence commitments.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented the companion rezoning from RS-8 to CG(D), which prohibited buildings, required a 22.5-foot vegetated buffer and decorative fence taller than four feet along Francis Street, and preserved mature trees. Council Member Don Moffitt clarified for the record that Planning staff only enforces commitments in the development plan, while private side agreements must be enforced by the parties in court. Council Member Steve Schewel questioned why BPAC-recommended bicycle parking on the existing Guglhupf site was not proffered as a text commitment; applicant Howard Partin stated UDO site plan review would require bike parking on the new lot, and Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Guglhupf Rezoning (Z14-00007)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement following approval of Z14-00007.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following approval of the Guglhupf parking expansion zoning map change, Council entertained the required North Carolina statutory consistency statement confirming the rezoning's alignment with the newly amended Comprehensive Plan. No additional debate occurred, and the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Zoning Map Change: Laxmi's Plaza (Z14-00005)
votes.notes: Rezones 0.82 acres at 4823 Hopson Rd from OI to CN(D) for up to 7,078 sq ft commercial, prohibiting drive-thrus, banks, and fuel sales.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Z14-00005 to rezone 0.82 acres at 4823 Hopson Road from Office and Institutional to Commercial Neighborhood with a Development Plan restricting intensity and banning drive-through restaurants, banks, and fuel sales, following a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Project engineer Cliff Craddle explained that no exterior building expansions were proposed, and prospective tenant Vijay stated the space would serve nearby new residential subdivisions as a neighborhood grocery store with produce and food items. No opponents spoke, and Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Laxmi's Plaza Rezoning (Z14-00005)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement for Z14-00005.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the Laxmi's Plaza rezoning vote, Council took up the statutory statement of consistency with the Comprehensive Plan and adopted policies. With no further comments from Council members, the motion was moved, seconded, and approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Consolidated Annexation, Utility Extension Agreement, and Initial RR Zoning: Herndon Partners LLC
votes.notes: 26 acres on Herndon Rd in SW Durham; initial Rural Residential (RR) zoning supporting up to 48 units with city water/sewer.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented the utility extension agreement, voluntary contiguous annexation petition, and initial Rural Residential zoning for 26 acres on Herndon Road, noting adequate utility capacity and positive fiscal impact shortly after annexation. Council Member Steve Schewel sought clarification on how RR zoning permits higher density once city water and sewer are extended, Council Member Eddie Davis confirmed with applicant Jared Edens that no opposition had been reported from nearby Lakehurst residents, and Council Member Don Moffitt confirmed identical initial zonings bypass Planning Commission review. Council approved the consolidated annexation actions 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Herndon Partners Initial Zoning
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement for initial RR zoning on Herndon Rd.
votes.discussion_detail: After approving the Herndon Road consolidated annexation and initial Rural Residential zoning, Council voted on the required consistency statement. No additional discussion took place, and the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt UDO Text Amendment: Wireless Communications Facilities (TC12-00013)
votes.notes: Approved as drafted by staff; Council directed staff to examine remaining neighborhood safety questions in subsequent technical revisions.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Michael Stock presented the comprehensive overhaul of UDO Section 5.3.3.N initiated in November 2012, expanding special use permit notifications to 600 feet, requiring balloon tests, adding natural gas line setbacks, regulating unipoles, and requiring Board of Adjustment quasi-judicial hearings for non-concealed towers and concealed towers over 60 feet near residential districts. Six neighborhood advocates urged Council to adopt the Planning Commission's 8-4 recommended 85-foot cap in suburban RR zoning, require public hearings for towers under 60 feet because FCC rules allow later height expansion, and add explicit structural/storm safety standards. Council Members Diane Catotti, Don Moffitt, Steve Schewel, Eddie Davis, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Mayor Bell praised residents' multi-year advocacy but concluded that 5-acre lot minimums, BOA review, and Telecommunications Act compliance warranted adopting the draft now while directing staff to study the remaining safety issues later. The amendment passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Wireless Communications Facilities Text Amendment (TC12-00013)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement for TC12-00013.
votes.discussion_detail: Following passage of the Wireless Communications Facilities UDO text amendment, Council voted on the companion statement of consistency. With debate concluded, the consistency statement was moved, seconded, and approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Street Closing: Willow Street (SC14-00018)
votes.notes: Closes 7,251 sq ft unimproved portion of Willow St right-of-way to enable a 7-lot residential cul-de-sac.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented SC14-00018 to close an unimproved 7,251-square-foot segment of Willow Street right-of-way for B. Wallace Design & Construction, noting 20 reviewing agencies and utility providers identified no negative impacts. Council Member Don Moffitt questioned why Council should approve a cul-de-sac that prevents street connectivity to Huron Street when the Comprehensive Plan and UDO favor connectivity. Planning staff and applicant Jared Edens explained that the surrounding Tuscaloosa-Lakewood grid already has good connectivity and that extending Willow Street south or connecting to Huron Street would require crossing a buffered stream, after which Council approved the closing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Street Renaming: Northern Portion of Willow Street to Anchor Way
votes.notes: Renames the northern disconnected segment of Willow St to Anchor Way for EMS/emergency response clarity.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young explained that closing the middle portion of Willow Street left two disconnected segments, necessitating renaming the northern portion to Anchor Way as cleared by Durham County EMS. Although not legally a public hearing, Mayor Bell allowed adjacent resident Elizabeth Shearer and neighbor Susan Sewell to speak; they expressed concern about severe hillside drainage, creek impacts from seven new houses, and not receiving mailed notice of the renaming. Planning staff and Jared Edens noted that the seven lots were existing lots of record and that a wet detention pond, vegetative filter strip, and riparian buffers would meet city stormwater ordinances, after which Council approved the renaming 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Guglhupf Bakery Commercial Parking Expansion into Francis Street Residential Block (A14-00007 / Z14-00007)
disagreements.summary: While the Tuscaloosa-Lakewood Neighborhood Association board and Guglhupf reached a negotiated compromise allowing commercial parking across Francis Street with covenants and buffers, a nearby resident opposed breaching the residential boundary and Council Member Steve Schewel questioned the lack of binding bike-rack text commitments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the FLUM amendment and CG(D) rezoning based on negotiated buffers, building prohibition, tree preservation, and private side agreements.
side_a_arguments: Alleviates heavy overflow staff and customer parking and pedestrian safety hazards on neighborhood streets and Durham-Chapel Hill Blvd.
Includes a binding 22.5-foot vegetated buffer, decorative fencing, no-building commitment, private restrictive covenant, and TLNA board endorsement.
disagreements.side_b_position: Preserve strict backyard-to-backyard residential boundaries and require BPAC-recommended bicycle parking commitments on the parent site.
side_b_arguments: Opposing resident Susan Sewell argued commercial uses should not leap across Francis Street into residential blocks and neighborhoods should not have to negotiate piece-by-piece for buffer protections.
Council Member Steve Schewel noted the applicant declined to proffer BPAC's requested bike racks on the existing restaurant parcel in the binding development plan.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 7-0 after applicant noted UDO site plan review will require bike racks on the new parking lot and Council Member Catotti cited stringent negotiated protections.

disagreements.issue: Wireless Communications Facilities Text Amendment Scope and Suburban Height Cap (TC12-00013)
disagreements.summary: Council unanimously adopted the 2012-2015 cell tower ordinance overhaul as drafted by staff, declining to delay passage to incorporate an 85-foot height cap in suburban Rural Residential areas (recommended 8-4 by the Planning Commission) or additional resident-proposed safety and FCC upsizing safeguards.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the drafted WCF text amendment immediately and refer remaining safety and technical questions for future annual technical review.
side_a_arguments: After more than two years of work by staff, JCCPC, and citizen groups, the ordinance delivers major gains including 600-foot notice, balloon tests, gas-line setbacks, and Board of Adjustment hearings.

Five-acre minimum lot sizes and quasi-judicial BOA hearings already protect suburban RR neighborhoods, whereas an 85-foot cap could risk federal Telecommunications Act litigation or poor rural coverage.
Holding the ordinance for new drafting would cause multi-cycle delays and require re-coordination with the Board of County Commissioners.
disagreements.side_b_position: Cap tower height at 85 feet in suburban RR zones, require public hearings for all concealed towers under 60 feet, and write explicit storm-safety standards into the ordinance before adoption.
side_b_arguments: Neighborhood speakers (Fred Bauer, Al Fahrenbacher, Ms. Rudolph) warned FCC rules allow <60-foot concealed towers approved administratively to later expand significantly without neighborhood input.
Speakers cited Hurricane Sandy antenna failures and generator fuel hazards as requiring explicit structural and safety language rather than reliance on implied building codes.
Four Planning Commissioners and the InterNeighborhood Council backed an 85-foot height limit in suburban RR areas.
disagreements.resolution: Adopted 7-0 as drafted, with Council Members Schewel and Bell requesting staff follow up on remaining safety issues through JCCPC and future technical amendments.

disagreements.issue: Willow Street Closing and Cul-de-Sac Street Connectivity (SC14-00018)
disagreements.summary: Council Member Don Moffitt questioned closing an unimproved segment of Willow Street to create a cul-de-sac rather than preserving a street connection to Huron Street, before joining a unanimous vote after staff and the applicant cited stream-crossing barriers.
disagreements.side_a_position: Close the 7,251-square-foot right-of-way to enable access to seven interior residential lots via a cul-de-sac.
side_a_arguments: The right-of-way has remained platted and unimproved for decades while surrounding Tuscaloosa-Lakewood streets already provide strong grid connectivity.
Extending Willow Street south or connecting out to Huron Street would require crossing a protected buffered stream.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid creating dead-end cul-de-sacs when Comprehensive Plan and UDO policies favor street connectivity.
side_b_arguments: Approving a single cul-de-sac because surrounding streets are connected undermines connectivity principles for emergency services and traffic circulation.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 7-0 after Planning staff and Jared Edens clarified both potential through-connections would require stream crossings.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present and Council Member Eugene Brown excused absent, the Durham City Council reviewed affordable housing financing, public works contracts, parks needs, and workforce development alignment. Council unanimously approved (6-0) the City Manager's priority items, referring back Item 9 (annual truck purchase) and deferring discussion of Duke Energy tree-cutting and a 1982 permit ordinance until legal and utility details are gathered. Members heard updates on the Liberty Arts sculpture donation (Item 10), highway interchange improvements, and the Recreation Advisory Commission's annual report, during which a council member floated a future bond referendum to address pool and park maintenance needs. Council also scrutinized financial projections and tax-credit equity pricing for the $3.8 million Phase 2 Lofts at Southside loan (Item 5), reviewed reclaimed water and sewer root-control contracts (Items 6-7), and examined summer youth job funding under the WIOA Workforce Development Board agreement before unanimously setting the regular agenda (6-0).

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items & Duke Energy Tree-Cutting Ordinance Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested referring back Item 9 (annual truck purchase) and pulling Item 10 (Liberty Arts sculpture donation) for a brief presentation, while advising Council that staff and the City Attorney were meeting with Duke Energy regarding a 1982 tree-cutting permit ordinance ahead of a future work session. Council approved the priority items 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Liberty Arts Sculpture Donation, Road Corridor Updates & Recreation Advisory Commission Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council commended Liberty Arts and city staff on the sculpture donation (Item 10) and heard an update on highway/interchange and local street improvements along Hoover, Carr, Lynn, Pleasant, and Easton. The Recreation Advisory Commission presented its annual report praising American Tobacco Trail and park maintenance investments while noting pool/aquatics challenges, prompting a suggestion to consider a future bond referendum for pools and parks.

agenda_items.title: Lofts at Southside Phase 2 Subordinate Financing ($3.8 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council questioned McCormick Baron Salazar consultant Carl Schlocker on per-unit sources and uses math, 9 percent versus 7.5 percent low-income housing tax credit pricing, and sharing potential financing savings. Schlocker reported that Building 2 was being accepted and pre-leased with tenant move-ins beginning around May 1.

agenda_items.title: Reclaimed Water, Sewer Root Control, Workforce Board & Police Grants

meetings.title: Durham City Council April 20, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: With six members present and Council Member Eugene Brown excused absent, the Durham City Council recognized retiring General Services Director Joel Reitzer, held a public hearing on the 2015-2020 HUD Consolidated Plan and Analysis of Impediments, and approved several development cases unanimously, including Southside East Phases 2 and 3, Hendrick Automotive Group street closings, Sutton Station, and Hamilton Centre II. On the final items, a 320-unit multifamily plan amendment and rezoning along NC Highway 54 (Highway 54 Residential) drew sharp concerns over traffic congestion, tree clearing, and the absence of affordable housing units, passing by split 4-2 voice votes.

agenda_items.title: Crime Victims' Rights Week Proclamation & General Services Director Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell proclaimed April 19-25, 2015 as Crime Victims' Rights Week, received by DPD Lieutenant Brown who highlighted events at NCCU and Shepherd House for the 'Start by Believing' campaign. City Manager Tom Bonfield then honored retiring General Services Director Joel Reitzer for nearly six years of service overseeing projects including the Durham Convention Center, Carolina Theatre, and Durham Bulls Athletic Park renovations.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-4, 6-13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council adopted the consent agenda covering minutes, board appointments to the Housing Appeals Board, Environmental Affairs Board, and Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission, renewal of the City-County planning interlocal agreement, Jordan Lake protected area interpretation, BPAC reauthorization, the Alston Avenue bridge replacement agreement, Hillandale Golf Course management amendment, Twin Lakes Park improvements, a Cleveland Street renovation change order, and a water-only utility extension on Farrington Mill Road.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved 6-0 (unanimous voice vote; Eugene Brown excused absent)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Southside East Phases 2 & 3 (Z14-00034)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a rezoning of 10.7 acres at Plum Street from PDR 5.12 to Residential Urban Multifamily (RU-M(D)) for 250 units with a parking reduction from 2.0 to 1.2 spaces per unit and a bus shelter commitment. Council Member Diane Catotti confirmed FY16 CIP funding for ADA ramps and pedestrian signals at Roxboro, Lakewood, and Mangum, and Council Member Don Moffitt secured a binding commitment from the applicant to install a bicycle maintenance and repair station on site.

agenda_items.title: Street Closings: Hendrick Automotive Group (SC14-00012 through SC14-00016)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a request by Hendrick Automotive Group to close approximately 5,800 linear feet of five public streets in the former Kenton Heights subdivision (including Caris Place, Kenton Drive, and Santa Clara Drive) to recombine the right-of-way into its approved auto park site. No members of the public spoke during the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Draft 2015-2020 Consolidated Plan, FY15-16 Annual Action Plan & Analysis of Impediments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development staff and consultant Urban Design Ventures presented Durham's five-year HUD Consolidated Plan and Analysis of Impediments covering CDBG ($1.81 million), HOME ($776,323 plus program income), ESG ($160,046), and HOPWA ($282,226) funds, with testimony from Rebuilding Durham and Habitat for Humanity. Council Member Steve Schewel questioned racial disparities in HMDA mortgage lending, Durham Rescue Mission's non-participation in HMIS data reporting, Medicaid non-expansion impacts on homelessness, and rising housing cost burdens, while Diane Catotti and Cora Cole-McFadden pressed staff on Habitat's funding capacity and helping smaller nonprofits access HUD and Penny for Housing grants.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved 6-0 (accepted public comments and approved draft plan)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Sutton Station (Z14-00025)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a rezoning of 15.94 acres at 5800 Fayetteville Road from Office and Institutional to Mixed Use with a Development Plan to permit additional retail uses within the existing square footage, capped by trip limits and paired with a bus shelter. Applicant representative Ron Horvath confirmed compliance with BPAC bike rack recommendations and American Tobacco Trail signage.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Hamilton Centre II (A14-00006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a Future Land Use Map amendment for 5.02 acres at 7010 NC 751 Highway (southwest quadrant of NC 54 and NC 751) from Office to Commercial, noting 12-0 Planning Commission support. No public opposition was voiced.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Hamilton Centre II (Z14-00021)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: This companion rezoning changed 7010 NC 751 Highway from Office and Institutional to Commercial General with a Development Plan allowing up to 40,000 square feet of retail and restaurant uses (capped around 50% retail) along with a bus shelter pad. Applicant representative Ron Horvath noted the total square footage slightly exceeded Neighborhood Commercial limits, requiring CG zoning.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Highway 54 Residential (A14-00005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Hopper Communities requested changing 21.72 acres at 1413-1501 NC Highway 54 (at Revere Road) from Office to Medium-High Density Residential. Mayor Bill Bell questioned cumulative traffic saturation on un-widened NC 54 and tree loss—prompting Planning staff to acknowledge corridor traffic is nearing the threshold for recommending denial—while Council Member Steve Schewel criticized the absence of affordable housing among 320 market-rate units despite a proffered $21,500 contribution to Durham Public Schools.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved 4-2 (voice vote with two audible nays)

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Highway 54 Residential (Z14-00018)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Companion rezoning of 21.72 acres at 1413-1501 NC Highway 54 from RS-20 and OI/OI(D) to Residential Suburban Multifamily with a Development Plan (RS-M(D)) allowing up to 320 apartments or townhouses, with NC 54 right-of-way dedication and a bike lane. Following the preceding debate on corridor traffic and affordability, the rezoning and consistency statement passed on split voice votes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved 4-2 (rezoning and consistency statement, voice votes with two audible nays)

votes.item_title: Approve Zoning Map Change: Southside East Phases 2 & 3 (Z14-00034)
votes.notes: Rezones 10.7 acres at Plum St from PDR 5.12 to RU-M(D) for 250 units with 1.2 parking spaces/unit reduction. Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented the 250-unit Southside East Phases 2 and 3 rezoning with a 1.2 spaces-per-unit parking reduction and bus shelter commitment. Council Member Diane Catotti confirmed with Transportation staff Bill Judge that sidewalk ramps and pedestrian signals at Roxboro, Lakewood, and Mangum were included in the city's FY16 Capital Improvement Project budget. Council Member Don Moffitt secured a verbal proffer from the developer (MBS) to install a bicycle maintenance and repair station on private Phase 1 or Phase 2 property rather than public right-of-way, and the rezoning passed unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Southside East Phases 2 & 3 (Z14-00034)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement for Z14-00034; Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after approving the Southside East Phases 2 and 3 rezoning, Council moved and seconded the statutory consistency statement affirming alignment with the Comprehensive Plan. No additional discussion occurred, and the motion passed unanimously 6-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Street Closings: Hendrick Automotive Group (SC14-00012 through SC14-00016)
votes.notes: Closes ~5,800 linear ft across five former Kenton Heights subdivision streets. Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young outlined Hendrick Automotive Group's request to close approximately 5,800 linear feet across five streets in the former Kenton Heights subdivision—including Caris Place, Kenton Drive, and Santa Clara Drive—to merge the right-of-way into the previously approved auto mall development. No council members asked questions and no members of the public spoke during the hearing. The motion passed unanimously 6-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Accept Public Hearing Comments and Approve Draft 2015-2020 Consolidated Plan, FY15-16 Annual Action Plan & Analysis of Impediments
votes.notes: Required HUD public hearing prior to May 15 submission; Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Community Development staff presented the draft 2015-2020 Consolidated Plan, FY15-16 Annual Action Plan, and Analysis of Impediments ahead of the May 15 HUD deadline, while Edith Thompson (Rebuilding Durham) and Rebecca Howard-Barnes (Habitat for Humanity) testified on affordable housing partnerships. Council Member Diane Catotti reviewed Habitat's 11-lot acquisition/rehab and 20 second-mortgage allocations, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden urged technical assistance workshops so newer nonprofits can compete for federal and Penny for Housing funds. Council Member Steve Schewel raised concerns over HMDA mortgage lending racial disparities, Durham Rescue Mission's absence from HMIS data, 59% renter cost-burden, and Medicaid non-expansion before Council unanimously approved the item 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Zoning Map Change: Sutton Station (Z14-00025)
votes.notes: Rezones 15.94 acres at 5800 Fayetteville Rd from OI to MU(D) with no added square footage. Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Z14-00025 to rezone the existing Sutton Station office and retail center from OI to Mixed Use with a Development Plan allowing expanded retail uses without increasing building square footage, adding trip caps and a bus shelter. Applicant representative Ron Horvath explained that the 2006 UDO restricted retail flexibility under OI zoning, and confirmed in response to Council Member Don Moffitt that BPAC recommendations for bicycle racks and American Tobacco Trail signage were addressed. Council approved the rezoning 6-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Sutton Station (Z14-00025)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement for Z14-00025; Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the Sutton Station zoning map change vote, Council took up the statutory consistency statement. No further discussion occurred, and the motion passed unanimously 6-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Hamilton Centre II (A14-00006)
votes.notes: Changes 5.02 acres at 7010 NC 751 Highway from Office to Commercial. Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented A14-00006 on behalf of Horvath Associates to change the Future Land Use Map designation of 5.02 acres at 7010 NC 751 Highway from Office to Commercial, noting a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Representative Ron Horvath stood ready to answer questions on the companion zoning case, and no members of the public spoke. Council closed the hearing and approved the amendment unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Zoning Map Change: Hamilton Centre II (Z14-00021)
votes.notes: Rezones 7010 NC 751 Highway from OI to CG(D) for up to 40,000 sq ft retail/restaurant (~50% retail cap) and bus shelter. Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented the companion rezoning for Hamilton Centre II from OI to Commercial General with a Development Plan allowing up to 40,000 square feet of retail and restaurant uses plus a bus shelter pad. Ron Horvath explained that adding up existing small buildings slightly exceeded Neighborhood Commercial square-footage limits, requiring CG zoning while capping retail at 50% and office at 50%. Council approved the rezoning unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Hamilton Centre II (Z14-00021)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement for Z14-00021; Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after approving the Hamilton Centre II zoning map change, Council voted on the statutory consistency statement. The motion passed unanimously 6-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Highway 54 Residential (A14-00005)
ayes: All present members (4 of 6 voting Aye; individual roll call not recorded)
nays: Two dissenting members (voice vote nays not individually named)
votes.notes: Changes 21.72 acres at 1413-1501 NC 54 from Office to Medium-High Density Residential; 6 members present (Eugene Brown excused absent); two audible nays in voice vote following traffic/tree/affordability critiques by Mayor Bell and Steve Schewel.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Hopper Communities' request to change 21.72 acres at NC 54 and Revere Road from Office to Medium-High Density Residential, noting higher market demand for apartments than office and lower peak-hour trip generation than office zoning. Mayor Bill Bell strongly questioned cumulative traffic congestion along un-widened NC 54 and woodland clearing, leading Young to confirm corridor traffic is very close to the threshold where staff would recommend denial. Applicant Jared Edens highlighted right-of-way dedication, bike lanes, and a proffered $21,500 ($500 per projected student) donation to Durham Public Schools, while Council Member Steve Schewel criticized the inclusion of 320 market-rate units with zero affordable housing; the voice vote passed 4-2 with two audible nays.

votes.item_title: Approve Zoning Map Change: Highway 54 Residential (Z14-00018)
ayes: All present members (4 of 6 voting Aye; individual roll call not recorded)
nays: Two dissenting members (voice vote nays not individually named)
votes.notes: Rezones 21.72 acres at 1413-1501 NC 54 to RS-M(D) for up to 320 multifamily units; 6 members present (Eugene Brown excused absent); two audible nays in voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young introduced the companion rezoning of 21.72 acres at 1413-1501 NC 54 from RS-20 and OI/OI(D) to RS-M(D) for up to 320 multifamily units, incorporating NC 54 right-of-way dedication, a bike lane, and site entrance improvements along with the applicant's $21,500 DPS proffer from the prior item. With the prior debate incorporated into the record and no additional public speakers, Council closed the public hearing. Two members voiced 'Nay' in the voice vote, and the rezoning passed 4-2.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Highway 54 Residential (Z14-00018)
ayes: All present members (4 of 6 voting Aye; individual roll call not recorded)
nays: Two dissenting members (voice vote nays not individually named)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement for Z14-00018; 6 members present; two audible nays in voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the split 4-2 rezoning vote on Highway 54 Residential, Council voted on the required statutory consistency statement. As with the underlying FLUM amendment and zoning map change, two members voiced 'Nay' during the voice vote, passing the consistency statement 4-2.

disagreements.issue: NC Highway 54 Traffic Saturation, Tree Loss, and Lack of Affordable Housing in Highway 54 Residential (A14-00005 & Z14-00018)
disagreements.summary: The 21.72-acre plan amendment and rezoning for 320 market-rate multifamily units at NC Highway 54 and Revere Road passed on split 4-2 voice votes after sharp questioning over corridor traffic congestion, wooded land clearing, and zero affordable housing units.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve changing 21.72 acres from Office to Medium-High Density Residential / RS-M(D) for 320 multifamily units.
side_a_arguments: Multifamily residential has strong market demand and generates slightly fewer peak-hour trips than existing Office zoning.

The applicant's traffic impact analysis showed adequate peak-hour intersection service and provided NC 54 right-of-way dedication, a bike lane, center turn-lane continuity, and a $21,500 donation to Durham Public Schools.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose adding 320 market-rate multifamily units along an un-widened NC 54 corridor without affordable housing commitments.
side_b_arguments: Mayor Bill Bell warned that approving more developments on NC 54 before state widening risks severe cumulative traffic gridlock and removes wooded areas.
Council Member Steve Schewel objected that all 320 units were market-rate with zero affordable housing units, urging stronger local affordable housing tools.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-2 on voice votes (with two audible nays out of six members present; individual vote names not called).

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Durham City Council reviewed board appointments, summer youth employment funding, Hillandale Golf Course management, and the Southside East Phases 2 and 3 expedited rezoning. Council approved the City Manager's priority items adding continued public hearings (Items 25-29), presented ceremonial proclamations, and heard Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden introduce Dr. Eugene Washington, the new Chancellor of Health Affairs and CEO of Duke University Health System. During Citizens Matters, Council and staff examined the expiration of $94,000 in solid-waste hauling contract grants that previously supported summer youth litter-abatement jobs, leaving funding for five of ten targeted positions. On Item 14 (Southside East Phases 2 and 3 rezoning), Council requested advance clarity on the proposed 1.2 spaces-per-unit parking reduction, affordable unit counts across 37 parcels, and five Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) crosswalk recommendations. Council confirmed 7-0 appointments to the Housing Appeals and Environmental Affairs Boards, referred the BPAC appointment back for re-advertisement, granted an excused absence request, and unanimously set the regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items & Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager added continued public hearings (Items 25-29) carried over from the prior Council meeting, which Council approved unanimously. Council then presented two ceremonial items, including a Parks and Recreation and public safety proclamation.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of Dr. Eugene Washington (Duke University Health System)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden introduced Dr. Eugene Washington, who joined Duke on April 1 as Chancellor of Health Affairs and President/CEO of Duke University Health System after his prior leadership at UCLA. Council welcomed Dr. Washington and underscored Duke's ongoing partnership with Durham.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters & Summer Youth Employment Funding Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A speaker commended Durham Police for rescuing him during a Thanksgiving mugging and raised a signage complaint on Liberty Street. Council then questioned OEWD Director Kevin Dick and Solid Waste staff about the loss of ~$94,000 in solid-waste contract tonnage grants for summer youth litter-control jobs, noting remaining funds covered five of ten positions in the PAC 1 / Poverty Reduction area and discussing how to improve youth outreach.

agenda_items.title: Alston Bridge, Hillandale Golf Course Agreement & Southside East Phases 2-3 Rezoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed the Hillandale Golf Course management amendment (Item 10), noting a small contract-language discrepancy and praising manager Carl Kimball's four-year turnaround of the course. On the expedited Southside East Phases 2 and 3 rezoning (Item 14), members asked staff and the applicant to provide advance answers on the 1.2 parking-space ratio, affordable unit distribution, and whether the developer would voluntarily adopt five BPAC pedestrian recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments, Excused Absence & Setting the Regular Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk reported 7-vote appointments to the Housing Appeals Board and Environmental Affairs Board (three members) while referring Item 5 (BPAC) back for re-advertisement. Council unanimously approved an excused absence for the next Council meeting and work session and set the regular agenda: Consent 1-4 and 6-13, and GBA Public Hearings 14-16 and 25-29.

votes.item_title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Items (Continued Public Hearings 25-29)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Added continued public hearings 25 through 29 from the prior Council meeting.

votes.item_title: Board Appointments (Housing Appeals Board & Durham City-County Environmental Affairs Board)
votes.notes: Item 5 (Durham Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission) was sent back to be re-advertised.
votes.discussion_detail: Clerk announced 7 votes for the Housing Appeals Board nominee and 7 votes each for three Environmental Affairs Board appointees.

votes.item_title: Approve Excused Absence for Next Council Meeting and Work Session
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved a council member's request for an excused absence at the upcoming Council meeting and work session.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-4, 6-13; Public Hearings 14-16, 25-29)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Set Consent Items 1-4 and 6-13, GBA Public Hearings 14-16 and 25-29, disposed of Items 17-24, and referred back Item 5.

meetings.title: Durham City Council April 6, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: All seven members of the Durham City Council met on April 6, 2015, issuing seven civic proclamations and continuing five planning hearings to April 20 at the applicants' requests. Council unanimously approved Hendrick Southpoint Overall (330,000 sq ft auto mall consolidation), Magnolia Grill's outdoor dining expansion for Monuts Donuts on 9th Street, the FY 2015-16 Budget Development Guidelines, and the 2015 HIDTA drug grant, while passing the Auto Park Center rezoning for a Sheetz convenience store and fuel station 6-1 over Council Member Diane Catotti's environmental objection.

agenda_items.title: Seven Civic Proclamations (Diabetes, Community Development, Early Childhood, Water Conservation, Fair Housing, Everyone Matters, Sexual Assault Awareness)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented proclamations for Alicia B. Angels Day, National Community Development Week (highlighting Durham's national Audrey Nelson Award), Week of the Young Child, National Mayor's Challenge for Water Conservation, Fair Housing Month, Everyone Matters Day (with Durham Youth Commission), and Sexual Assault Awareness Month / Start by Believing campaign. Council members also shared light-hearted remarks regarding water conservation and the Duke-Wisconsin NCAA championship wager.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Requests to Continue Five Planning Cases to April 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield reported that applicants for Items 15 (Sutton Station), 17-18 (Hamilton Centre II), and 21-22 (Highway 54 Residential) requested continuances to the April 20, 2015 business meeting. Council approved opening and continuing those public hearings.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-4, 7-11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved unpulled consent agenda items including minutes, Historic Preservation Commission and Appearance Commission appointments, street and infrastructure acceptances, the bid report, annual police vehicle purchase, West Ellerbee Creek Trail design amendment with Stewart Engineering, Diamond View I LLC encroachment at DBAP, and condemnation of 531 East Carver Street for the Carver Street Extension project. Items 5 and 12 were pulled by resident Victoria Peterson.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Hendrick Southpoint Overall (Z14-00023)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Z14-00023 for 80.7 acres at 107 Kenton Drive within the Falls/Jordan Watershed overlay, combining two previously approved auto park zonings (Z12-00025 and Z14-00002) into a single Commercial General Development Plan up to 330,000 square feet and removing the internal project boundary buffer. Louis Cheek represented Hendrick Automotive Group, with no public opposition.

agenda_items.title: Continuance of Public Hearings for Sutton Station, Hamilton Centre II, and Highway 54 Residential
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consistent with the City Manager's priority items, Council formally opened and continued the public hearings on Item 15 (Sutton Station, Z14-00025) and en masse on Items 17-18 (Hamilton Centre II, A14-00006/Z14-00021) and Items 21-22 (Highway 54 Residential, A14-00005/Z14-00018) to the April 20, 2015 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Auto Park Center / Sheetz (Z14-00011)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a rezoning of 6.23 acres at 7520 NC 751 (at Interstate 40) from Commercial Neighborhood (CN(D)) to Commercial General (CG(D)) for 5,000-40,000 square feet of retail/restaurant uses, represented by Patrick Byker on behalf of Sheetz, with a berm/wall buffer reduction and state-compliant upland floodplain corridor protections. Council Member Diane Catotti opposed the rezoning, echoing DOST's concern about gasoline sales next to the Lower New Hope Creek natural heritage floodplain forest and arguing CN zoning was more appropriate.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Rezoning passed 6-1 (Catotti Nay); Consistency Statement passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Magnolia Grill (A14-00008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a FLUM amendment for a 0.165-acre parcel on the east side of 9th Street (between Englewood Avenue and West Knox Street) from Medium Density Residential to Commercial for outdoor dining at Monuts Donuts. Applicant representative Ron Horvath committed to a 9:00 PM outdoor closing time; neighbor David Jolly supported the 9:00 PM limit but urged 'no parking here to corner' signage and enforcement at West Knox and Ardelle Streets, which City Manager Tom Bonfield agreed to have Transportation evaluate.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Magnolia Grill (Z14-00024)

agenda_items.title: FY 2015-16 Budget Development Guidelines

agenda_items.title: 2015 High-Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) Grant Award

disagreements.issue: Auto Park Center / Sheetz Commercial General Rezoning Adjacent to Lower New Hope Creek Floodplain (Z14-00011)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to rezone 6.23 acres at NC 751 and Interstate 40 from Commercial Neighborhood to Commercial General for a Sheetz convenience store and gas station, over Council Member Diane Catotti's dissent citing DOST environmental concerns.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve CG(D) rezoning to allow Sheetz convenience retail, restaurant, and fuel sales near I-40.
side_a_arguments: The site sits directly across from an auto mall next to I-40 and brings jobs and private investment to Durham.
The development plan prohibits residential and electronic gaming uses, meets state natural heritage floodplain buffer guidelines, and received 12-0 Planning Commission support.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain Commercial Neighborhood zoning and oppose gasoline sales adjacent to the Lower New Hope Creek natural heritage corridor.
side_b_arguments: Echoed Durham Open Space and Trails Commission concerns about placing fuel sales directly adjacent to the exceptional-quality Lower New Hope Creek floodplain forest and steep slopes.
Neighborhood Commercial zoning remains more appropriate for the corridor than General Commercial.
disagreements.resolution: Rezoning passed 6-1 with Diane Catotti voting Nay; the statutory consistency statement subsequently passed 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden in Mayor Bill Bell's absence, the Durham City Council reviewed FY 2015-2016 budget development guidelines, approved affordable housing financing for the Whitted School project, and scrutinized police vehicle and investigative expenditures. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items, including a request to suspend the rules for immediate action on Item 6 due to low-income housing tax credit deadlines. On Item 5 (FY15-16 Budget Development Guidelines), Budget Director Bertha Johnson clarified the 14.02-cent debt and capital tax cap, Downtown Business Improvement District collections, an estimated $6-$7 million risk from potential state sales tax redistribution, and a 3 percent cap on water and sewer rate increases. Following staff explanation of the 0 percent, 40-year loan terms required to match state housing finance agency rules, Council unanimously suspended the rules and approved Item 6 (commitment to Integral Development LLC for the Whitted School project). Council also questioned police fleet V6/V8 vehicle allocations and $44,000 in informant/special investigation funds (Item 8) before unanimously setting the regular agenda and entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items & Closed Session Notice
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested suspending the rules to vote today on Item 6 (Integral Development LLC commitment for the Whitted School project) due to tax credit filing deadlines, plus a brief introduction by Police Chief Lopez. Council approved the priority items unanimously, and the City Attorney requested a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(7) regarding alleged criminal misconduct investigations.

agenda_items.title: FY 2015-2016 Budget Development Guidelines
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson explained that the 14.02-cent debt service and cash capital cap comprised 12.76 cents for the General Fund (~$20 million annually) and 1.26 cents for enterprise funds (parking and ballpark), alongside a potential 1-cent public safety allocation and a maximum 3 percent water/sewer rate increase. Members also requested a budget-time accounting of Downtown BID revenues and clean-and-safe expenditures and discussed $6-$7 million in potential exposure from state sales tax redistribution.

agenda_items.title: Commitment to Integral Development LLC for the Whitted School Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff clarified that the 0 percent interest, 40-year loan terms were required to align the pro forma with North Carolina Housing Finance Agency and HUD financing requirements. Council unanimously suspended the rules and unanimously approved the commitment by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Police Vehicle Purchase Inquiry, Agenda Setting & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eugene Brown questioned the more than $1 million police vehicle purchase regarding V6 versus V8 engine deployment and asked about a $44,000 PEP line item, which staff confirmed was for informant and special investigation funds. Council then unanimously set the regular agenda (Consent 1-5 and 7-12; GBA Public Hearings 14-22; Items 6 and 13 disposed) and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided; Mayor Bill Bell was noted as delayed at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved priority handling for Item 6 and an introduction by Chief Lopez.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Vote on Item 6 (Whitted School Project)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules to allow immediate work-session action ahead of tax-credit filing deadlines.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Commitment to Integral Development LLC for the Whitted School Project
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the city financing commitment (0 percent, 40-year loan terms matching NCHFA requirements) for the Whitted School affordable housing project.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-5, 7-12; Public Hearings 14-22)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Set Consent Items 1-5 and 7-12 and GBA Public Hearings 14-22, with Items 6 and 13 disposed.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(7) Criminal Misconduct Investigations)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(7) to hear reports concerning investigations of alleged criminal misconduct.

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 16, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting briefly on March 16, 2015 with six members present and Council Member Eddie Davis granted an excused absence, the Durham City Council issued proclamations for Creek Week and the 41st Annual Durham CROP Hunger Walk. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda—including dedicated housing funds for DCLT and Woodland Resources to preserve affordable rental units—the Brier Creek Assembly 115-acre consolidated annexation and initial Rural Residential zoning, and Civilian Police Review Board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Council Member Eddie Davis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon roll call showing six members present, Council unanimously granted an excused absence to Council Member Eddie Davis.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations for Creek Week and 41st Annual CROP Hunger Walk Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell proclaimed March 21-28, 2015 as Creek Week (received by Laura Webb Smith, Tanya Dautlick of Keep Durham Beautiful, and Nathan Lee Williams) and March 22, 2015 as Durham CROP Hunger Walk Day (received by Bob Newlin). Council also congratulated Council Member Steve Schewel on completing a marathon and qualifying for the Boston Marathon.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1, 3-6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council adopted the consent agenda except Item 2 (pulled by a public speaker) and Item 10 (on the General Business Agenda), approving a Housing Appeals Board appointment, dedicated housing funds to Durham Community Land Trustees Inc. and Woodland Resources Inc. to preserve rental housing at Morehead Hill, West Park Apartments, Mutual Manor, and Rockwood Cottages, the 2015-2016 property/casualty insurance plan, the Joint City-County Economic Development Strategic Plan, and SunGard police software renewals.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Brier Creek Assembly
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented M/I Homes' request for a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and initial Rural Residential (RR) zoning across 115 acres in Durham and Wake Counties south of Andrews Chapel Road, projecting positive fiscal impact in year four under 132 single-family homes. Applicant Jared Edens noted a future rezoning for ~450 units was planned for June.

agenda_items.title: Confirmation of Civilian Police Review Board Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speaker Ralph Zaidi (Assistant Minister, Nation of Islam) pulled Item 2 to serve and place on the public record his notarized North Carolina public records and FOIA requests delivered to City Manager Tom Bonfield and City Attorney Patrick Baker. Following his remarks, Council confirmed the Civilian Police Review Board appointments.

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absence to Council Member Eddie Davis
votes.notes: Eddie Davis absent (excused).
votes.discussion_detail: During the opening roll call, the City Clerk noted that Council Member Eddie Davis had requested an excused absence. A motion to excuse Davis was made and seconded without objection. All six present members voted Aye by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Consolidated Annexation, Utility Extension Agreement, and Initial RR Zoning: Brier Creek Assembly
votes.notes: 115 acres south of Andrews Chapel Rd in Durham and Wake Counties; initial RR zoning (up to 132 homes). Eddie Davis excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented M/I Homes' consolidated annexation request for 115 acres at Brier Creek Assembly, covering utility extension capacity, voluntary annexation, and initial Rural Residential (RR) zoning supporting up to 132 single-family homes, while noting the developer intends to return later for an upzoning. Representative Jared Edens estimated under 1,000 projected residents even under a planned 450-unit rezoning in June, and Mayor Bell commented that annexation follows growth already arriving in the region. No opponents spoke, and Council approved the consolidated items unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Brier Creek Assembly Initial Zoning
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement for Brier Creek Assembly initial RR zoning; Eddie Davis excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the Brier Creek Assembly consolidated annexation approval, Council moved and seconded the required statutory consistency statement. No further discussion occurred, and the motion passed unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Confirm Civilian Police Review Board Members (Pulled Consent Item 2)
votes.notes: Pulled by speaker Ralph Zaidi to present public records requests; Eddie Davis excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Ralph Zaidi, Assistant Minister with the Nation of Islam, spoke on pulled Item 2 to announce that he had served notarized North Carolina General Statutes Chapter 132 public records and FOIA requests on City Manager Tom Bonfield and City Attorney Patrick Baker regarding the confirmation and related records, requesting timely responses. Council asked no questions of the speaker and offered no debate on the appointments. The motion to confirm the Civilian Police Review Board members passed unanimously 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 5, 2015 Durham City Council Work Session, Council reviewed workers' compensation insurance renewals, economic development planning, light rail alignment and rail maintenance facility input to the MPO, and the joint City-County Disparity Study. Finance Director David Boyd explained a 25% workers' compensation premium increase tied to a 15-month renewal cycle and detailed the city's $1 million self-insured retention, while Council Member Steve Schewel questioned OEWD staff on whether synthetic TIF revenues for economic development infrastructure could compete with core services like police, fire, and EMS. Duke Energy representatives presented the second year of their Residential Neighborhood Program serving low-income residents, and Council discussed coordinating MPO input on the rail maintenance facility with Council representatives Steve Schewel and Diane Catotti after public hearings. Consultants presented the City's first disparity study in 15 years, finding underutilization of minority- and women-owned firms across all procurement categories and prompting discussion of expanding Durham's 2003 ordinance beyond subcontractor-focused goals and the certified city database; at the close, it was announced that six council members confirmed the City Manager's five appointments to the Civilian Police Review Board before setting the agenda.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Closed Session Request (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney requested one closed session item for attorney-client consultation regarding a claim pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3). The City Manager reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Workers' Compensation and Excess Liability Insurance Renewal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member asked why workers' compensation premiums increased substantially. Finance Director David Boyd explained that premiums rose approximately 25% due to moving to a 15-month renewal period to align with the budget cycle, and clarified how the $1 million self-insured retention works alongside excess liability and excess workers' compensation coverage.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Strategic Plan Study and Infrastructure Financing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel questioned Kevin Dick of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development regarding whether staff would lead model development site creation or support external efforts, and noted shorter timeframes in the slideshow compared to the five-year timeframes in the full report. Schewel also cautioned that synthetic TIF or value-added tax revenues for economic development infrastructure face competing demands from essential services such as police, fire, and EMS.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment Alleging Discrimination in Application Selection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A speaker expressed dissatisfaction with how winning applications were handled, alleging religious discrimination and stating an intent to challenge the outcome before departing.

agenda_items.title: Duke Energy Residential Neighborhood Program (Year 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Duke Energy District Manager Indira Everett and Program Manager Valencia Rauner presented the second year of the Residential Neighborhood Program, which provides free home energy assessments and up to 16 efficiency measures to income-qualifying residents. Having served roughly 396 homes in its first Durham neighborhood and over 12,000 across the Carolinas since March 2013, Duke Energy plans a kickoff targeting the Eastern Durham community and coordination with local groups and police.

agenda_items.title: Light Rail Alignment, Traffic Management, and Rail Maintenance Facility Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff discussed coordination with Duke, NCDOT, and City Transportation to avoid concentrating conflicting vehicular, pedestrian, and transit movements at a single intersection. Council also discussed the anticipated process for submitting recommendations to the Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) on the rail maintenance facility, with members favoring waiting until after public hearings so community feedback informs Council's priorities shared with MPO representatives Steve Schewel and Diane Catotti.

agenda_items.title: Joint City-County Disparity Study on MWBE Participation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consultants presented the joint City-County Disparity Study—the City of Durham's first in 15 years since the 2000 study—documenting underutilization across all major ethnic groups in construction, architecture and engineering, general services, and goods. Council and staff discussed how Durham's 2003 ordinance focuses primarily on subcontractors and limits availability tracking to firms certified in the city's database (noting Callis Contracting as the only database firm with an unlimited GC license), as well as capacity-building through SBA bond/loan guarantees, mentor-protege programs, and racial equity training.

agenda_items.title: Civilian Police Review Board Confirmation and Agenda Setting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: It was announced that six council members confirmed the City Manager's five appointments to the Civilian Police Review Board. Council then proceeded to set consent agenda items 1 through 6 and GBA public hearing item 10.
