meetings.title: Durham City Council March 2, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on March 2, 2015 (with six members at roll call and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden arriving late), hearing a snowstorm recovery briefing, the 2014 Annual Police Crime Report, and a public hearing on the FY 2015-16 Budget and CIP. During the crime report, Council Member Steve Schewel challenged Police Chief Jose Lopez's argument that a one-year spike in aggravated assaults justified hiring more frontline officers, while resident Victoria Peterson pressed Council on gun violence in Black neighborhoods and minority workforce participation on the new Police Headquarters contracts. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda, Hendrick Southpoint Phase 2 consolidated annexation, and three pulled contracts (Frontier 911 settlement and Lendlease/O'Brien Atkins Police Headquarters contracts).

agenda_items.title: Arbor Day and MS Awareness Week Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented an Arbor Day proclamation (celebrating Durham's 32nd year as a Tree City USA and announcing a March 14 planting of 100 trees in Old West Durham) to Urban Forestry Manager Alex Johnson and partners, followed by an MS Awareness Week proclamation to Constance McCleary. Council Member Don Moffitt and Mayor Bell also thanked city staff for winter storm work and noted chamber renovations.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: Winter Snowstorm Recovery Recap
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield briefed Council on city operations during the recent 4-to-8-inch snowstorm, noting crews spread over 1,100 tons of salt and 22,000 gallons of brine, Police handled over 1,000 assistance calls and 45 accidents, General Services cleared dozens of downed trees, and Solid Waste completed nearly all two-week makeup routes by Saturday.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-6, 8-13, 16-20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the unpulled consent agenda covering minutes, board appointments, Regional Scenario Planning and Regional Freight Plan agreements with Raleigh and NCDOT, the Q2 Financial Report, January 2015 bid report, Mission Place upset-bid sale, NCDOT property sales/conveyances for Old Chapel Hill Road and Alston Avenue widening/bridge projects, a Duke Park lease to the Durham Bicycle Co-op, police promotional testing, Carver Street Extension and Guess Road agreements. Items 7, 14, and 15 were pulled by Victoria Peterson.

agenda_items.title: 2014 Annual Police Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez reported that Part 1 violent crime rose 15% in 2014 (driven by shootings into occupied dwellings/vehicles increasing aggravated assault victim counts by 23%) and property crime rose 2%, though 2000-2014 violent and property crime rates dropped 22% and 41% respectively. Council Members Steve Schewel, Diane Catotti, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt questioned Chief Lopez on officer staffing requests, Black male applicant written-test pass rates, misdemeanor diversion training, mental health CIT calls, written consent searches, non-sworn vacancies, and community group meetings, while Victoria Peterson clashed with Mayor Bell over Black homicides.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Hendrick Southpoint Phase 2 (PDG14-01 / Z14-02)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Scott Whiteman and applicant attorney Louis Cheek presented a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and initial Commercial General (CG(D)) zoning for up to 150,000 square feet of non-residential auto park development in Phase 2, featuring wall, berm, and lighting commitments negotiated with nearby neighbors. Transportation staff Bill Judge clarified for Steve Schewel that Fayetteville Road widening earned street impact fee credits.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved unanimously (annexation/UEA/initial zoning and consistency statement)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2015-2016 Budget and FY 2016-2021 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson introduced the early budget and CIP public hearing ahead of the Manager's May 18 budget presentation. Four speakers—Stephen Hopkins, Victoria Peterson, Louise, and Kevin Armstrong—called for investments in Northeast Central Durham, homelessness prevention, $5 million for youth and job-skills programs at Holton Resource Center, affordable housing near transit, and D3 Community Outreach, while Don Moffitt placed Part 2 crime declines and Chapel Hill homicide jurisdiction into the record.

agenda_items.title: Frontier Telephone Settlement ($600,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Communications Director Jim Soukup explained that the $600,000 settlement resolved a five-year tariff and 911 fee dispute with Frontier Communications out of 911 surcharge funds with no General Fund or tax impact. Victoria Peterson asked the City Manager to inquire how many Durham residents Frontier has hired.

agenda_items.title: Construction Manager at Risk Contract: Police Headquarters Complex (Lendlease US Construction Inc.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 14 to challenge Lendlease's workforce diversity and demand disaggregated reporting on African-American male and Durham-resident hires across prime and subcontracted trades. Staff explained the initial $215,000 pre-construction phase pairs Lendlease with Durham-based Black-owned Callis Construction Company (40% of construction work) and that a formal workforce development plan will be required prior to setting the Guaranteed Maximum Price.

agenda_items.title: Architectural Design Contract: Police Headquarters Complex (O'Brien/Atkins Associates, PA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson questioned African-American representation and subcontracting opportunities under the roughly $5 million architectural design contract with O'Brien/Atkins Associates (which staff noted includes a senior African-American partner and M/WBE commitments) and criticized work sessions not being televised. Mayor Bell noted work sessions are audio-streamed online and called the vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Consolidated Annexation, Utility Extension Agreement, and Initial CG(D) Zoning: Hendrick Southpoint Phase 2 (PDG14-01 / Z14-02)
votes.notes: Initial CG(D) zoning for up to 150,000 sq ft non-residential development. Roll call had 6 members present (Cole-McFadden arrived late).
votes.discussion_detail: Scott Whiteman presented the utility extension agreement, voluntary contiguous annexation, and initial CG(D) zoning for Hendrick Southpoint Phase 2, highlighting immediate positive fiscal impact, a 12-0 Planning Commission endorsement, and neighbor-negotiated buffers, walls, berms, and loudspeaker/lighting limits. Applicant attorney Louis Cheek noted collaboration with neighboring residents on Auburn Drive, while Transportation staff Bill Judge answered Council Member Steve Schewel's questions regarding Fayetteville Road widening impact-fee credits and lack of residential parks impact fees. Council approved the three consolidated actions unanimously.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Hendrick Southpoint Phase 2 Initial Zoning (Z14-02)
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement under NCGS 160A-383.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after approving the Hendrick Southpoint Phase 2 consolidated annexation and initial zoning, Council moved and seconded the required statutory consistency statement. No further questions were raised, and the motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Accept Public Hearing Comments on FY 2015-2016 Budget and FY 2016-2021 CIP
votes.notes: Public hearing input ahead of May 18 City Manager budget presentation.
votes.discussion_detail: Bertha Johnson introduced the budget and CIP public hearing, noting the City Manager's budget presentation on May 18 and subsequent hearing on June 1. Four residents testified in favor of sustained Northeast Central Durham investment, homelessness integration, $5 million for youth job-skills training at Holton Resource Center, affordable housing near transit corridors, and funding for D3 Community Outreach. Council Member Don Moffitt also placed into the record that Part 2 crimes declined from 8,993 in 2012 and clarified jurisdiction of the recent Chapel Hill murders before Council voted unanimously to close and accept the hearing comments.

votes.item_title: Approve Frontier Telephone 911 Settlement ($600,000) (Pulled Consent Item 7)
votes.notes: Pulled by Victoria Peterson; paid from 911 surcharge funds with no General Fund impact.
votes.discussion_detail: In response to Victoria Peterson pulling Item 7, Emergency Communications Director Jim Soukup explained that the $600,000 settlement concluded five years of tariff and 911-fee negotiations with Frontier following Durham's transition to a next-generation 911 system with Intrado, using surcharge funds rather than property taxes. Peterson urged City Manager Tom Bonfield to request local hiring figures from Frontier in connection with the Mayor's Poverty Initiative. Council approved the settlement unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Construction Manager at Risk Contract with Lendlease US Construction Inc. for Police Headquarters Complex (Pulled Consent Item 14)
votes.notes: $215,000 pre-construction phase; partners with Durham-based Black-owned Callis Construction Company for 40% of construction work.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 14 to question Lendlease's workforce demographics and demand specific tracking of African-American male and Durham-resident hires rather than aggregated minority figures. City staff clarified that the current $215,000 award covers only pre-construction services, that Lendlease has partnered with Black-owned Durham firm Callis Construction Company for 40% of construction work, and that a full workforce development plan will be executed with Economic and Workforce Development prior to setting the Guaranteed Maximum Price. Mayor Bell invited Peterson to attend the upcoming disparity study work session, and Council approved the contract unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approve Architectural Design Contract with O'Brien/Atkins Associates, PA for Police Headquarters Complex (Pulled Consent Item 15)
votes.notes: Pulled by Victoria Peterson; ~$5M design contract.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 15 to question African-American representation at O'Brien/Atkins Associates on the nearly $5 million Police Headquarters design contract, advocate for local Black subcontractors and city-trained youth in fiber optics, and urge that Council work sessions be televised. Staff noted O'Brien/Atkins includes a senior African-American partner and exceeds design-contract M/WBE participation targets, while Mayor Bell noted work-session audio is streamed online. Council approved the contract unanimously by voice vote.

disagreements.issue: Police Officer Staffing Request Logic vs. Long-Term Crime Decline (2014 Annual Crime Report)
disagreements.summary: During discussion of the 2014 Annual Crime Report, Council Member Steve Schewel disputed Police Chief Jose Lopez's budget rationale for adding frontline police officers based on a one-year spike in aggravated assaults, while public speaker Victoria Peterson clashed with Mayor Bill Bell over Council responsiveness to Black homicide victims.
disagreements.side_a_position: A 15% one-year rise in Part 1 violent crime (driven by aggravated assaults and shootings into residences/vehicles) requires additional police staffing and targeted enforcement.
side_a_arguments: Shooting into occupied dwellings and vehicles increased aggravated assault victim counts by 23% in 2014.
Police leadership argued in budget sessions that additional line officers are needed to address violent crime and improve response-time targets.
disagreements.side_b_position: A single-year spike in aggravated assaults does not logically justify permanent officer increases given a 15-year 40% crime decline; any expansion must be justified by specific community-policing plans.
side_b_arguments: Durham achieved a 40% long-term drop in crime since 2000 and near-record-low property crime with roughly the same or fewer officers.

Four different departmental staffing formulas yielded estimates ranging from zero to 111 added officers, showing the department needs to present a concrete community-policing model before expecting Council budget support.
disagreements.resolution: Informational report (no vote); Chief Lopez agreed to keep Schewel's community-policing criteria in mind during upcoming budget deliberations.

meetings.title: Durham City Council February 19, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: Convening early at 5:00 PM during severe cold weather with all seven members present, Mayor Bill Bell delivered his 13th Annual State of the City Address highlighting Durham's 4.4% unemployment rate, 29% population growth since 2001 alongside nearly 50% lower total index crime, Triple-A bond ratings, Southside redevelopment, Durham-Orange Light Rail planning, police-community relations recommendations, and the 2015 'Year of Action' for the Northeast Central Durham Poverty Reduction Initiative. Council also proclaimed Larry Stogner Day with a Key to the City and unanimously approved winter-weather recycling makeup plans and an 11-item consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: 13th Annual State of the City Address by Mayor Bill Bell
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell reviewed 2014 economic and civic milestones—including the Durham Innovation District, new hotels, national rankings, 4.4% unemployment, and a long-term drop in index crime per 100,000 from nearly 7,960 in 2001 to 5,300 in 2014—framed around the city's five strategic plan goals. Looking ahead to 2015, he emphasized equitable employee discipline, Southside East and West mixed-income housing, veteran homelessness, the new police headquarters charrette, Durham-Orange Light Rail engineering timelines (2016-2026), fiber deployment, U.S. Conference of Mayors police-community trust reforms, and executing Northeast Central Durham poverty-reduction action plans.

agenda_items.title: Larry Stogner Day Proclamation and Key to the City
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief recess, Mayor Bell proclaimed February 19, 2015 as Larry Stogner Day and presented the Key to the City to retiring WTVD ABC11 news anchor Larry Stogner after 39 years of regional broadcast journalism. Council Members Don Moffitt, Eddie Davis, and Eugene Brown also shared acknowledgments and tributes (including condolences to the family of former Council Member Johnny 'Red' Williams).

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: Winter Weather Solid Waste and Recycling Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson announced that due to icy street conditions that suspended Tuesday-Thursday collections, regular refuse would resume the following week without makeup while Blue Week recycling customers would receive special Saturday collection. Council voted to accept the manager's priority report.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously adopted the 11-item consent agenda, including the January 2015 Cash Collections Performance Audit, FY 2014-15 budget/grant/CIP ordinance amendments, two rapid rehousing contracts with Housing for New Hope using ESG, general, and dedicated housing funds, a household hazardous waste contract, software maintenance, an Open Data Initiative professional services contract, a CivicPlus website agreement, LAN network improvements, transit bus disposal, and a railroad waterline agreement.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Item (Winter Weather Solid Waste and Recycling Makeup Schedule)
votes.notes: Establishes Saturday makeup collection for Blue Week recycling customers after cold-weather service suspensions.
votes.discussion_detail: Deputy City Manager for Operations Bo Ferguson explained that street icing forced suspension of solid waste, recycling, and yard waste collections Tuesday through Thursday. Because recycling runs biweekly, staff scheduled Saturday makeup routes for affected Blue Week recycling customers while resuming standard refuse routes on Monday. No questions were raised by Council, and the priority item was accepted 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided over the February 5, 2015 City Council Work Session, where the City Manager highlighted a recently completed debt refinancing generating substantial savings and Council reviewed several administrative consent items including the January 2015 cash collections performance audit, FY 2014-15 budget and CIP amendments, and rapid rehousing contract amendments with Housing for New Hope. Staff and council also reviewed purchasing audit findings comparing higher in-store Office Depot expenditures against lower online city-contract pricing. The centerpiece of the session was an engineering and budget assessment of Durham's five municipal pools—Long Meadow, Forest Hills, Hillside, Campus Hills, and Edison Johnson—detailing floodplain non-compliance and cost-prohibitive repairs at Forest Hills, pump room water infiltration threatening Long Meadow's summer 2015 reopening, significant shell leakage at Hillside, and failing dehumidification units at Campus Hills and Edison Johnson. Council requested pool usage statistics for upcoming budget workshops and unanimously voted by voice vote to set the regular meeting agenda with consent items 1 through 11 and disposal of items 12 through 16.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Debt Refinancing Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager noted that Agenda Item 13 (Katina Parker) would not be present and presented a hard-copy report summarizing a successful debt refinancing completed the prior week with considerable savings. Finance staff were recognized for months of work leading to the transaction.

agenda_items.title: Scheduling Budget and Environmental Affairs Board Discussions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members coordinated with the City Manager on scheduling a presentation involving Alex Johnson during or ahead of the budget process, as well as a follow-up with the Environmental Affairs Board.

agenda_items.title: Consent Items: Cash Collections Audit, Budget Amendments, and Housing for New Hope
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed Consent Item 1 (January 2015 cash collections performance audit), Item 2 (FY 2014-15 budget, grant project, and CIP ordinance amendments), and Items 3 and 4 (Emergency Solutions Grant, General Fund, and Dedicated Housing Fund contract amendments with Housing for New Hope for rapid rehousing services). Council praised Housing for New Hope leadership and city staff for moving residents out of shelters, and waived a redundant staff presentation after confirming members had read the written materials.

agenda_items.title: Office Supply Purchasing Audit Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters walked Council through specific purchasing audit examples showing items bought in-store at Office Depot costing over $38 more than identical online orders under the city discount.

agenda_items.title: Engineering and Budget Assessment of City Aquatics Facilities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: An engineering consultant presented condition findings and budget estimates for five city pools: Long Meadow (closed in 2014 due to pump room electrical hazards; awaiting April assessment of Phase 1 stormwater drain fixes to determine June 2015 reopening versus Phase 2 work into 2016), Forest Hills (aging structure with bathhouse and pump room 4 to 6.5 feet below UDO 100-year floodplain requirements, failing retaining wall, and $70,000 ADA ramp needs judged cost-prohibitive), Hillside (4-6 inches daily shell water loss), and Campus Hills and Edison Johnson (dehumidification failures and lighting/code deficiencies). Council asked the City Manager to return with recommendations and pool usage statistics during upcoming budget workshops.

agenda_items.title: Set Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-11 and Disposal of Items 12-16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the City Manager's recommendation, Council moved, seconded, and approved by unanimous voice vote to set consent items 1 through 11 and dispose of items 12 through 16 before adjourning at 2:17 PM.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda for Regular Meeting (Consent Items 1-11 and Disposal of Items 12-16)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote with no opposition. Cora Cole-McFadden, Diane Catotti, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt were recorded present at roll call; Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Eugene Brown were noted as en route at roll call, and Steve Schewel was not recorded in the roll-call excerpt.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager recommended setting consent items 1-11 and disposing of items 12-16; a council member moved and another seconded.

meetings.title: Durham City Council February 2, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council opened with a recognition of Keep Durham Beautiful and city staff for securing a $10,000 Waste Management Think Green grant targeting urban-tier litter hotspots and public recycling. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda (with Item 7 pulled for public comment), approved a $170,000 economic development incentive agreement with A&J Capital Corporation to redevelop a blighted building at 406 South Driver Street, and authorized a public art mural along the NC 147 retaining wall at Willard Street.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Keep Durham Beautiful and Waste Management Think Green Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell recognized Keep Durham Beautiful, General Services, Solid Waste Management, and Stormwater Services for partnering on a $10,000 Waste Management Think Green grant. Keep Durham Beautiful coordinator Tanya and Waste Management representatives explained that the competitive grant supports an Urban Tier pilot assessing five litter hotspots, increasing recycling at large public events, and evaluating permanent public-space recycling.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Minutes, University Drive Bike/Ped Grant EB-5514, Roundabout Sidewalk Agreement, Dec. 2014 Bid Report, 700 N. Alston Ave Lease)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda titles, pulling Item 7 (Willard Street mural) for a registered speaker and noting Item 8 was on the General Business Agenda. Remaining items included council minutes, a University Drive bicycle and pedestrian facilities grant agreement (TIP EB-5514), a roundabout sidewalk agreement, the December 2014 bid report, and a lease at 700 N. Alston Avenue.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Economic Development Incentive Agreement with A&J Capital Corporation (Ashley Corners, 406 S. Driver Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chris Dickey of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development presented a $170,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant toward a $525,336 redevelopment of a blighted 8,500-square-foot structure at 406 South Driver Street into four ground-floor commercial bays and two second-floor apartments. Council Member Steve Schewel confirmed staff reviewed the project's operating pro forma and urged future agreements to secure binding affordability covenants when developers propose affordable units, while Mayor Bell, Council Member Eddie Davis, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden praised the Northeast Central Durham corridor investment.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Authorizing a Public Art Project on the NC 147 Retaining Wall on the South Side of Willard Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from the consent agenda for public comment, the resolution authorized a mural on the NC 147 retaining wall along the south side of Willard Street. Visual artist and teacher Mark Iwinski spoke in favor of the mural, arguing that newspaper coverage framing it around the Durham Bulls sold the optical-art design short and praising the project for bringing dynamic color to drab concrete.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Consent Agenda (Items 1-5, excluding pulled Item 7)
votes.notes: Item 7 was pulled by Mayor Bell prior to the consent vote because a member of the public signed up to speak.
votes.discussion_detail: Council Member Don Moffitt earlier welcomed a visiting Duke University ethics class and noted that most agenda items had been reviewed at the prior work session. After the City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk reported no priority items, Mayor Bell read the headings for Items 1 through 5, covering minutes, the University Drive bicycle and pedestrian grant agreement (EB-5514), a roundabout sidewalk agreement, the December 2014 bid report, and a city lease at 700 N. Alston Avenue with Yarborough and Hesse Warehouses LLC. Mayor Bell pulled Item 7 for public comment, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved adoption of the remaining consent items with Council Member Eugene Brown seconding, passing unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with A&J Capital Corporation for 406 S. Driver Street (Ashley Corners)
votes.notes: Up to $170,000 city grant disbursed only upon project completion; total project cost $525,336.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff presenter Chris Dickey explained that the $170,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant leverages approximately $355,000 in private investment to eliminate an unsafe building hazard cited in September 2013 and create four commercial bays plus two second-floor apartments at 406 South Driver Street. In response to Council Member Steve Schewel's questions, Dickey confirmed staff independently vetted the developer's pro forma with a local bank and noted funds are only disbursed after completion, though the two second-floor units carried no binding long-term affordability covenant because the program focuses on commercial revitalization. Schewel urged staff to consider requiring affordability guarantees in future mixed-use subsidy deals when developers advertise affordable units. Mayor Bell praised the corridor investment and commented on undergrounding/mast-arm traffic signal aesthetics, Council Member Eddie Davis highlighted its proximity to the Mayor's Poverty Reduction Initiative census tract, and Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden congratulated local developer Attorney Rogers before the public hearing closed with no public speakers and the agreement passed 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden in Mayor Bill Bell's excused absence (with five members present at roll call and Eugene Brown en route), the January 22, 2015 Work Session focused primarily on environmental testing and purchase negotiations for the Carpenter site designated for the new Police Headquarters Complex. Council unanimously voted 5-0 by voice vote to accept the City Manager's priority item (Item 6, an amendment with TerraCon Consultants, Inc.) and unanimously approved 5-0 the City Attorney's two closed session items including Developer Surety v. City of Durham. During open discussion of Item 6, TerraCon consultant Lori Denton and seller's attorney Richard Prentis (representing GWC Properties) addressed an estimated $250,000 worst-case soil remediation figure and an option deadline expiring the next day, while council members also reviewed Item 7 (an NC 147 retaining wall public art proposal that one member cautioned resembled an advertisement for the Durham Bulls) and Item 8 (an economic development incentive with NJ Capital Corporation). Council then voted unanimously 5-0 to enter closed session to address the Police Headquarters real estate negotiations and attorney consultation items.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: TerraCon Consultants Contract Amendment (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested pulling Item 6 (amendment to contract with TerraCon Consultants, Inc. for additional investigation and testing services for the Police Headquarters Complex project) for questions and suspending the rules to vote on it that day. Council voted 5-0 by voice vote to accept the priority item.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Closed Session Items (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney presented two closed session items under attorney-client consultation, including Developer Surety vs. City of Durham (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)). Council approved the items by a 5-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Administrative Consent Item 5 ($2,600/Year Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member pulled Item 5 for clarification on contract payment figures in the memo, confirming the amount was $2,600 per year for four years plus escalation (and referencing $600/month times 12).

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comment: Dolores Bynum on Unmaintained Street and Trash Service
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Dolores Bynum, nearly 70 years old and operating a small home daycare, told Council that because her street is not city-maintained she must roll her garbage cart roughly 100 feet to the end of the street despite paying city taxes.

agenda_items.title: Police Headquarters Complex (Carpenter Site) Environmental Testing and Escrow
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff, TerraCon consultant Lori Denton, and seller's attorney Richard Prentis (representing GWC Properties / Carpenter family) reviewed preliminary soil testing at the Carpenter site, including an escrow agreement for remediation and a conservative ~$250,000 worst-case estimate assuming all potential spots are contaminated and require DENR closure. Council questioned what assurance the amended testing contract would provide and decided to examine negotiation options in closed session given the purchase option expiring the next day.

agenda_items.title: NC 147 Retaining Wall Public Art Project Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that OEWD, Transportation, NCDOT, and American Tobacco presented the NC 147 retaining wall public art project to the Public Art Committee and Cultural Advisory Board, both of which recommended approval with public engagement prior to final design. A council member expressed concern that the artwork appeared to function as an advertisement for the Durham Bulls rather than an appropriate public art use.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with NJ Capital Corporation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD staff answered a council member's question regarding language indicating that lender Premier Solutions had not yet committed project funds, confirming the city's incentive payment would only occur on the back end.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Police Headquarters Negotiations and Attorney Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council agreed to take up the Police Headquarters Carpenter site real estate negotiation first in closed session before handling the remaining attorney items, and voted 5-0 by voice vote to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Item (Item 6: TerraCon Consultants Contract Amendment)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote among the five members present (Mayor Bill Bell had an excused absence; Council Member Eugene Brown was noted as en route at roll call).
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager requested accepting Item 6 as a priority item for discussion and potential rule suspension to vote the same day.

votes.item_title: Approve City Attorney's Closed Session Items (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote with no opposition among the five members present at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: City Attorney presented two attorney-client consultation items, including Developer Surety vs. City of Durham.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session (Police Headquarters Carpenter Site Negotiations and Attorney Items)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; the recorded open session ended as Council convened closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Council moved into closed session to discuss the Carpenter site Police Headquarters purchase option expiring the next day along with the City Attorney's items.

meetings.title: Durham City Council January 20, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: In a brief 21-minute business session, the Durham City Council recognized the Durham Convention Center and Global Spectrum for winning ConventionSouth Magazine's 2014 Readers' Choice Award and proclaimed January 20, 2015 as Dr. Brian Lamont Johnson Day to honor the Durham native's appointment as president of Tuskegee University. Following a legal authority clarification from the City Attorney regarding no-build easements at 505 Rigsbee Avenue, the council unanimously approved all 10 consent agenda items and granted an excused absence for the upcoming Thursday work session.

agenda_items.title: ConventionSouth 2014 Readers' Choice Award Recognition for Durham Convention Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell announced that the Durham Convention Center, managed by Global Spectrum, received ConventionSouth Magazine's 2014 Readers' Choice Award for Best Meeting Sites in the South, selected from over 175 nominated venues. Convention Center Authority Chair Patrick Byker and General Manager Jen Noble thanked the council, city and county staff, and authority board members for supporting operations and extending Global Spectrum's management contract through 2019.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation Honoring Dr. Brian Lamont Johnson Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden and Mayor Bell proclaimed January 20, 2015 as Dr. Brian Lamont Johnson Day in Durham, celebrating the Few Gardens and Durham High School alumnus's selection as the seventh president of Tuskegee University. Dr. Johnson's mother, Gwendolyn Johnson, and executive assistant Vernon Little offered remarks thanking the community and council, and Cole-McFadden praised local MLK Day commemorations and community volunteerism.

agenda_items.title: Legal Authority Clarification for Item 6 (No-Build Easements at 505 Rigsbee Avenue)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney noted for the record that additional legal authority for the proposed sale of no-build easements at 505 Rigsbee Avenue (Item 6) comes from Section 86 of the Durham City Charter. He advised council that his office was working with the developer to finalize the document in line with work session discussions, requiring no separate action.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Transit Bus Procurement, DATA Title VI Update, Water/Sewer Contracts, 505 Rigsbee Easements, EPA Brownfields, MS4 Inspections, Kronos, Kramden Institute)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the headings of the 10 consent agenda items covering regional transit bus procurement with Triangle Transit and Chapel Hill, DATA's 2014 Title VI update, North Durham Water Reclamation Facility generator and waterline contracts, sewer lift station and outfall repairs, no-build easements at 505 Rigsbee Avenue for Liberty Warehouse Apartments LLC, an EPA Brownfields grant contract, MS4 stormwater inspections, a Kronos software agreement, and a computer donation agreement with Kramden Institute. No items were pulled by council or the public.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request for Upcoming Thursday Work Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Immediately prior to adjournment, a council member requested an excused absence for the upcoming Thursday work session. The council approved the request without debate.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Thursday City Council Work Session
votes.notes: Requested for the upcoming Thursday work session just prior to 7:22 p.m. adjournment.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after the consent agenda passed, a council member requested an excused absence for the upcoming Thursday work session before adjournment. No discussion or objection was raised by any member of the council. The motion was seconded and approved unanimously 7-0, after which Mayor Bell adjourned the meeting at 7:22 p.m.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Legislative Breakfast
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 16, 2015 Special City Council Legislative Breakfast with the Durham state legislative delegation, Senior Assistant to the City Manager Karmisha Wallace and city representatives reviewed Durham's 2015 legislative agenda adopted on January 5 ahead of the North Carolina General Assembly long session. Key city priorities included two charter-amendment local bills on voluntary annexation—allowing initial zoning public hearings prior to annexation ordinance adoption and granting discretionary authority to annex adjacent streets and rights-of-way—as well as addressing the $2.9 million FY 2015-16 budget shortfall from the repeal of municipal privilege licenses and potential compounding losses from sales tax redistribution. Council and legislators also discussed restoring full Justice Reinvestment Act funding, granting state authority for revenue-neutral speed cameras near parks, schools, and hospitals following an Inter-Neighborhood Council resolution, and reviving SB 78 to shield law enforcement officers' home addresses from public property and tax websites. No formal council votes were taken during the informational legislative breakfast.

agenda_items.title: Voluntary Annexation Local Bill Requests (Zoning Hearings and Adjacent Rights-of-Way)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Karmisha Wallace presented two Planning Department local bill requests from the January 5 legislative agenda: authorizing the city to give notice and hold initial zoning public hearings for voluntary annexation properties prior to annexation ordinance passage (reviving concepts from 2013 HB 541), and granting discretionary authority to annex adjacent streets and street rights-of-way alongside voluntary annexations to prevent fragmented emergency service and NCDOT/county maintenance jurisdictions.

agenda_items.title: Privilege License Repeal ($2.9M Budget Gap) and Sales Tax Redistribution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City leadership and legislators discussed the impact of losing $2.9 million in privilege license revenue—which Durham and North Carolina's five largest cities zeroed out in FY 2015-16 budget planning—and warned that proposed state sales tax reallocation would compound the gap. Officials noted that without an equitable replacement methodology for privilege license fees, cities face pressure to raise property taxes to fund basic operations and public safety.

agenda_items.title: County Requests and Justice Reinvestment Act Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Participants briefly discussed County requests and urged full funding of the Justice Reinvestment Act so state savings from reduced Department of Corrections prison populations (down from roughly 41,000-42,000 to 38,000) are reinvested into local community programs as originally intended.

agenda_items.title: Inter-Neighborhood Council Traffic Safety Resolution and Speed Cameras
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Philip Azar presented requests from an Inter-Neighborhood Council resolution seeking state authority to operate speed cameras in sensitive zones—parks, schools, and hospitals—on a revenue-neutral safety basis without deploying police officers. Delegation members asked about signage, pedestrian crossings, bicycle issues, and model legislation such as school bus stop-arm cameras.

agenda_items.title: Law Enforcement Officer Home Address Privacy (SB 78)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ms. Fountain urged council members and state legislators to revive SB 78—which passed the House unanimously in 2013 before stalling in the Senate Rules Committee and NC Courts Commission—to remove law enforcement officers' and non-elected officials' home addresses from public tax and property websites. Legislators discussed the bill's procedural history and agreed to follow up in a delegation meeting.

agenda_items.title: MLK Service Announcement and State Preemption Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After an informational question on the 6:00 PM Martin Luther King Jr. service, a council member highlighted an NPR report on Texas Governor Greg Abbott and state preemption of local ordinances (citing Denton, Texas) as a cautionary parallel to challenges facing North Carolina cities before the meeting adjourned.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 8, 2015 Durham City Council Work Session, Council observed a moment of silence for victims of the Paris assassinations and unanimously voted 7-0 across four voice votes to accept the City Manager's priority items (Items 7 and 15), suspend the rules for Item 7, adopt Item 7 (the City of Durham Employment and Training 2014-2016 Grant Project Ordinance superseding Ordinance 14632), and set the upcoming regular meeting agenda with consent items 1-6 and 8-11. Council members praised staff for strengthening MWBE participation on the North Durham Water Reclamation Facility generator improvements (Item 3), reviewed the DATA 2014 Title VI program update (Item 2) while requesting interim follow-up on bus shelters and ridership trends, and examined a software licensing contract (Item 10) being rolled out to Fire and Parks and Recreation alongside a Fire diversity recruitment initiative. A public speaker criticized Police Chief Jose Lopez for failing to return calls from residents seeking dialogue on police violence and recounted police inaction during a protest incident involving a transfer truck at Southpoint Mall. Council also questioned the City Attorney on a proposed Durham Central Park easement for East West Partners to safeguard continued city access to the Liberty Arts Foundry casting facility and ensure binding sidewalk commitments.

agenda_items.title: Moment of Silence, Joint Committee Reminder, and City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a moment of silence for victims of the Paris assassinations, and the City Manager reminded members about parking relocation and the upcoming Tuesday Joint City-County Committee meeting on the Joint Economic Development Strategic Plan and TTA light rail alignment. Council voted 7-0 to accept the City Manager's priority items (Item 7 for rule suspension and same-day vote, and noting Item 15 citizen Katina Parker would not attend).

agenda_items.title: Transportation and Water Management Consent Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed Item 1 (interlocal agreement with Research Triangle Regional Public Transportation Authority and Town of Chapel Hill for procurement of buses, equipment, and parts), Item 2 (DATA 2014 Title VI update, pulled for discussion), Item 3 (North Durham Water Reclamation Facility generator improvements, with a council member commending staff for improving MWBE participation with the contractor), and Item 4 (contracts for Hope Valley/Keystone lift station abandonment and West Street sewer outfall repair).

agenda_items.title: City of Durham Employment and Training 2014-2016 Grant Project Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the City Manager's priority request for the Office of Economic and Workforce Development grant project ordinance superseding Grant Project Ordinance 14632, Council voted 7-0 to suspend the rules and then voted 7-0 to approve Item 7.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items: EPA Brownfield Grant, MS4 Inspections, and Software Licensing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Item 8 (contract with Mid-Atlantic Resources Inc. for implementation of an EPA Brownfield assessment grant), Item 9 (Public Works MS4 inspections), and Item 10 (Technology Solutions Department software license and services agreement) for questions.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Police Chief Responsiveness and Southpoint Mall Protest Incident
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A resident stated that Police Chief Jose Lopez had publicly expressed willingness to meet with concerned residents about police violence and protest responses, yet had not returned calls or messages since mid-November. The speaker also described witnessing a white transfer truck driver driving into protesters blocking a street near Southpoint Mall while police stood by without intervening.

agenda_items.title: DATA 2014 Title VI Program Update and Transit Performance Standards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member reviewed the Title VI service standards PowerPoint, noting data only ran through February 2014 and that daily boardings appeared slightly down from FY13 to FY14, and requested updates on cost recovery ratios and bus shelter/bench amenities. Staff indicated most performance measures are covered in budget workshops and offered to provide an interim follow-up report on bus shelter status.

agenda_items.title: Durham Central Park Easement Request by East West Partners and Liberty Arts Access
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member raised three concerns with the City Attorney regarding selling an easement on portions of Durham Central Park to East West Partners: ensuring the city preserves full rights to use and lease the Liberty Arts Foundry casting facility, clarifying a vertical line in the site drawing so no park re-grading occurs, and confirming East West Partners' sidewalk and park commitments are tied to certificates of occupancy regardless of future ownership. The City Attorney agreed to verify the existing party wall agreement and add protective language into the easement agreement if needed.

agenda_items.title: Software Licensing Rollout and Fire Department Diversity Recruitment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that the software system is rolling out initially in Fire—supporting a diversity initiative to broaden applicant recruitment—and Parks and Recreation, and clarified that future expansion to Police or Public Works would scale through per-user licensing and department training costs.

agenda_items.title: Set Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-6, 8-11; Disposal of Items 7, 12-15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 by voice vote to set consent items 1 through 6 and 8 through 11 for the regular meeting, with item 7 and items 12 through 15 disposed of.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items (Agenda Items 7 and 15)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the City Manager's priority items adding Item 7 for rule suspension and immediate vote and noting the absence of speaker Katina Parker for Item 15.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Vote on Item 7 (Employment and Training Grant Project Ordinance)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend council rules to take immediate action on the Office of Economic and Workforce Development grant project ordinance during the work session.

votes.item_title: Adopt Item 7: City of Durham Employment and Training 2014-2016 Grant Project Ordinance
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote immediately following rule suspension.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the Employment and Training 2014-2016 Grant Project Ordinance superseding Grant Project Ordinance 14632.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda (Consent Items 1-6 and 8-11; Disposal of Items 7 and 12-15)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set consent agenda items 1-6 and 8-11 and marked items 7 and 12-15 as disposed.

meetings.title: Durham City Council January 5, 2015
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council approved its consent agenda—including a resolution welcoming unaccompanied migrant children—and referred the Auto Park Center rezoning (Z1400011) back to staff, but split sharply over two major policy items. On a 3-4 vote, the council rejected adding the Durham County Sheriff's proposal to elevate stolen firearm offenses and impose a 72-month mandatory minimum to its 2015 legislative agenda before approving the remaining legislative package 6-0. After an extensive public hearing featuring residents from Parkwood, Eno Trace, and Green Street, council voted 5-1 (Council Member Eugene Brown dissenting) to rescind 11 previously ordered $5-per-foot petition sidewalk projects while pledging to revisit sidewalk funding in the budget process.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations for Dr. John Hope Franklin Centennial, Justice Sunday 2015, and National Mentoring Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented three proclamations honoring Dr. John Hope Franklin's centennial birthday, proclaiming January 18, 2015 as Justice Sunday (accepted by NCCU Professor Dr. John B. Wilson), and recognizing January 2015 as National Mentoring Month (accepted by Durham County Juvenile Crime Prevention Council Vice Chair DeWarren Langley and Thomas Leadership Mentoring Academy President Larry Thomas). Council Member Steve Schewel also recognized community members present in support of the consent-agenda resolution welcoming unaccompanied migrant children, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden received an excused absence to depart early for a citywide revival.

agenda_items.title: Referral of Zoning Map Change Auto Park Center (Z1400011) Back to Administration / Planning Department
agenda_items.discussion_summary: As a City Manager priority item, the manager reported that the applicant's attorney and design consultant for Auto Park Center (Z1400011) requested late that afternoon to refer the item back to the City-County Planning Department to address a site plan issue. Council referred the rezoning case back to administration for consideration at a later date.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Unaccompanied Migrant Children Resolution, Expedited Rezoning Z1400034, EV Charger License, Avondale Sidewalk, Street/DOT & Property Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved all remaining consent agenda items in a single vote, including board appointments to the Firefighters' Relief Fund, RDU Airport Authority, and Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission, a resolution welcoming unaccompanied migrant children in Durham, an expedited hearing request for Southside East Phases 2 and 3 (Z1400034), a BrightField DC fast charger license in Parking Lot 32, Avondale Drive sidewalk construction, street acceptances, and several NCDOT and facility contracts.

agenda_items.title: 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda and Sheriff's Stolen Firearms Penalty Enhancement Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Assistant to the City Manager Karmisha Wallace presented the 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda, highlighting a separate request from the Durham County Sheriff to elevate larceny, sale, or receipt of stolen firearms from Class H to Class E felony and impose a 72-month mandatory minimum when another felony is committed with a stolen firearm. Criminal justice advocates opposed the enhancement as disruptive to NC's sentencing structure and ineffective, while the Sheriff and his legal advisor urged action amid rising gun violence and break-ins; council split 3-4 against including the Sheriff's item and then adopted the rest of the legislative agenda 6-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Sheriff proposal failed 3-4; Remainder of legislative agenda passed 6-0

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Resolution to Rescind 11 Previously Ordered Petition Sidewalks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams presented a resolution to rescind 11 previously ordered $5-per-front-foot petition sidewalk projects so council could transition to updated assessment rates ($35/foot for projects in the Durham Walks plan or full construction cost outside it). Residents from Parkwood, Eno Trace, and Green Street spoke about pedestrian hazards, flawed consultant scoring, and underfunded sidewalk budgets, while one Green Street homeowner favored rescission; council passed the rescission 5-1 with Council Member Eugene Brown opposed.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence Request for Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden
votes.notes: Cole-McFadden remained through the 3-4 legislative agenda vote on the Sheriff's proposal before departing for Union Baptist Church.
votes.discussion_detail: During council announcements, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden congratulated the Durham Ministerial Alliance on its Emancipation Proclamation service and citywide revival beginning that evening at Union Baptist Church. Explaining her desire to join the city's spiritual leaders in corporate prayer, she requested an excused absence to leave the meeting around 7:45 p.m. Council Member Eddie Davis moved to grant the excused absence, Council Member Diane Catotti seconded, and the motion passed 7-0 (though Cole-McFadden later stayed through the Sheriff's legislative proposal vote before departing).

votes.item_title: Refer Zoning Map Change Auto Park Center (Z1400011) Back to Administration / City-County Planning Department
votes.notes: City Manager priority item; applicant's attorney and design consultant requested referral to address a site plan issue.
votes.discussion_detail: During priority items, the City Manager informed council that the applicant's attorney and design consultant for Item 23, Zoning Map Change Auto Park Center (Z1400011), contacted the city late that afternoon requesting that the case be referred back to the City-County Planning Department to address a site plan issue. No members of council objected or requested discussion on the deferral. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved the referral, Council Member Don Moffitt seconded (with Diane Catotti also initially referenced), and the motion passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Include Durham County Sheriff's Stolen Firearms Felony Enhancement Proposal in 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda
votes.notes: Electronic board tally announced as 3 yeses and 4 noes without clerk reading every individual member name aloud; Cole-McFadden (mover), Brown (seconder, confirmed Yes), and Bell spoke in support, while Schewel, Moffitt, and Davis argued against and Catotti formed the fourth Nay.
votes.discussion_detail: Senior Assistant to the City Manager Karmisha Wallace explained that the Sheriff requested council support—without requiring city lobbying—to elevate larceny, sale, or receipt of stolen firearms from a Class H to a Class E felony and establish a 72-month mandatory minimum sentence for felonies committed with a stolen firearm. Public speakers Leo Rupert (Carolina Justice Policy Center), Marcia Owen (Religious Coalition for a Nonviolent Durham), and Prof. George Wilson (NCCU) opposed the proposal as counterproductive, arguing it equates property theft with violent crimes against persons, imposes ~$175,000 incarceration costs per sentence without deterrence evidence, and worsens mass incarceration compared to safe-storage education or gun legislation. Sheriff Mike Andrews and legal advisor Curtis Massey arrived mid-debate to argue that rising residential break-ins (30-40% increase, including stolen gun safes) and street gun violence justify Class E classification alongside other hazard offenses, with Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden, and Council Member Brown voicing support for sending a strong anti-violence message. However, Council Members Steve Schewel, Don Moffitt, and Eddie Davis criticized the lack of consultation with the NC Sentencing Commission, the absence of crime-reduction projections, and the removal of judicial discretion through a six-year mandatory minimum, and Schewel requested an up-or-down vote on isolating the Sheriff's request, which failed 3-4.

votes.item_title: Adopt 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda (Excluding Sheriff's Stolen Firearms Proposal)
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden departed under her previously approved excused absence immediately after the 3-4 vote on the Sheriff's proposal, leaving six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after the council voted 3-4 against adding the Sheriff's stolen firearms proposal to the legislative package, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden departed for the Union Baptist Church revival under her previously granted excused absence. Council Member Steve Schewel thanked the Sheriff for his daily public safety work, and Mayor Bell was about to move to Item 22 when a council member noted they still needed to vote on the underlying 2015 Long Session Legislative Agenda itself. A motion to adopt the remainder of the legislative agenda was made, seconded, and approved unanimously 6-0 by the remaining members.

votes.item_title: Resolution Rescinding 11 Previously Ordered Petition Sidewalk Projects (Item 22)
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden was absent (excused); Council Member Eugene Brown voted No. Clarified post-vote that council adopted the base rescission recommendation without yet selecting any of staff's follow-up budget alternatives.
votes.discussion_detail: Public Works Director Marvin Williams presented the proposal to rescind 11 previously ordered $5-per-front-foot sidewalk petitions so council could clear an unfunded backlog and require new petitions to pay $35 per foot (for projects in the Durham Walks plan) or full construction cost (~$55 per foot) outside it. During the public hearing, Parkwood Association President Bill Mitchell (citing Grandale and Sedgwick Road safety and disputed consultant scoring), Eno Trace residents Wallace Lam and Jesse Vassel (describing blind hills and Lam's broken arm from walking without sidewalks), and Green Street petition owner Maria Pajowski (arguing the $200,000 sidewalk budget versus $14 million in needs was a false choice) urged council not to rescind, while Green Street resident Ron De Silva supported rescission over tree and privacy impacts. Council Member Diane Catotti moved rescission to prioritize scarce funds via the Durham Walks plan, backed by Steve Schewel and Don Moffitt (who entered an opposing email from Deidre Murphy on University Drive into the record while noting it was misleading to keep 7-to-8-year-old unfunded petitions on the books). Council Member Eugene Brown cast the sole dissent in the 5-1 vote, faulting consultant scoring that gave zero points to Parkwood's HOA park and arguing Durham must better fund neighborhood sidewalk connectivity.

disagreements.issue: Inclusion of Sheriff's Stolen Firearms Felony Elevation and 72-Month Mandatory Minimum in 2015 Legislative Agenda
disagreements.summary: Council divided 3-4 over whether to endorse the Durham County Sheriff's proposal asking the General Assembly to elevate stolen firearm offenses from Class H to Class E felony and impose a mandatory 72-month minimum prison term when a stolen firearm is used in another felony.
disagreements.side_a_position: Endorse the Sheriff's stolen firearm penalty enhancement in the city's 2015 legislative package to deter gun thefts and violence.
side_a_arguments: Stolen firearms and residential burglaries (up 30-40%, including stolen gun safes) feed street-level gun violence, aggravated assaults, and homicides in Durham.
Stealing a firearm is an intentional act whose purpose is typically resale or criminal use, warranting tougher Class E felony status and incapacitation.
Supporting the Sheriff sends a clear community message that gun violence is intolerable.
disagreements.side_b_position: Decline to add the Sheriff's sentencing enhancement to the city's legislative agenda.
side_b_arguments: Elevating property theft of a firearm to Class E disrupts North Carolina's structured sentencing grid by equating theft with violent crimes against persons.
A mandatory 72-month minimum eliminates judicial discretion contrary to national sentencing reform trends and carries high incarceration costs without evidence of deterrence.
The Sheriff had not consulted the NC Sentencing Commission, lacked crime-reduction projections, and existing 2013 firearm sentencing enhancements have not yet been evaluated.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to add the Sheriff's proposal to the legislative agenda failed 3-4; the remaining 2015 legislative agenda was then approved 6-0.

disagreements.issue: Rescission of 11 Previously Ordered $5/Foot Petition Sidewalk Projects
disagreements.summary: Following resident testimony over pedestrian safety and consultant scoring fairness, council split 5-1 on rescinding 11 older petition sidewalk orders to transition toward the Durham Walks prioritization framework and higher $35/foot petitioner assessments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Rescind the 11 older petition orders now and revisit sidewalk funding and prioritization alternatives during the upcoming budget process.
side_a_arguments: Leaving petitions approved 7-8 years ago on the active list when they lack funding is misleading to residents.
Very limited sidewalk funds should be directed through the Durham Walks priority plan to maximize safety, school proximity, and overall connectivity.
Five of the 11 corridors remain in the Durham Walks plan and can be re-petitioned at $35/foot alongside future budget discussions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose rescinding the previously ordered neighborhood petition sidewalks.
side_b_arguments: Consultant scoring criteria unfairly penalized neighborhood projects such as Sedgwick Road in Parkwood because the adjacent park is HOA-owned rather than city-owned and the route connects to an existing school sidewalk rather than fronting the school directly.
Durham is already 'sidewalk poor' and should prioritize intra-neighborhood connectivity and citizen volunteer efforts rather than canceling approved projects.
disagreements.resolution: Resolution rescinding the 11 petition sidewalk projects passed 5-1 (Cole-McFadden excused absent), with staff directed to bring sidewalk funding and Durham Walks options back during the FY2015-16 budget process.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 18, 2014 Durham City Council Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell presided over a session with no split or contested votes, in which Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (requesting rule suspension and immediate action on $60.5 million in Series 2015 General Obligation Refunding Bonds, a New Durham Corporation installment purchase contract amendment, and the East Durham Recreation Center lease and services contract with the East Durham Children's Initiative) and unanimously backed the City Attorney's priority recommendation for Durham to join a U.S. Supreme Court amicus brief supporting the Fair Housing Act. Council reviewed the consent and public hearing agenda, including a slightly revised resolution concerning unaccompanied migrant children in Durham presented by Council Member Steve Schewel, and heard citizen comments on unpaved Briggs Avenue, local veterans' service needs, Northern High School pedestrian safety, and recent street protests. Public Works staff presented Pavement Condition Study findings contrasting arterial (PCI 75) and residential street maintenance scenarios under $1 million and $2 million annual budgets, with members emphasizing road maintenance as a top resident priority. Following unanimous agenda-setting by voice vote, Mayor Bell and the City Attorney clarified that Durham had not banned nighttime protests, reviewed police coordination during highway and jail demonstrations, and addressed misstatements aired on a recent radio broadcast.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:04 p.m. and apologized for a brief delay; the clerk called roll with Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel answering (Eddie Davis was called with no response recorded in the digest). The City Manager presented three priority items requesting rule suspension and same-day votes (Items 12, 13, and 16), and the City Attorney presented a memorandum recommending Durham join a U.S. Supreme Court amicus brief supporting the Fair Housing Act without expending city resources; both sets of priority items passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review: Appointments, Unaccompanied Migrant Children Resolution, Bonds, Contracts, and Public Hearings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent and departmental items including minutes, Firefighters' Relief Fund Board of Trustees, Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority, and Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission appointments, street and infrastructure acceptances, and Council Member Steve Schewel's slightly revised resolution concerning unaccompanied migrant children in Durham (Item 6). Members also reviewed the November 2014 bid report, $60.5 million GO refunding bonds (Item 12), the New Durham Corporation amendment (Item 13), a masonry change order at 400 Cleveland Street (Item 14), property management at 616 East Main Street (Item 15), and upcoming public hearings on rescinding 11 petition sidewalks (Item 22) and the Auto Park Center rezoning (Item 23).

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: Briggs Avenue Paving, Veterans Support, Northern High Pedestrian Safety, and Protests
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under Citizens' Matters, Dave Rush (Item 24) urged Council to address poor road conditions on Briggs Avenue between Angier Avenue and Pettigrew/Katie Street affecting a business and nearby residences. Subsequent speakers highlighted growing demand for local veterans' services in Durham and funding needs to hire staff, Northern High School student Odessa Wingian presented survey findings that 50 percent of surveyed students avoid walking due to poor road conditions and cited recent pedestrian and bicycle crashes, and another speaker offered comments regarding recent protests.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Resolution Concerning Unaccompanied Migrant Children in Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel introduced the slightly revised resolution concerning unaccompanied migrant children in Durham before the middle portion of the transcript digest was truncated.

agenda_items.title: Item 21: Pavement Condition Study Findings Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented follow-up Pavement Condition Study scenarios separating arterial streets (targeted at PCI 75) from local residential streets (modeled at PCI 65 versus PCI 55) under $1 million and $2 million annual resurfacing budgets. Council members emphasized that residents ranked good roads as their top survey priority, noted strong public support for street resurfacing bonds, expressed concern that a PCI 55 target for residential streets was inadequate, and requested smoothed multi-year budget projections showing a $2 million baseline plus potential half-cent tax equivalent funding.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Agenda for the Next City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager outlined the upcoming Council meeting agenda: consent items 1–7, 9–11, 14–15, and 17–20; General Business Agenda (GBA) item 8; GBA public hearings 22 and 23; and disposed items 12, 13, 16, 20, 21, and 24–28. Council approved the agenda by voice vote without opposition.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Street Protests, Parade Permit Rules, and Plaza Signage
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell and the City Attorney addressed public emails and a recent radio interview with a UNC law professor regarding Durham's protest and parade policies. The City Attorney clarified that Council had merely restated existing state law in January, that no ordinance or state law bans nighttime protests, and that no one had applied for a nighttime parade permit; staff also discussed Sheriff's Office and Highway Patrol coordination during recent protests at the jail and near Southpoint and considered temporary, removable signage rather than permanent signs at CCB Plaza before adjourning at 3:15 p.m.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items (Items 12, 13, and 16)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('Motion passes unanimously'). Mover and seconder were not identified by name in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager requested rule suspension and same-day votes on $60.5M Series 2015 GO Refunding Bonds (Item 12), the New Durham Corporation installment purchase contract amendment (Item 13), and the East Durham Recreation Center lease and services contract with the East Durham Children's Initiative (Item 16).

votes.item_title: Accept City Attorney's Priority Item (Fair Housing Act Supreme Court Amicus Brief)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('Motion passes unanimously'). Mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Attorney sought Council authorization for Durham to sign onto a U.S. Supreme Court amicus brief supporting the Fair Housing Act at no resource cost to the city.

votes.item_title: Set Regular City Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote with no opposition ('all in favor of motion indicate by saying aye... those opposed, the motion passes'). Mover and seconder were not named.
votes.discussion_detail: Set consent items 1–7, 9–11, 14–15, and 17–20; GBA item 8; GBA public hearings 22 and 23; and noted disposed items 12, 13, 16, 20, 21, and 24–28.
