meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 23, 2014 Durham City Council Work Session, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided (with Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Steve Schewel absent on excused absences and Council Member Eugene Brown arriving after the opening) and Council acted unanimously on all votes—with no split or contested votes—to suspend the rules and adopt Item 15 (a 2014–2017 U.S. EPA Environmental Workforce Development and Job Training grant project ordinance) and set the November regular meeting agenda. Cole-McFadden opened by reporting on a domestic violence summit and proposing to reform the city's Domestic Violence Task Force, and members later raised concerns about local domestic violence shelter capacity turning away victims. Council received a Liberty Arts update regarding a downtown sculpture donation and developer site discussions, heard the Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau's State of Durham presentation highlighting a 19-to-1 positive resident self-image ratio, and closely questioned Water Management Director Don Greeley over engineering firm CDM Smith's Durham Central Park waterline contract (Items 7–8). Although Greeley noted CDM Smith's combined design-and-construction MWBE participation would reach roughly 18 percent across an estimated $12 million project, Council members criticized CDM Smith's persistent 3–4 percent African American workforce representation in Raleigh and requested company representatives appear before Council on Monday.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Domestic Violence Task Force Proposal, and Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the work session with Mayor Bell and Council Member Steve Schewel absent and Council Member Eugene Brown en route. Cole-McFadden discussed attending a domestic violence summit and wanting to talk with the Mayor about reviving Durham's Domestic Violence Task Force, while the City Manager presented Item 15 (EPA Environmental Workforce Development and Job Training 2014–2017 grant) for rule suspension once a supermajority arrived and Council pulled Items 7, 9, and 12.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters and Liberty Arts Sculpture Donation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Tarantino spoke during Citizens' Matters, followed by a presentation on Liberty Arts' donation of the Bull City Sculpture Show Purchase Award sculpture. City staff reported ongoing discussions with a downtown developer and Liberty Arts board members regarding placement and continued access to casting facilities.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau State of Durham Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DCVB presented regional perception research showing Durham achieved a 19-to-1 positive-to-negative image ratio among residents (reversing a 4-to-1 negative ratio in 1992) compared to Wake County's 3-to-1 ratio, alongside a 100,000-subscriber permission marketing database and 400-respondent polling methodology.

agenda_items.title: Item 15: EPA Environmental Workforce Development and Job Training Grant Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Council Member Eugene Brown's arrival to provide the required vote threshold, Council unanimously suspended the rules and unanimously adopted Item 15, the U.S. EPA Environmental Workforce Development and Job Training 2014–2017 grant project ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Domestic Violence Shelter Capacity and Item 7: Transit Bonus Points
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden noted domestic violence conference reports on the number of victims turned away due to limited shelter funding and capacity. Council also thanked staff for adding four transit-proximity bonus points to an item and asked for redlined tracked changes on future revised reports.

agenda_items.title: Items 8 & 9: CDM Smith Waterline Contract Diversity and Jordan Lake Partnership Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley explained that CDM Smith's Phase 1 design contract ($1.3M–$1.6M within a ~$12M total waterline project) would reach roughly 18 percent MWBE participation once construction-inspection subcontractors are added by amendment. Council members voiced strong dissatisfaction with CDM Smith's persistent 3–4 percent African American workforce rate in Raleigh—contrasting it with Kimley-Horn's diversity plan—and requested CDM Smith representatives attend the next Council meeting; members also discussed an APA-NC partnership award won with the Jordan Lake Partnership.

agenda_items.title: Financial/Facility Questions and Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council questioned installment-sales language for lighting, verified a minor 200–300 sq. ft. legal/party question, and flagged a typo in an automated controls memo covering 37 city facilities. At 2:10 p.m., Council unanimously approved the next Council meeting agenda (consent items 1–14 and GBA public hearings 17–20) before adjourning at 2:11 p.m.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Consider Item 15 (EPA Workforce Development Grant)
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote without opposition. Mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Council rules once Council Member Eugene Brown arrived to achieve the required threshold.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 15 (U.S. EPA Environmental Workforce Development and Job Training 2014–2017 Grant Project Ordinance)
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote without opposition. Mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the 2014–2017 EPA Environmental Workforce Development and Job Training grant project ordinance.

votes.item_title: Set Regular City Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote without opposition. Mover and seconder were not identified by name.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting October 20, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council unanimously adopted the Downtown Open Space Plan after extensive public support and approved a Neighborhood Stabilization Program 3 grant project ordinance for Southside infrastructure. In a 6-1 vote with Council Member Eugene Brown dissenting, the Council approved the $5.69 million acquisition of East Main Street, Elizabeth Street, Ramsey Street, and Hood Street properties for a new police headquarters and 911 communications complex despite concerns over cost, demolition of historic buildings, and urban design. The Council also approved the consent agenda and a pulled FY 2015 regional transportation modeling agreement with North Carolina State University.

agenda_items.title: Championship Proclamations and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented proclamations recognizing the 2014 NCAA national champion Duke University men's lacrosse and women's golf teams as well as the NCCU men's tennis HBCU national championship team. Council Member Diane Catotti also congratulated Durham dance pioneer Chuck Davis on receiving a Bessie Award in New York.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items (Supplemental Items 20 and 21)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield introduced two supplemental items for addition to the evening's agenda: Item 20 regarding property acquisition for the proposed police headquarters on East Main Street and Item 21 for the Neighborhood Stabilization Program 3 grant project ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the headings of the consent agenda, covering minutes, a Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission appointment, FY14 carryover and FY15 budget/grant ordinances, CDBG contracts with Interfaith Hospitality Network and Urban Ministries of Durham, the City-County 911 interlocal agreement, and a stormwater repair contract amendment. Item 7 was pulled for separate discussion.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Open Space Plan Public Hearing and Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tom Dawson of the Planning Department presented the three-year Downtown Open Space Plan, noting it is a non-binding policy guideline document for parks, plazas, and greenways recommended unanimously by the Planning Commission. Nine public speakers representing downtown residents, Triangle Land Conservancy, and Durham Area Designers urged adoption, while Council Members Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel emphasized retaining flexibility, developing future cost estimates, and protecting DPAC Green and the Beltline.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Property Acquisition for Police Headquarters (East Main / Elizabeth / Ramsey / Hood Streets)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services Director Joel Reiser presented purchase options totaling $5.69 million for 4.439 acres from GWC Properties ($5.49 million) and 0.084 acres at 102 Hood Street from W.T. Wilkerson ($200,401) for a new police headquarters and 911 complex. Council Member Eugene Brown opposed the acquisition over its high per-acre cost, single appraisal, and ~$300,000-$400,000 demolition expense, while public speakers debated East Durham investment, total cost, and preservation of the 1928 and 1948 Carpenter Motor Company buildings.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Stabilization Program 3 (NSP3) Grant Project Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson presented a grant project ordinance to accept additional state-awarded NSP3 funds with a November 3 expenditure deadline to support infrastructure for the Southside redevelopment project.

agenda_items.title: FY 2015 Agreement with North Carolina State University for Triangle Regional Model
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker James Chavis questioned why citizens had limited advance notice of the packet and asked whether the modeling contract connected to light rail and East Durham jobs. Mayor Bell clarified the contract covers regional transportation demand modeling rather than light rail construction and pledged community engagement, after which Council approved Item 7 and discussed establishing credibility criteria for future affordable housing market studies.

votes.item_title: Addition of City Manager's Priority Items (Items 20 and 21) to Agenda
votes.notes: Added supplemental Item 20 (Police Headquarters property acquisition) and Item 21 (NSP3 grant project ordinance).
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested the addition of two supplemental priority items to the October 20 agenda: Item 20 for the proposed acquisition of GWC Properties and W.T. Wilkerson parcels for a new police headquarters, and Item 21 for a Neighborhood Stabilization Program 3 grant project ordinance. No council member objected to adding the items. The Council voted 7-0 via the electronic voting system to add both items to the agenda.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 10, excluding pulled Item 7)
votes.notes: Item 7 (NCSU Triangle Regional Model agreement) was pulled for separate discussion.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell read through the consent agenda headings, including Council minutes, a Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission appointment, FY14 carryover and FY15 budget/grant ordinances, CDBG contracts for Interfaith Hospitality Network and Urban Ministries of Durham, the 911 interlocal agreement, and a stormwater infrastructure repair contract amendment. Item 7 was pulled from the consent docket for separate consideration. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval of the remaining consent items, seconded by Council Member Diane Catotti, passing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Adoption of the Downtown Open Space Plan
votes.notes: Non-binding long-range policy guideline document; Council retains discretion over individual projects and funding.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff member Tom Dawson presented the Downtown Open Space Plan developed over three years with five public meetings and unanimous Planning Commission endorsement. Nine speakers, including Reynolds Smith, John Goebel, Chad Jemison of Triangle Land Conservancy, Dan Jewell of Durham Area Designers, Randolph Hester, and downtown residents, strongly urged adoption as a living, community-built plan. Council Member Diane Catotti requested future overall cost estimates and project prioritization while affirming council flexibility on individual sites, and Council Member Steve Schewel praised the Beltline, Convention Center Plaza, Church/Roxboro park, and DPAC Green concepts. After Eugene Brown called the question, the Council adopted the plan 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Acquisition of East Main, Elizabeth, Ramsey, and Hood Street Properties for Police Headquarters
votes.notes: Purchase options of $5.49M (GWC Properties, 4.439 acres) and $200,401 (W.T. Wilkerson at 102 Hood St, 0.084 acres).
votes.discussion_detail: General Services Director Joel Reiser presented options to acquire 4.439 acres from GWC Properties for $5.49 million (appraised at $5.39 million, with 11 tenants providing 2015 lease revenue) and 0.084 acres at 102 Hood Street from W.T. Wilkerson for $200,401 (appraised at $80,000 for land/building alone, excluding ~$175,000 in annual net restaurant revenue). Mayor Bell questioned paying 2.5 times appraised value on Hood Street, and Council Member Eugene Brown criticized relying on a single appraisal and spending ~$1.33 million per acre plus $300,000-$400,000 in demolition costs (~$6 million total). Public commenters included GWC broker Marcus Jackson supporting the East Main location, Victoria Peterson opposing the $6 million outlay in favor of youth job training, and Rob Emerson opposing demolition of the historic 1928 and 1948 Carpenter Motor Company buildings. Council Members Diane Catotti, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel voted yes while requesting public urban design forums, walkable Main Street retail activation, and parking coordination with the Dillard light rail station; the motion passed 6-1 with Brown voting no.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Neighborhood Stabilization Program 3 (NSP3) Grant Project Ordinance
votes.notes: Accepts additional state-awarded NSP3 funds for Southside infrastructure with a November 3 expenditure deadline.
votes.discussion_detail: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson explained that the state awarded the City additional Neighborhood Stabilization Program 3 funds the previous week, subject to a strict November 3 expenditure deadline. The funds were designated for infrastructure improvements in the Southside redevelopment project. Without debate, the Council approved the grant project ordinance 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 7 (Pulled from Consent): FY 2015 Agreement with North Carolina State University for Triangle Regional Model
votes.notes: Following the vote, Mayor Bell questioned Community Development Director Reginald Johnson on establishing validation criteria for housing market studies, and Catotti explained the 10-day work session and 5-day agenda public notice timeline.
votes.discussion_detail: East Durham resident James Chavis pulled Item 7 to ask why citizens received late notice of large agenda packets and whether the NCSU agreement was tied to the light rail project and East Durham job opportunities. Mayor Bill Bell explained that the item was strictly a contract for the Triangle Regional Model transportation demand study rather than a light rail construction decision, while assuring Chavis of extensive public outreach as Triangle Transit moves forward. The Council then approved Item 7 by a 7-0 vote before Mayor Bell raised a follow-up question regarding validation criteria for credible housing market studies.

disagreements.issue: Acquisition of East Main Street / Carpenter Motor Company Site for New Police Headquarters
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over acquiring 4.523 acres along East Main Street for ~$5.69 million (plus demolition) for a new police headquarters and 911 complex, with Eugene Brown dissenting on cost and appraisal grounds while other members supported the site while pressing for urban design, retail activation, and historic/transit trade-offs.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the GWC Properties and W.T. Wilkerson land acquisition options to secure a consolidated central East Main Street site for police and 911 operations.
side_a_arguments: Extensive site search ruled out Fayetteville Street (planned for DHA redevelopment) and showed rebuilding on the existing site was cost-prohibitive.
Police and 911 departments wholeheartedly endorse the site, and GWC tenant rents during 2015 help offset the purchase premium over appraisal.
Staff committed to public design forums to improve Main Street walkability, streetscape, and potential public-private retail partnerships.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the acquisition due to excessive cost (~$1.33M/acre plus demolition), reliance on a single appraisal, and paying 2.5x appraised value for the Hood Street parcel.
side_b_arguments: The city normally obtains two appraisals for major real estate acquisitions, whereas only one appraisal was done per property here.
Combined acquisition and $300,000-$400,000 demolition costs total roughly $6 million, representing an exceedingly high price per acre.
Public speakers also objected to demolishing the historic 1928 and 1948 Carpenter Motor Company buildings and questioned spending $6 million on a large headquarters.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 6-1; General Services proceeded with geotechnical/environmental due diligence and committed to public design forums and periodic Council updates.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 9, 2014 Durham City Council Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell presided and all formal Council votes were unanimous—with no split or contested votes—including excused absences for Bell and Council Member Steve Schewel for the October 23 work session, rule suspension and approval of Item 19 (a third air-lease modification with Shaner SPE Associates Limited Partnership settling space-allocation litigation), a 7-0 ballot appointment of Diana Hall to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, agenda-setting, and entry into closed session. Union representative Nathan Mayo alleged unequal treatment and retaliation in the Police Department and other city departments, prompting Council members to discuss referring systemic workplace concerns to the Human Relations Commission. In an extended presentation on Item 13 (the new Durham Police Headquarters and E911 facility), staff recommended the former Carpenter Chevrolet site on East Main Street over the four-acre Chapel Hill Street site (which would require 12–18 months longer for phased construction) and placing E911 on the second floor of the City Hall Annex while rejecting a $3.4 million temporary relocation. Although Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved to accept the recommended site, Council members hesitated to act before public and media reaction and withdrew the motion to revisit site selection at an upcoming Council meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absences, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:01 p.m. and Council unanimously granted excused absences to Mayor Bell and Council Member Steve Schewel for the October 23 work session due to the Metro Mayors Conference. Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority items (referring Item 9 Liberty Arts sculpture donation back to administration, scheduling the Long Meadow Pool study for 2:00 p.m., and noting a 9th Street update and economic development closed session) and the City Attorney's priority items (Item 19 air-lease modification and two attorney-client closed sessions).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Item 19: Shaner SPE Associates Air Lease Modification
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent, presentation, and public hearing items—pulling Item 4 (FY 13–14 carryover), Item 7 (NCSU transportation agreement), Item 10 (stormwater infrastructure amendment), and Item 13 (Police Headquarters and 911). Council then unanimously suspended the rules and unanimously approved Item 19, the third modification of the air lease with Shaner SPE Associates Limited Partnership finalizing a joint City-County space-allocation court settlement.

agenda_items.title: Union Remarks on Police and City Workplace Retaliation Allegations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Union speaker Nathan Mayo alleged escalating unequal treatment and workplace retaliation in the Durham Police Department and other city departments. Council members stressed they would not intervene in individual personnel cases but urged addressing broader systemic workplace concerns and bringing a report back through the Human Relations Commission.

agenda_items.title: Item 13: Police Headquarters and E911 Facility Site Selection Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, staff presented site, design, and procurement updates for the new Police Headquarters and E911 facility, shortlisting three design firms and four construction-management firms and proposing an open, non-'bunker' downtown office aesthetic with E911 on the second floor of the Annex. Staff favored the East Main Street former Carpenter Chevrolet site over the four-acre Chapel Hill Street site (citing a $3.4M temporary move cost or 12–18 month phased delay and asking to assess reusing the El Centro building); a unanimous voice vote occurred at 03:40:09 after a gap, and a later motion to accept the East Main site was withdrawn at 03:48:11 so the public could weigh in before Council votes.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting October 6, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council unanimously approved the Amanda Road street closing, the Hanover Point subdivision rezoning (reducing units from 68 to 41 despite neighbors' concerns over deteriorating state-maintained roads), and accepted public comments on the FY 2015-2020 Consolidated Plan needs hearing focused on transit-oriented affordable housing and homebuyer education. Council also appointed Steve Schewel as primary member and Mayor Bill Bell as alternate to the Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro MPO Board, and voted 6-0 to continue pulled Item 4 (dedicated housing funding guidelines) to the October 23 work session to incorporate transit-proximity bonus points and allow public comment.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions for Council Member Steve Schewel, National Arts & Humanities Month, DollarWise Award, and Domestic Violence Awareness Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mary Henderson of the NC Recreation and Parks Association presented Council Member Steve Schewel with the Distinguished Legislator Award for championing the half-cent parks maintenance tax and greenways. Mayor Bell also recognized National Arts and Humanities Month, DollarWise youth winner Kayla Ponce-DeLeon, Domestic Violence Awareness Month with Durham Crisis Response Center, retiring Community Development Assistant Director Larry Jarvis, and the U.S. Supreme Court's action clearing the way for marriage equality in North Carolina.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden & Supplemental DCHC MPO Board Appointment Item
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to excuse Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden to leave early after approximately five minutes, and voted 7-0 to add the DCHC MPO Board appointments as a supplemental priority item ahead of Wednesday's MPO meeting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Excluding Pulled Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council adopted the consent agenda excluding Item 4 (pulled by Council Member Steve Schewel and speaker Stephen Hopkins), approving minutes, a Workforce Development Board appointment, the June 2014 Code Enforcement Performance Audit, biosolids/water contracts, the August 2014 bid report, stop-loss insurance renewal, a WIA contract amendment, and a utility extension agreement.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing — Amanda Road (SC1400001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Steve Medlin presented a request by Tony M. Tate Landscape Architecture PA to close approximately 870 linear feet (the entire length) of Amanda Road, noting no negative impacts were identified by reviewing agencies and no members of the public spoke.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Hanover Point Subdivision (Z1400004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lennar Carolinas LLC sought to rezone 13.96 acres at 1030 McLamb Drive from PDR 4.76 to PDR 4.0, reducing allowed units from 68 to 41 single-family homes and removing 2006 off-site road commitments on Sharon Road. Resident Greg Stocking submitted a 32-signature petition opposing the required UDO street connection to McLamb Drive due to narrow, crumbling state-maintained roads, but Council approved the rezoning and consistency statement 6-0, noting denial would revert to 68 units with the same connection.

agenda_items.title: FY 2015–2020 Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan Needs Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Larry Jarvis and Wilmur Conyers outlined expected HUD entitlement funds (~$1.795M CDBG, $832k HOME, $147k ESG). Nine public speakers advocated for equitable transit-oriented affordable housing near light rail stations, homebuyer and financial literacy education for minority/Latino residents, senior home rehab in Northeast Central Durham, rapid rehousing capacity, and longer affordability covenants beyond 15-20 years.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro (DCHC) MPO Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Having been elected Chair of the Triangle Transit Authority, Mayor Bill Bell proposed stepping down as Durham's primary voting representative on the DCHC MPO Board and serving as alternate while Council Member Steve Schewel becomes primary representative.

agenda_items.title: Guidelines for Dedicated Funding Source for Small Project Development and Neighborhood Revitalization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Stephen Hopkins objected to the lack of external public input on the draft scoring criteria, while Council Member Steve Schewel relayed Bo Glenn's proposal to award 4 bonus points for affordable housing within a half-mile of proposed Durham-Orange light rail stations. Staff agreed to incorporate the transit bonus points, and Council continued the item to the October 23 work session to allow public review.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Continued to Oct. 23 work session 6-0 (Cole-McFadden excused)

votes.item_title: Procedural Motion: Excuse Early Departure of Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden requested to be excused in approximately five minutes; she remained through Item 11.
votes.discussion_detail: During council announcements, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden requested to be excused from the remainder of the meeting in approximately five minutes. The motion to excuse her early departure was properly moved, seconded, and approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Addition of Supplemental Item: Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro MPO Board Appointments
votes.notes: City Clerk priority item added so appointments would be effective before the Wednesday MPO Board meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: City Clerk D. Ann Gray announced a supplemental item titled Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro MPO Board Appointments, noting Mayor Bill Bell requested moving it from Thursday's work session to Monday night so the change would be effective before Wednesday's MPO meeting. Mayor Bell explained he had been elected Chair of Triangle Transit Authority and wanted Steve Schewel to serve as primary MPO representative with Bell as alternate. Council voted 7-0 to add the item to the agenda.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-3 and 5-10, excluding pulled Item 4)
votes.notes: Item 4 was pulled by Council Member Steve Schewel and speaker Stephen Hopkins.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda headings, covering minutes, Workforce Development Board appointment, June 2014 Code Enforcement Performance Audit, Synagro Central biosolids contract, water management structure demolition contract, August 2014 bid report, Reliance Standard stop-loss insurance renewal, WIA contract amendment, and the Eakes utility extension agreement. Item 4 was pulled for separate discussion. Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden and seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, the remaining consent items passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Amanda Road Street Closing (SC1400001)
votes.notes: Closes ~870 linear feet (entire length) of Amanda Road for recombination with adjacent properties.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Steve Medlin presented SC1400001, an application by Tony M. Tate Landscape Architecture PA to close approximately 870 linear feet comprising the entirety of Amanda Road. Reviewing city, county, and outside utility agencies identified no negative effects, and staff recommended approval. No council members had questions and no members of the public spoke during the hearing; Council Member Diane Catotti moved approval, seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown, passing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 12: Zoning Map Change — Hanover Point Subdivision (Z1400004)
votes.notes: Cora Cole-McFadden excused earlier in meeting. Rezones 13.96 acres at 1030 McLamb Drive from PDR 4.76 to PDR 4.0 (41 single-family units).
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Steve Medlin and Lennar Carolinas representative Robert Shunk presented Z1400004, rezoning 13.96 acres of Hanover Point from PDR 4.76 to PDR 4.0 to reduce homes from 68 to 41 single-family units and remove obsolete 2006 Sharon Road intersection improvement commitments, while retaining a $500/unit Durham Public Schools contribution and prohibiting zero-lot-line homes. Resident Greg Stocking presented photos and a 32-homeowner petition opposing the UDO-mandated road connection from Willow Crest Road into McLamb Drive, arguing McLamb, Bristolwood, and Danbury are narrow, crumbling state-maintained roads unable to handle cut-through traffic. Staff and Transportation confirmed the right-of-way was already dedicated in 2006 and most traffic would head south on city-standard Ashton Hall streets. Council members sympathized with neighbors' NCDOT road conditions—suggesting petitioning NCDOT or city annexation—but noted denying the rezoning would leave 68 homes approved under the 2006 plan, and voted 6-0 to approve.

votes.item_title: Item 12: Comprehensive Plan Consistency Statement for Hanover Point Subdivision (Z1400004)
votes.notes: Cora Cole-McFadden excused. Required separate statutory consistency motion.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following approval of the Hanover Point zoning map change, Planning staff reminded the Council that a separate statutory consistency motion was required. Council Member Don Moffitt moved adoption of the consistency statement as stated in the staff report, seconded by Council Member Steve Schewel. The motion passed 6-0 with Cora Cole-McFadden absent.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Acceptance of Public Hearing Comments on FY 2015–2020 Consolidated Plan Needs
votes.notes: Cora Cole-McFadden excused. Mayor Bell briefly misstated the item number as Item 4 before staff clarified it was the Consolidated Plan needs public hearing (Item 13).
votes.discussion_detail: Community Development staff Larry Jarvis and Wilmur Conyers opened the first required HUD public hearing for the FY 2015-2020 Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan, outlining ~2.77 million in expected CDBG, HOME, and ESG funds. Nine speakers—including leaders from the Durham Regional Financial Center, Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit, Housing for New Hope, Durham Community Land Trustees, and Northeast Central Durham—urged prioritizing transit-oriented affordable housing (at least 100 units/year within a half-mile of stations), an Equitable TOD fund, bilingual homebuyer education, senior home weatherization/rehab, rapid rehousing, and extending affordability periods beyond 15-20 years. Council Members Steve Schewel and Don Moffitt highlighted the dedicated penny tax for affordable housing and its use to extend affordability terms, after which Moffitt moved and Diane Catotti seconded accepting the public comments, passing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Supplemental Item: Appointment of Steve Schewel as Member and Bill Bell as Alternate to DCHC MPO Board
votes.notes: Cora Cole-McFadden excused. Swaps Mayor Bell and Council Member Schewel's roles on the Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro Metropolitan Planning Organization Board.
votes.discussion_detail: Following addition of the City Clerk's supplemental item earlier in the meeting, Mayor Bill Bell requested a formal motion to appoint Council Member Steve Schewel as Durham's primary voting member and Mayor Bell as alternate on the Durham-Chapel Hill-Carrboro MPO Board prior to its Wednesday meeting. The swap accommodated Bell's election as Chair of the Triangle Transit Authority. The motion passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 4 (Pulled from Consent): Motion to Continue Dedicated Housing Funding Guidelines to October 23 Work Session
votes.notes: Cora Cole-McFadden excused. Audio of 6-0 vote was slightly garbled in transcript as 'six to see one okay'.
votes.discussion_detail: On pulled Item 4 regarding dedicated funding guidelines for small project development and neighborhood revitalization, resident Stephen Hopkins criticized the lack of external housing stakeholder input before bringing the scoring criteria for adoption. Council Member Steve Schewel cited an email from Bo Glenn proposing bonus points for projects within one-half mile of proposed light rail stations to strengthen federal FTA grant competitiveness, and Assistant Director Larry Jarvis proposed reallocating points in both categories to grant 4 bonus points for transit-proximate projects. Mayor Bill Bell expressed concern about adopting guidelines without giving housing stakeholders an opportunity to comment on the revised criteria and requested a two-week continuance to the October 23 work session so staff could distribute the updated draft via listserv, passing 6-0.

disagreements.issue: Hanover Point UDO Road Connection to McLamb Drive (Z1400004)
disagreements.summary: Residents along McLamb Drive, Bristolwood Drive, and Danbury Road opposed connecting Hanover Point (Willow Crest Road) to McLamb Drive due to narrow, deteriorating state-maintained roads, while Council approved the rezoning 6-0 because the connection was required by UDO connectivity rules and already dedicated in 2006.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Z1400004 rezoning to reduce density from 68 to 41 single-family homes while maintaining the previously dedicated UDO street connection.
side_a_arguments: Denying the rezoning leaves the 2006 approval intact, allowing 68 higher-density homes while still requiring the exact same McLamb Drive connection.
UDO connectivity standards mandate tying into dedicated stub roads for emergency access and interconnected neighborhoods.
Most Hanover Point traffic will travel south through modern city-standard Ashton Hall streets rather than north onto deteriorating state roads.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose connecting Willow Crest Road to McLamb Drive and direct new development traffic elsewhere until roads are upgraded.
side_b_arguments: McLamb and Bristolwood are 18-foot-wide, uncurbed 1984 tar-and-gravel state roads already disintegrating into dirt.
Cut-through commuters heading north toward Highway 98 and Wake Forest will accelerate road deterioration without developer or NCDOT repair funding.
32 neighbors signed a petition favoring use of an alternate future connector stub further from existing homes.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 6-0; Council advised residents to petition NCDOT (including former Durham Mayor Nick Tennyson) or consider voluntary city annexation for street maintenance.

disagreements.issue: Process and Transit Scoring Criteria for Dedicated Housing Funding Guidelines (Item 4)
disagreements.summary: Community member Stephen Hopkins and Mayor Bell objected to adopting new small-project and neighborhood revitalization scoring criteria without external public review, while Schewel requested adding half-mile transit-station bonus points.
disagreements.side_a_position: Continue adoption for two weeks to October 23 work session so staff can incorporate transit-proximity bonus points and solicit public comments.
side_a_arguments: No external housing stakeholders had reviewed the draft scoring criteria prior to the Council vote.
Incorporating Bo Glenn's last-minute suggestion for 4 bonus points near light rail stations warrants transparent public circulation via listserv.
A brief two-week delay will not derail late-December or early-January application timelines.
disagreements.side_b_position: Original staff recommendation sought immediate adoption to issue competitive application documents without delay before Assistant Director Larry Jarvis's departure.
side_b_arguments: Adopting guidelines promptly gives prospective developers adequate optioning and due diligence time ahead of late December/early January deadlines.
Staff followed the same internal drafting process used in prior funding cycles.
disagreements.resolution: Continued 6-0 to the October 23 work session with direction to add 4 transit-proximity bonus points and circulate the draft for public feedback.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 18, 2014 Durham City Council Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell presided and all votes were unanimous—with no split or contested votes—including acceptance of City Manager and City Attorney priority items, a 7-0 ballot appointment to the Workforce Development Board, agenda-setting for the regular meeting, and entry into closed session for attorney-client consultations including Developer Surety vs. City of Durham. Council members asked staff to prepare a Chapter 70 ordinance amendment delegating administrative approval of single-resident sewer extensions caused by failed septic tanks, and heard Citizens' Matters remarks from John Tarantino and a second speaker. On affordable housing underwriting and Dedicated Funding Source guidelines, staff explained aligning replacement-reserve assumptions ($250/unit new construction, $350/unit rehab) and 1.15 debt-coverage ratios with the North Carolina Housing Finance Agency QAP, though members worried low reserves could force future city refinancing, while staff noted the $500,000 small-project set-aside would primarily serve Habitat for Humanity lot acquisition and Northeast Central Durham/Southside revitalization. Council also extensively questioned Police Department leadership regarding Human Relations Commission recommendations, I-85/I-40/NC-147 highway interdiction traffic stops, multi-car police backups, written consent search forms, and responsibility for property damage during forced-entry warrant executions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:01 p.m. with Council Member Eugene Brown present and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden en route. Members shared updates on a DDI board meeting, the Ellerbe Creek Nature Tour, and a Triangle J Council of Governments resolution circulated by Eddie Davis, then unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (moved by Diane Catotti, seconded by Eugene Brown) and the City Attorney's request for two attorney-client closed sessions under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Chapter 70 Septic-Failure Sewer Extension Delegation and Agenda Review

Engineering staff confirmed Chapter 70 currently requires Council approval and agreed to draft an ordinance amendment delegating that authority.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council heard three-minute public remarks from John Tarantino and another speaker regarding local civic issues and Council member interactions.

agenda_items.title: Affordable Housing Underwriting Standards and DFS Small-Project Set-Aside
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained why city underwriting uses a 1.15 debt-coverage ratio and $250/$350 per-unit replacement reserves to match the North Carolina Housing Finance Agency QAP, though Council members cautioned those reserve levels seemed low and risked future city refinancing requests. Staff also outlined how the $500,000 Dedicated Funding Source small-project category would mainly support Habitat for Humanity lot acquisition and neighborhood revitalization in Northeast Central Durham and the Southside CNI footprint.

agenda_items.title: Human Relations Commission Follow-Up and Police Traffic Stop, Consent Search, and Warrant Practices
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed Human Relations Commission recommendations—including recruitment steps, Durham One Call complaint routing, and written consent search forms—and questioned police leadership on highway drug-interdiction traffic stops along I-85, I-40, and NC-147. Members asked why multiple police cruisers converge on single stops and who bears repair costs when doors are forced open during warrant executions.

votes.notes: Seconded by Council Member Eugene Brown; passed by voice vote without opposition.

votes.discussion_detail: Fair housing consultant Stella Adams pulled Item 5 to argue that HUD Section 3 plans and subcontractor allocations must be determined prior to contract award rather than relying on after-the-fact best-efforts reporting, stating she would submit a FOIA request on Phase 1 and Phase 2 compliance and file a complaint if non-compliant. Mayor Bell noted the item was a recommended consent action and invited any further technical questions to be directed to Community Development staff. Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden and seconded by Council Member Diane Catotti, the item passed 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Police Consent Search Policy, Marijuana Enforcement, and Community Trust (Item 4: City Manager's HRC/CPRB Report)
disagreements.summary: While Council did not vote on Item 4, council members pressed City Manager Tom Bonfield and DPD leadership to go further than the manager's report on mandatory written consent forms for vehicle searches and lowering enforcement priority for low-level marijuana offenses.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require written consent forms for all consensual vehicle searches, deprioritize low-level marijuana arrests, and expand neighborhood foot patrols and informant protections.
side_a_arguments: Young Black men report arbitrary stops, making written consent forms urgent and legally permissible.
High marijuana arrest rates among African American males induct young people into the criminal justice system despite polling favoring treatment.
McDougald Terrace residents want officers out of patrol cars walking neighborhoods and stronger confidentiality when reporting crimes.
disagreements.side_b_position: City Manager's report favored officer discretion on vehicle consent searches (requiring written/recorded consent for homes and HEAT teams), semi-annual data reviews, and multi-agency dialogue before changing marijuana enforcement.
side_b_arguments: Requiring written forms during every patrol traffic stop raises situational control and officer safety considerations.
Meaningful changes to low-level drug enforcement require buy-in from the District Attorney, Sheriff, and District Court judges.
DPD has already begun Fair and Impartial Policing racial equity training and expanded data analytics.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; City Manager Bonfield committed to returning for a comprehensive page-by-page work-session discussion on Thursday, September 4, 2014.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session August 21, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: At a packed City Council work session, City Manager Tom Bonfield presented his 131-page response to the 34 Human Relations Commission recommendations and 10 Civilian Police Review Board recommendations regarding racial disparities and Durham Police Department practices. Council members questioned staff on mandatory written consent for vehicle searches, body/car cameras, bias-based policing training, and marijuana enforcement, while 19 public speakers split between civil rights/community advocates demanding mandatory written search consent and police union/Hispanic speakers supporting Chief Jose Lopez and the manager's report. Council also heard a Falls Lake Algal Turf Scrubber pilot presentation, cast paper ballots for BPAC and Environmental Affairs appointments, and unanimously set the September 2 agenda.

agenda_items.title: Direct-Hire Employee Evaluations (City Clerk and City Attorney)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell reported that Council met in closed session for evaluations of the City Clerk and City Attorney, voted to continue the closed session to Tuesday at 5:00 p.m. (moved by Cole-McFadden, seconded by Schewel), and returned to open session (moved by Cole-McFadden, seconded by Davis).

agenda_items.title: Work Session Consent & Departmental Items Review (BPAC/EAB Ballots, Emergency Plan, Southside Phase II, SODE Grant, Duke/Gregson Curb Extensions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council cast paper ballots for BPAC (Emily Egge 4 votes, Kendra Bridges 5 votes) and Environmental Affairs Board (Frank Hahn 7 votes) to be placed on the Sept. 2 consent agenda, heard a resident update on the Angier-Driver corridor project, and questioned staff on McCormick Baron Salazar's management fee and unit costs for Southside Phase II (79 units), SODE breakfast grant balances, and lowest-bid sequencing on Duke/Gregson curb extensions.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Ballots tallied; placed on Sept. 2 consent agenda

agenda_items.title: Presentation: BioHabitats Inc. Algal Turf Scrubber Mobile Pilot System for Falls Lake Nutrient Reduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works staff Danielle Mier and Michelle Woolfolk presented the Falls Lake Stage 1 nutrient reduction mandate ($45 million estimated compliance cost) and the ~$400,000 Algal Turf Scrubber pilot study as a potentially cost-saving technology prior to any $5-12 million full-scale facility. Council members questioned minority/women business participation (0% minority, 3% women), modeling assumptions, and taxpayer/Watershed funding burdens.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Response to Human Relations Commission and Civilian Police Review Board Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented his 60-day team review acknowledging unexplained racial disparities and proposing semi-annual stop data reviews, Fair and Impartial Policing training, expanded CIT mental health training, and written/recorded consent for home and HEAT-team searches while leaving patrol vehicle consent searches discretionary. Council Members Steve Schewel, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Diane Catotti pushed for mandatory written vehicle search consent, body/car camera guidelines, and multi-agency action on marijuana arrests, followed by 19 public speakers debating systemic racial profiling vs. support for Chief Jose Lopez.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Placed on Sept. 2 General Business Agenda

agenda_items.title: Setting the September 2, 2014 City Council Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council briefly debated whether to place the HRC/CPRB report (Item 4) on the Sept. 2 General Business Agenda or hold it directly for a deeper Sept. 4 work session review, ultimately approving the Sept. 2 agenda (Consent Items 1-3, 5-12; GBA Item 4) by unanimous voice vote after electronic voting malfunctioned.

votes.item_title: Setting the September 2, 2014 City Council Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-3, 5-12 and GBA Item 4)
votes.notes: Electronic voting board malfunctioned; Mayor Bell called a voice vote which passed unanimously. Paper ballots for Items 1 and 2 (BPAC: Kendra Bridges 5, Emily Egge 4; EAB: Frank Hahn 7) were tallied immediately prior.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved and Council Member Eugene Brown seconded setting the September 2, 2014 City Council agenda with Consent Items 1-3 and 5-12 and General Business Agenda Item 4 (the HRC/CPRB report). Council Member Diane Catotti asked whether Item 4 could be held until the September 4 work session for a page-by-page discussion, and Eugene Brown asked whether another public hearing was planned; Mayor Bell clarified Sept. 2 would not be a public hearing and would allow initial council feedback before moving to Thursday if desired. After the clerk read the BPAC and Environmental Affairs Board ballot results and the electronic voting machines failed to open, Mayor Bell conducted a voice vote that passed unanimously 7-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session August 21, 2014
disagreements.issue: Written Consent for Vehicle Searches, Camera Mandates, CPRB Authority, and Marijuana Enforcement (HRC/CPRB Response)
disagreements.summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield's 131-page response and supporters (including FOP lodges and Hispanic community speakers) backed discretionary patrol vehicle consent searches and a measured review of DPD practices, whereas Council Members Steve Schewel and Cora Cole-McFadden and FADE/People's Alliance/NAACP/Durham CAN speakers demanded mandatory written vehicle search consent, stricter camera rules, independent CPRB authority, and immediate action on racial disparities.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require mandatory written consent forms for all vehicle consent searches, establish firmer camera activation rules, and pursue marijuana deprioritization and stronger civilian oversight.
side_a_arguments: Written consent is the most reliable safeguard against racial disparities in vehicle stops where dashcams/microphones cannot capture out-of-range encounters.
Wait-and-see data reviews until 2015 fail to stop ongoing harm, including 86% of simple marijuana arrests falling on African Americans.

Advocacy groups (FADE, SCSJ, People's Alliance, Durham CAN, NAACP, Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People) warned that without mandatory written vehicle consent and CPRB investigative authority, systemic disparities will persist.
disagreements.side_b_position: Adopt the City Manager's recommendations requiring written/recorded consent only for home/premises and HEAT-team searches while preserving patrol officer discretion, and defend Chief Jose Lopez and DPD.
side_b_arguments: Requiring patrol officers to return to cruisers for paper forms during traffic stops creates officer safety and situational control risks.
DPD has already launched Fair and Impartial Policing training, expanded CIT training (180 officers), and strong data analytics.
Police union (FOP Lodge #2) and Hispanic speakers urged adopting Bonfield's report and opposed calls to remove Chief Lopez.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote on the substance at the work session; Item 4 was placed on the September 2 General Business Agenda for Council deliberation.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting August 18, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: With Council Member Eugene Brown excused absent, the Durham City Council voted 6-0 across all items, including a $924,676 seven-year economic development incentive agreement with Argos Therapeutics Inc. matched by Durham County to secure a $40.9 million biopharmaceutical manufacturing expansion in Durham. Council also approved four street closings (South Miami Blvd, Belmont Dr, Dodson St, Waterbury Dr), two consolidated annexations (Jovan/Northeast Creek and 1307 Old Oxford Rd), and two pulled consent items (Crime Statistics Performance Audit and a Time Warner Cable network services contract) after public questions on youth detention and local/minority hiring.

agenda_items.title: Swearing-In of Durham Youth Commission, New Deputy City Clerk, and Homeless Services Advisory Committee Member
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office of Youth Director Evelyn Scott introduced incoming Durham Youth Commission members who took the oath of office. City Clerk D. Ann Gray also introduced new Deputy City Clerk Diana Schreiber and swore in Latasha Wilson to the Durham Homeless Services Advisory Committee.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items (Revisions to Items 7, 18, and 19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented minor memo corrections for Item 7 (Microsoft Enterprise Agreement) and updated recommendations/statutory consistency statements for Items 18 and 19 pursuant to a new N.C. Court of Appeals ruling, while noting the HRC/CPRB response report was posted online.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Excluding Pulled Items 2 and 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda excluding Items 2 and 9 (pulled by Victoria Peterson), covering an appointment, the Overtime Follow-Up Performance Audit, a utility extension at 602 Pleasant Dr, Right-of-Way ordinance updates, Microsoft and Munis software agreements, generator maintenance, and railroad pipeline agreements for the Downtown Loop waterline.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Argos Therapeutics Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD's Kevin Dick presented a $924,676 seven-year incentive (matched by Durham County) to retain Argos Therapeutics and support a $40.9 million capital investment and biopharmaceutical jobs over competing offers from Mebane/Orange County ($3.1M), Florida, Texas, and Quebec. Chamber President Ted Conner and Argos CEO Jeff Abbey spoke in support; Victoria Peterson asked for local and African American hiring data, and Steve Schewel urged increasing the 25-30% Durham resident workforce target.

agenda_items.title: Street Closings: South Miami Blvd (SC1400010), Belmont Dr (SC1400008), Dodson St (SC1400009), and Waterbury Dr (SC1400006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Pat Young presented four uncontested street closing requests for unopened/unused rights-of-way: South Miami Blvd (Edens Land Corp.), Belmont Dr and Dodson St (Stewart Inc.), and Waterbury Dr (Robert Murphy). Review agencies identified no adverse impacts and Council approved all four 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexations: Jovan / Northeast Creek and 1307 Old Oxford Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented consolidated utility extension, voluntary annexation, and initial zoning requests for Jovan/Northeast Creek (177 acres at Ellis Rd/Durham Freeway, up to 676 units) and 1307 Old Oxford Rd (1.33 acres, IL zoning for self-storage expansion), noting both were projected to be revenue-positive. Council approved both annexations and the Item 19 consistency statement 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items: Crime Statistics Performance Audit (June 2014) and Time Warner Cable MAN Services Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 2 to criticize the lack of youth arrest breakdowns and raise alarm over 26 juveniles held in the Durham County Jail without schooling, and Audit Director Germaine Brewington clarified the audit verified data reporting controls. Peterson also pulled Item 9 to question Time Warner Cable's local Durham and African American hiring and criminal-record exclusions, with Mayor Bell and Steve Schewel noting 51% of the 1,500-1,800 employees in that Time Warner division were African American; both items passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Addition of City Manager's Priority Items (Modifications to Items 7, 18, and 19)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield introduced three priority modifications to the printed agenda: minor corrections to the issues/analysis section of Item 7 (Microsoft Enterprise Agreement) and revised recommendations plus statutory consistency statements for consolidated annexations Items 18 and 19 following a recent N.C. Court of Appeals decision. Bonfield also noted the HRC/CPRB response report was now posted online. Council approved the priority items 6-0 with Eugene Brown absent.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1, 3-8, 10-11, excluding pulled Items 2 and 9)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. Items 2 and 9 were pulled by Victoria Peterson.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell read the consent agenda headings covering the Homeless Services Advisory Committee appointment, Overtime Follow-Up Performance Audit, utility extension at 602 Pleasant Drive, right-of-way ordinance revisions, Microsoft and Munis software contracts, generator maintenance, and railroad pipeline agreements for the Downtown Loop waterline replacement. Items 2 and 9 were pulled for separate discussion. Council adopted the remaining consent items 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Economic Development Incentive Contract with Argos Therapeutics Inc. ($924,676)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. Performance-based 7-year incentive matched by Durham County for $40.9M capital investment.
votes.discussion_detail: OEWD's Kevin Dick presented a $924,676 seven-year performance-based incentive agreement (matched 100% by Durham County) to retain Duke spin-out Argos Therapeutics for a $40.9 million biopharmaceutical manufacturing expansion over higher competing bids from Mebane/Orange County ($3.1 million), Florida, Texas, and Quebec. Chamber President Ted Conner and Argos CEO Jeff Abbey testified that keeping 100 existing Durham employees and proximity to NCCU's BRITE Center and Durham Tech training tipped the scale toward Durham despite smaller state incentives. Speaker Victoria Peterson urged tracking Durham and African American hires, Mayor Bell noted workforce demographics already in the packet (25-35% Durham residents, 17% non-Caucasian, 50% female), and Council Member Steve Schewel urged Argos to increase its Durham resident hiring share and praised its YouthWorks internships. Council approved the agreement 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Street Closing — South Miami Boulevard (SC1400010)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. Closes 3,585 sq ft unused right-of-way requested by Edens Land Corp.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Pat Young presented SC1400010, an application by Edens Land Corporation to close a 3,585-square-foot segment of South Miami Boulevard right-of-way that is open on paper but unused for vehicular traffic. Twenty city departments and public service agencies reviewed the request and found no negative impacts. With no council questions or public speakers, the Council closed the public hearing and approved the street closing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Street Closing — Belmont Drive (SC1400008)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. Closes two unused segments totaling ~7,035 sq ft requested by Stewart Inc.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Pat Young presented SC1400008, a request by Stewart Incorporated to close two unused segments of Belmont Drive totaling approximately 7,035 square feet. Applicant representative Mike Tarrant appeared to answer any questions, and no opposition was raised during the public hearing. With 20 reviewing agencies reporting no negative impacts and staff recommending approval, Council approved the closing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 16: Street Closing — Dodson Street (SC1400009)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. Companion item to SC1400008; electronic vote board had to be reset before tally.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Pat Young presented SC1400009 as a companion request by Stewart Incorporated to close approximately 199.81 linear feet of unused Dodson Street right-of-way. Reviewing departments and outside agencies identified no adverse impacts, and no public speakers came forward. After resetting the electronic voting machines due to a signal glitch, Council approved the street closing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Street Closing — Waterbury Drive (SC1400006)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. Closes 160.3 linear feet requested by Robert Murphy; Parks & Rec confirmed infeasible as Sandy Creek Park access.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Pat Young presented SC1400006, an application by Robert Murphy to close 160.3 linear feet of unused Waterbury Drive right-of-way. Young noted that while the site had once been considered as a potential access point to Sandy Creek Park, Parks and Recreation determined access there would be infeasible and none of the 20 reviewing agencies found adverse impacts. With no public speakers, Council approved the closure 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Jovan / Northeast Creek Consolidated Annexation, Utility Extension, and Initial Zoning
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. 177 acres at Ellis Rd & Durham Freeway (max 676 units). Although staff noted two motions were required, the audio shows a single 6-0 vote before moving to Item 19.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Pat Young presented a consolidated utility extension, non-contiguous voluntary annexation, and transitional initial zoning request (PDR 4.840, CG(D), RS-20, IL(D)) for ~177 acres at Ellis Road and the Durham Freeway allowing up to 676 residential units and 122 projected students, noting positive projected fiscal revenues and adequate water/sewer capacity. Council Member Steve Schewel asked for an explanation of street impact fee credits on page 5 of the memo, and Public Works' Rob Joyner explained developers earn impact fee offsets by constructing off-site turn lanes and road improvements. With no public speakers, Mayor Bell called the vote, passing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 19: 1307 Old Oxford Road Consolidated Annexation, Utility Extension, and Initial Zoning (IL)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. Annexes 1.33-acre portion for self-service storage expansion.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Pat Young presented the consolidated annexation, utility extension agreement, and initial Industrial Light (IL) zoning for a 1.33-acre portion of 1307 Old Oxford Road to expand an existing self-service storage facility. Public Works confirmed utility capacity and Budget and Management Services projected positive fiscal impact. With no council questions or public comment, Council approved the annexation, UEA, and initial zoning 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Comprehensive Plan Consistency Statement for 1307 Old Oxford Road
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. Separate statutory consistency statement motion.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the main approval on 1307 Old Oxford Road, Council voted on the separate required consistency statement affirming the Industrial Light zoning aligns with the Comprehensive Plan future land use designation. The motion was moved, seconded, and approved 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 2 (Pulled from Consent): Acceptance of Crime Statistics Performance Audit (June 2014)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent. Mayor Bell committed to passing Peterson's juvenile jail concerns to the Sheriff.
votes.discussion_detail: Speaker Victoria Peterson pulled Item 2 to argue the crime statistics audit lacked demographic and youth arrest breakdowns, reporting that Sheriff's data showed 26 youth under age 18 in the Durham County Jail—mostly African American—without educational services in violation of federal mandates. City Manager Tom Bonfield and Audit Services Director Germaine Brewington clarified that the audit's scope was specifically to verify internal controls, accuracy, and completeness of crime statistics reporting once entered into the system rather than arrest demographics. Mayor Bell thanked Peterson and committed to passing her concerns to the Sheriff, and Council accepted the audit report 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 9 (Pulled from Consent): Agreement with Time Warner Cable Business Class for Metropolitan Area Network Services
votes.notes: Eugene Brown excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Speaker Victoria Peterson pulled Item 9 to criticize Time Warner Cable for failing to hire trained Durham residents with criminal records and for reporting statewide rather than Durham-specific African American hiring figures after receiving city contracts. Mayor Bill Bell noted the Equal Opportunity/Equity Assurance Department verified compliance with Durham's equal opportunity ordinance, and Council Member Steve Schewel pointed out that 51% of the 1,500-1,800 employees in Time Warner's Triangle Business Unit were African American. Council approved the contract 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 7, 2014 Durham City Council Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell presided and all formal Council votes were unanimous—with no split or contested votes—including an excused absence for the following Monday's meeting, acceptance of the City Manager's removal of Item 24, a 7-0 appointment of Chris Tullo to the Homeless Services Advisory Committee, and setting the regular meeting agenda. During Citizens' Matters, resident Ms. Lear sought city relief for a collapsed 170-foot private stormwater pipe causing an eight-foot-deep sinkhole 25 feet from her home, though staff explained the site was ineligible for the Private Drainage Assistance Program until it imminently threatened the structure or primary ingress/egress; a second resident, June Forte, requested an ordinance banning or regulating invasive running bamboo. Council members questioned a water-only utility extension at 602 Pleasant Drive without annexation (Item 5), debated Chapter 62 right-of-way maintenance and semi-permanent non-commercial signage rules (Item 6), and reviewed Community Development funding recommendations to preserve existing affordable rental housing including $200,000 in capital improvements for a 20-unit DCLT townhouse property on Rock Street (Item 12).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence, Priority Items, and Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order with Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel answering roll call (Eddie Davis absent). Council granted an excused absence for the following Monday's meeting and early departure from the session, unanimously accepted the City Manager's removal of Item 24, and pulled Items 4, 5, 6, 12, 13, 14, 15, and 23 while noting a math error in Item 8's memo.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: Private Stormwater Sinkhole (PDAP) and Running Bamboo Ordinance Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Homeowner Ms. Lear described a collapsed 170-foot private stormwater pipe installed prior to 1966 annexation carrying street runoff from Hope Valley Road and Brookwood Drive and creating a 12-foot-wide, 8-foot-deep sinkhole 25 feet from her house; staff confirmed it did not yet meet Private Drainage Assistance Program criteria because the structure or primary ingress/egress was not imminently threatened. Resident June Forte then urged Council to enact an ordinance restricting invasive running bamboo (Phyllostachys), citing northeastern municipal ordinances.

agenda_items.title: Audit Oversight, Pump Station Cost-Sharing, and Item 5: 602 Pleasant Drive Utility Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle section of the transcript, Council discussed Audit Services Oversight Committee tracking, a $200,000 city share (split equally with Durham County from water/sewer capital funds) for pump station upgrades, and public versus private sewer maintenance lines. On Item 5 (utility extension to 602 Pleasant Drive for water only), a member asked why the parcel one lot outside city limits was not being annexed; staff explained failed contaminated wells are exempt from mandatory annexation under city policy.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Chapter 62 Right-of-Way Ordinance Revisions and Signage Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained proposed Chapter 62 right-of-way revisions—five years in development—noting that existing rules require a $200 Council license agreement just to plant annuals around a mailbox while restricting permanent plantings over 18 inches for pedestrian and motorist sightlines. Council members also urged staff and the City Attorney to address semi-permanent non-commercial signs placed in public rights-of-way and on City Hall property.

agenda_items.title: Item 12: Preservation of Existing Affordable Rental Housing Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development presented recommendations to award preservation loans for existing affordable rental housing, including $200,000 in capital improvements (roof replacement, retaining wall, and parking lot resurfacing) for a 20-unit DCLT townhouse development on Rock Street. Staff confirmed loan proceeds would be disbursed on a reimbursement basis upon receipt of trade contractor invoices.

agenda_items.title: Committee Appointment and Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The clerk reported that Chris Tullo received seven votes for the Homeless Services Advisory Committee. Council unanimously set the next regular meeting agenda with consent items 1–11, GBA public hearings 14–19, and disposed items 12 and 23.

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absence for Next Monday's Council Meeting and Early Departure
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote without opposition. Mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved excused absence request for the upcoming Monday City Council meeting and early departure from the August 7 work session.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items (Remove Item 24)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote. Mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Removed Item 24, which had been listed inadvertently on the agenda.

votes.item_title: Homeless Services Advisory Committee Appointment (Chris Tullo)
votes.notes: Unanimous 7-0 ballot tally across all seven seated Council members.
votes.discussion_detail: Clerk announced Chris Tullo received seven votes for the Homeless Services Advisory Committee.

votes.item_title: Set Regular City Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote. Mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Placed consent items 1–11 (clarifying Item 1 stayed on consent), GBA public hearings 14–19, and disposed items 12 and 23.
