meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting August 4, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council voted 5-2—with Council Members Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel dissenting—to approve the Harmony Road II zoning revisions (Z1400008), removing 2006 trail-connection commitments to Woodcroft in exchange for a $75,000 Chamberlain neighborhood recreation fund after Woodcroft refused an off-site easement. Council unanimously approved UDO technical text amendments (TC1300001), the 2919 Fayetteville Street rezoning (Z1400003), the consent agenda, and a pulled neighborhood parking permit signage item (Item 31), and elected board appointees to the Cultural Advisory Board, Planning Commission, and Human Relations Commission by written ballot.

agenda_items.title: National Night Out Proclamation & Fill the Bus Campaign
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented a proclamation to Police Chief Jose Lopez recognizing the 31st annual National Night Out on August 5, 2014, followed by remarks on the 25-site Fill the Bus school supplies drive.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Excluding Pulled Item 31)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council adopted the consent agenda excluding Item 31 (pulled by Eddie Davis and Linda Brown), including May 5 minutes, Homeless Services Advisory Committee appointment, June 2014 Crime Statistics Performance Audit, Verizon Wireless cell tower lease, Planning FY15 Work Program, NCSU stormwater retrofit project, Water Management on-call contracts, and the Downtown Loop waterline replacement contract.

agenda_items.title: Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment — Technical Changes (TC1300001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning's Michael Stock presented TC1300001 containing state/federal compliance updates, technical corrections, and clarifications to discretionary review standards (recommended 11-0 by the Planning Commission). With no public speakers, Council adopted the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 2919 Fayetteville Street (Z1400003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Steve Medlin presented Z1400003 to rezone 1.409 acres between Fayetteville Street Elementary School and the American Tobacco Trail from Office-Institutional to Commercial Neighborhood (recommended 10-0 by the Planning Commission). With no public speakers, Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — Harmony Road II Revisions (Z1400008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Standard Pacific (represented by Patrick Byker) requested removing 2006 committed elements requiring an off-site asphalt trail to Woodcroft and an on-site mulch trail because Woodcroft Community Association refused an easement, proposing instead a $75,000 Chamberlain recreation fund (net of legal/rezoning costs). Council Members Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel voted no to protect greenway connectivity and Safe Routes to School, while the 5-member majority approved the revisions citing Woodcroft's refusal and Chamberlain residents' support.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Residential Permit Parking Signage (Linda Brown)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Linda Brown opposed annual city parking decals and sign restrictions affecting residents with steep driveways and student relatives; Council Members Steve Schewel and Diane Catotti noted she had withdrawn her opposition at the prior work session and Council approved the item 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Ballot Appointments: Cultural Advisory Board, Planning Commission, and Human Relations Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment from Rafiq Zaidi on the Human Relations Commission appointment and Mayor Bell's defense of reappointing members with near-100% attendance, the City Clerk announced the ballot winners: Tess O'Connor (Cultural Advisory Board, 5 votes), Brian Buzby (Planning Commission, 5 votes), and Diane Standaert (Human Relations Commission, 4 votes).

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda Adoption (excluding pulled Item 31)
votes.notes: Item 31 was pulled by Council Member Eddie Davis and speaker Linda Brown.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell read through the consent agenda items, including May 5, 2014 minutes, Homeless Services Advisory Committee appointment, June 2014 Crime Statistics Performance Audit, Verizon Wireless cell tower lease, Planning Department FY 2015 Work Program, NCSU stormwater retrofit project, Water Management on-call master service agreements, and the Downtown Loop waterline replacement contract with J.F. Wilkerson Contracting Company. Item 31 was pulled for separate discussion. The remaining consent agenda passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 36: Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment — Technical Changes (TC1300001)
votes.notes: Recommended 11-0 by the Planning Commission on May 13, 2014.
votes.discussion_detail: Michael Stock of the Planning Department presented UDO text amendment TC1300001, grouping technical changes into three categories: state/federal compliance updates, technical corrections and codifications, and clarifications to discretionary review standards previously adopted under TC1100007. The Planning Commission had recommended approval 11-0. With no council questions and no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved TC1300001 by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Item 37: Zoning Map Change — 2919 Fayetteville Street (Z1400003)
votes.notes: Rezones 1.409 acres from Office-Institutional to Commercial Neighborhood; recommended 10-0 by Planning Commission on June 10, 2014.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Steve Medlin presented Z1400003, a request to rezone 1.409 acres at 2919 Fayetteville Street between Fayetteville Street Elementary School and the American Tobacco Trail from Office-Institutional to Commercial Neighborhood without an attached development plan, to allow retail uses such as a laundromat. Staff found the request consistent with the Comprehensive Plan commercial future land use designation, and the Planning Commission recommended approval 10-0. With no public speakers, Council voted 7-0 to approve.

votes.item_title: Item 38: Zoning Map Change — Harmony Road II Revisions (Z1400008)
votes.notes: Removes 2006 committed elements for off-site Woodcroft asphalt trail and on-site mulch trail while modifying timing triggers on remaining commitments.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Steve Medlin and Standard Pacific attorney Patrick Byker presented Z1400008 to remove 2006 committed elements requiring an off-site asphalt trail connecting the 185-unit Chamberlain/Harmony Road II subdivision to the Woodcroft trail network and an on-site southern mulch trail, after Woodcroft's Community Association refused all proposed easements over a year of talks. Instead, Standard Pacific signed a private agreement with seven Chamberlain residents to spend the $75,000 trail budget (less rezoning/legal/consulting costs) on Chamberlain common-area recreation improvements. Council Member Don Moffitt reluctantly supported the change on grounds that off-site commitments should not be required, and Mayor Bell and Eugene Brown cited Woodcroft's refusal and Chamberlain neighbors' support. Council Members Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel dissented (5-2), arguing that decommitting the trail sacrificed a vital off-road Safe Route to Southwest Elementary School and future Third Fork Creek Trail connection.

votes.item_title: Item 31 (Pulled from Consent): Neighborhood Permit Parking Signage
votes.notes: Pulled by Council Member Eddie Davis and speaker Linda Brown.
votes.discussion_detail: Resident Linda Brown addressed Item 31, objecting to annual city parking decal requirements and signage restrictions that she said burdened residents with steep driveways and her niece attending NCCU, while noting another neighbor (Linda Hunt) also had concerns. Council Members Steve Schewel and Diane Catotti pointed out that Brown had withdrawn her opposition at the earlier work session, prompting Council to proceed with the item. Following brief comments, Council approved Item 31 by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Ballot Appointments: Cultural Advisory Board, Planning Commission, and Human Relations Commission
votes.notes: Written ballot results read by City Clerk: Tess O'Connor (5 votes, Cultural Advisory Board); Brian Buzby (5 votes, Planning Commission); Diane Standaert (4 votes, Human Relations Commission). Clerk confirmed the ballots themselves constituted the formal vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Council members completed written ballots earlier in the meeting for vacancies on the Durham Cultural Advisory Board, Durham Planning Commission, and Human Relations Commission. Prior to the tally announcement, speaker Rafiq Zaidi commented on the Human Relations Commission appointment, and Mayor Bill Bell explained on the record that he voted to reappoint the incumbent (Diane Standaert) because she was eligible for a second term and had nearly 100% attendance rather than because of her policy stance. The City Clerk announced the winning totals—Tess O'Connor (5 votes), Brian Buzby (5 votes), and Diane Standaert (4 votes)—and confirmed no separate roll-call motion was required.

disagreements.issue: Decommitting Trail Connections in Harmony Road II / Chamberlain Subdivision (Z1400008)
disagreements.summary: Council split 5-2 over whether to release Standard Pacific from a 2006 committed element to build an asphalt trail connecting Chamberlain to Woodcroft's trail system and a southern mulch trail.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve removing the trail commitments because Woodcroft refused an off-site easement and Chamberlain residents negotiated a $75,000 recreation fund compromise.
side_a_arguments: Woodcroft Community Association formally rejected four to six proposed alignments across its private property.
Chamberlain residents agreed to redirect the $75,000 trail budget (net of legal/consulting costs) toward neighborhood recreation amenities.
Existing zoning lacked a timing trigger, and off-site easements beyond a developer's property boundary should not be enforced.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose decommitting the trails in order to preserve critical off-road pedestrian/bicycle connectivity to Southwest Elementary School and the Third Fork Creek Trail.
side_b_arguments: BPAC and residents rely on off-road trail links rather than forcing children onto city streets.
Removing the developer's commitment pushes the eventual cost of completing the Third Fork Creek tributary trail onto city taxpayers.
Woodcroft itself benefited from visionary trails, and the developer should pursue another alignment (such as toward Brindhurst/Tall Oaks) or mediation.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 5-2 (Catotti and Schewel voting no), removing the trail commitments.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the July 24, 2014 Durham City Council Work Session—opened while Mayor Bill Bell was en route, with Bell presiding upon arrival and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden and Council Member Don Moffitt excused—Council unanimously set the upcoming meeting agenda by voice vote and conducted a 3-2 split tie-breaker ballot for the Durham Cultural Advisory Board (Item 3), where Dale received three votes and Diane Standart received two votes (with individual Council members' written ballots not announced in the transcript). Members referred Item 7 (Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners) and another board appointment back to expand minority applicant outreach, questioned stark underrepresentation of African American workers at two city contractors, and heard Citizens' Matters remarks on water fluoridation and Rosewood Street student parking and Durham Tech GoPass transit access. On the Vermillion affordable housing project (Item 34), Council pressed the developer on deferred developer-fee adjustments and the absence of pre-award soil borings, expressing conditional support pending staff review of site costs. Planning staff also presented the long-term Downtown Open Space Plan (Item 35), proposing UDO private open-space requirements on sites over four acres and impact-fee funding, while the City Manager clarified that a recent TTA bus incident involved no explosion or bus damage.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Priority Items, and Board Referrals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The work session opened with Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden and Council Member Don Moffitt absent (already excused) and Mayor Bill Bell arriving shortly; Council Member Eugene Brown introduced his nephew Nick Brown, a Teach for America corps member. The City Manager removed Item 39 (citizen speaker absent) and noted completion of summer interior renovations at the Armory, while Council members referred a 19-applicant board slate and Item 7 (Durham Housing Authority Board) back to solicit additional minority applicants.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Contractor Workforce Diversity, and Citizens' Matters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled Items 31 (Rosewood Street controlled parking), 33 (Downtown Loop waterline public notice), and 38 (Herndon Road rezoning Z140008, requesting a clearer map and neighborhood letters), and heard Tamaya Parish (Item 40) opposing fluoridated water. Members also expressed dismay over contractor workforce data showing zero African American employees at a 40-employee Raleigh vendor and only one among 265 employees on the SCBA contract, asking whether Council should send letters to contractors.

agenda_items.title: Item 31: Rosewood Street Controlled Parking Residential Area and GoPass Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Rosewood Street resident Linda Brandon stated she disliked the appearance of controlled parking signs but urged Council to help nearby students obtain Durham Tech GoPass transit passes similar to Duke and NC State. Speaker Mr. Poole also addressed the 1300–1400 Rosewood Street parking petition and recommended mailed warning/citation notification practices.

agenda_items.title: Item 34: Vermillion Affordable Housing Project Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, Council questioned the Vermillion developer regarding a $54,000 adjustment (from $139,000 to $193,000) aimed at reducing the deferred developer fee to zero and criticized relying on past estimates without pre-award contractor site visits or soil borings prior to the tax-credit award. Staff confirmed they had not yet reviewed the site-cost estimates, and a Council member indicated conditional support subject to seeing more site-cost detail.

agenda_items.title: Item 35: Downtown Open Space Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the non-binding long-term Downtown Open Space Plan balancing civic gathering plazas and green spaces along the East Coast Greenway, proposing a UDO text amendment for private open space on sites larger than four acres and earmarking Parks and Recreation impact fees downtown. Council members emphasized two-waying the downtown loop to make parks accessible and inquired about implementation timeframes and future east-downtown open space.

agenda_items.title: Board Ballots, Agenda Setting, TTA Bus Incident Update, and 605 West Tour
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In a 3-2 tie-breaker ballot for the Durham Cultural Advisory Board (Item 3), Dale received three votes and Diane Standart received two votes; Council then unanimously set the regular agenda (consent items 2, 4, 6, and 10–33; GBA items 3, 8, and 9; GBA public hearings 36–38; and referred-back items 5 and 7). Finally, the City Manager clarified that two of three suspects had surrendered in a TTA bus incident that involved no explosion or bus damage, and members praised the newly opened 605 West apartment complex.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 3-2 (Cultural Advisory Board tie-breaker); Passed (Unanimous agenda)

votes.item_title: Durham Cultural Advisory Board Appointment Tie-Breaker Ballot (Item 3: Dale vs. Diane Standart)
votes.notes: Split 3-2 written/secret appointment ballot tally reported by the clerk; individual Council members' ballot choices were not announced in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Runoff ballot between two candidates who previously tied with three votes each: Dale received 3 votes and Diane Standart received 2 votes among the five members present (Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden and Council Member Don Moffitt had excused absences).

votes.item_title: Set Regular City Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote without opposition. Mover and seconder were not identified by name.
votes.discussion_detail: Set consent items 2, 4, 6, and 10–33; GBA items 3, 8, and 9; GBA public hearings 36–38; and referred-back items 5 and 7.

disagreements.issue: Durham Cultural Advisory Board Appointment Tie-Breaker (Item 3)
disagreements.summary: In a tie-breaker runoff ballot between two candidates who had tied with three votes each, Council split 3-2 with three votes for Dale and two votes for Diane Standart.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support Dale for Cultural Advisory Board (3 votes)
side_a_arguments: Three Council members cast tie-breaker ballots for Dale.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support Diane Standart for Cultural Advisory Board (2 votes)
side_b_arguments: Two Council members cast tie-breaker ballots for Diane Standart.
disagreements.resolution: Dale received 3 votes to Diane Standart's 2 votes among the five participating Council members (with Cora Cole-McFadden and Don Moffitt absent); individual ballot choices were not announced in the transcript.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting June 16, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: In a pivotal budget meeting, the Durham City Council voted 4-3 on a substitute motion by Steve Schewel (with Bell, Brown, and Cole-McFadden dissenting) to repeal the $1.80/month solid waste collection fee and replace it with a property tax increase, and then adopted the remaining FY 2014-15 budget and CIP ordinances 6-1 (with Eugene Brown dissenting over the final budget's inclusion of the fee repeal). Council also unanimously approved a $100,000 incentive grant for Reinvestment Partners' North Mangum Street food hub, the New Hope Church Transportation Special Use Permit and major site plan, a $74,985 Riverside on the Eno stormwater reimbursement, concealed-carry park ordinance updates conforming to state law, and accepted City Manager Tom Bonfield's 60-day review plan for the 44 HRC and CPRB police recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Parks & Recreation Month, DPD Forensics ISO Accreditation, Linda Bratcher Retirement, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented resolutions for Parks and Recreation Month and the Durham Police Department Forensics Services Division's ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation. Council members also recognized retiring staff member Linda Bratcher and praised Steve Schewel's Durham News op-ed on city taxes.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items (Item 33 Order, Supplemental Item 36, and HRC/CPRB Memo)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield moved Item 33 after Item 32, added supplemental Item 36 (Riverside on the Eno CIP ordinance amendment), and added his review/timeline memo on the Human Relations Commission and Civilian Police Review Board recommendations to the public record.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Excluding Pulled Items 10 and 11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda excluding Item 10 (FY15 Budget) and Item 11 (Concealed carry ordinance), encompassing numerous board/commission appointments, transportation grant amendments, WIA youth contracts, Downtown Durham MSD and DDI FY15 agreements, Balfour Beatty City Hall/Annex envelope CMAR contract, street repairs, Safe Routes to School near Fayetteville St. Elementary, and water tank/Jordan Lake contracts.

agenda_items.title: Amendment to City Code Section 38-21 (Alcoholic Beverages in Parks / McCown-Mangum House)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker presented an ordinance amendment permitting permitted alcohol consumption on the lawn of the McCown-Mangum House at West Point on the Eno Park consistent with other city park facilities. Speaker Victoria Peterson argued against allowing alcohol in parks, and Council approved the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Reinvestment Partners (902 N. Mangum St. Food Hub)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD's Grace DeShaniel presented a performance-based Neighborhood Revitalization Grant incentive of up to $100,000 to renovate 902 N. Mangum Street into a 4,500-square-foot community food hub with shared kitchen, cold storage, and nonprofit offices. No public speakers objected and Council approved 7-0.

agenda_items.title: New Hope Church Transportation Special Use Permit (T1400001) and Major Site Plan (D1300344)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In a quasi-judicial hearing, Council heard sworn testimony from Planning/Transportation staff and church attorney Jay Ferguson on New Hope Church's 27,034 sq ft sanctuary expansion (1,576 seats, 961 Sunday peak trips), questioning a 210-ft sidewalk gap and hearing acoustical consultant Noral Stewart detail sound encapsulation measures for neighbors across the American Tobacco Trail. Council approved the TSUP, TSUP order, and major site plan 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item: CIP Ordinance Amendment — Riverside on the Eno Failed Development Reimbursement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works' Robert Joyner explained that $74,985 in forfeited developer securities will reimburse a new developer to complete Riverside on the Eno stormwater facilities at zero cost to city taxpayers.

agenda_items.title: FY 2014–15 Budget and FY 2015–2020 CIP Adoption (Solid Waste Fee Repeal Severed)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council severed Item 10D and debated the $1.80/month solid waste collection fee at length before voting 4-3 on Steve Schewel's substitute Option 1 motion to repeal the fee in favor of property taxes (Bell, Brown, and Cole-McFadden voting no). Following comments from Victoria Peterson, Rafiq Zaidi, and Triangle Regional Film Commission's Rob Schoffer, Council adopted the remaining budget ordinances 6-1, with Eugene Brown voting no because the total budget incorporated the fee repeal.

agenda_items.title: Concealed Handguns at City Recreational Facilities (City Code Section 46-22 Amendment & Repeal of 46-23 to 46-27)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker explained that updates to Durham's code were strictly required to conform to N.C. General Assembly legislation limiting municipal authority to ban concealed carry in city parks outside specific buildings and playgrounds. After Victoria Peterson questioned the rules, Council approved the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Review & 60-Day Timeline Report on HRC and CPRB Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield read his memorandum establishing a 60-day team review of all 44 HRC and CPRB recommendations targeting an August 21 report. Twelve public speakers—including FADE, People's Alliance, FOP, National Latino Peace Officers Association, and Hispanic business owners—divided between demanding systemic action on racial profiling and defending Chief Jose Lopez, after which Council voted 7-0 to accept the manager's report.

votes.item_title: Addition of City Manager's Priority Items (Item 33 Order, Supplemental Item 36, and HRC/CPRB Memo)
votes.notes: Reordered Item 33 after Item 32, added Item 36 (Riverside on the Eno), and added HRC/CPRB timeline memo.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested three priority adjustments to the agenda: moving Item 33 (New Hope Church major site plan) after Item 32 (New Hope Church TSUP), adding supplemental Item 36 (Riverside on the Eno CIP ordinance amendment), and placing his review and timeline memorandum regarding the Human Relations Commission and Civilian Police Review Board recommendations on the public record. Mayor Bell clarified the memo item would be open for limited public comment later in the meeting rather than a formal public hearing. Council approved the priority items 7-0.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda Adoption (excluding pulled Items 10 and 11)
votes.notes: Item 10 (FY15 Budget/CIP) and Item 11 (Concealed handguns ordinance) were pulled for separate discussion.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell read the consent agenda items, spanning appointments to seven boards and commissions, transportation grant ordinances, workforce investment contracts, Downtown Durham MSD and DDI agreements, the City Hall/Annex envelope CMAR contract with Balfour Beatty, Carver Street and 2014 street repairs, Fayetteville Street Elementary Safe Routes to School, the Southeast Pressure Zone elevated water storage tank, and Jordan Lake Partnership work. Items 10 and 11 were pulled from consent. The remaining consent docket was moved, seconded, and passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 35: Amendment to City Code Section 38-21 (Alcoholic Beverages in Public Buildings and Parks)
votes.notes: Clarifies permit-required alcohol consumption on the lawn of the McCown-Mangum House at Eno Park.
votes.discussion_detail: City Attorney Patrick Baker presented an amendment to Section 38-21 clarifying where permitted alcoholic beverages may be consumed on the lawn of the McCown-Mangum House at Eno Park, aligning it with existing rules for other city park buildings and emphasizing that a permit is still required. Public speaker Victoria Peterson urged caution, arguing alcohol contributes to violent crimes and underage drinking. With no further council discussion, the Council approved the ordinance amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 31: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Reinvestment Partners ($100,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Grant)
votes.notes: Performance-based grant up to $100,000 for 902 N. Mangum St. food hub renovation in East Geer corridor.
votes.discussion_detail: Grace DeShaniel of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development presented a performance-based Neighborhood Revitalization Grant incentive of up to $100,000 for nonprofit Reinvestment Partners to renovate a 4,500-square-foot building at 902 North Mangum Street outside the downtown tier into a community food hub with shared commercial kitchen, cold storage, and nonprofit offices. No incentive funds are paid until project terms are met. With no council objections and no public speakers during the hearing, Council approved the agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 32: New Hope Church Transportation Special Use Permit (T1400001) — Approval with Conditions
votes.notes: Quasi-judicial hearing; subject to Transportation Management Plan mitigation conditions (traffic control officer and internal lot personnel).
votes.discussion_detail: In a quasi-judicial hearing with sworn witnesses and admitted Traffic Impact Analysis and Transportation Management Plan exhibits, Planning's Jacob Wiggins and Transportation's Bill Judge presented New Hope Church's TSUP request for a 750-seat expansion (1,576 total seats generating 961 Sunday peak-hour trips) at 7619 Fayetteville Road. Council Member Diane Catotti questioned a 210-foot sidewalk gap along the north parcel frontage, and church attorney Jay Ferguson and Planner Steve Medlin confirmed the sidewalk will be extended when future expansion reaches that residential parcel. No opponents testified, and Council voted 7-0 to approve the permit with staff's recommended conditions.

votes.item_title: Item 32: Adoption of Drafted Quasi-Judicial Order for New Hope Church TSUP (T1400001)
votes.notes: Formal written order required for quasi-judicial TSUP approval.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after voting to approve the New Hope Church Transportation Special Use Permit, staff reminded Council that a separate motion was required to adopt the formal written order as drafted by staff. The motion was moved, seconded, and approved 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 33: Major Site Plan — New Hope Church Building and Parking Addition (D1300344)
votes.notes: 27,034 sq ft addition and parking on 35.3 acres on Fayetteville Rd in Falls/Jordan Lake watershed.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Steve Medlin presented D1300344 for a 27,034-square-foot addition and parking expansion at New Hope Church, noting it met all UDO standards and Board of Adjustment conditions. Council Members Steve Schewel and Diane Catotti sought assurances that the larger sanctuary would resolve prior noise complaints from neighbors across the American Tobacco Trail; acoustical consultant Noral Stewart explained the sanctuary would be encapsulated by surrounding offices, corridors, a three-layer gypsum ceiling, and a six-foot higher perimeter roof barrier, and attorney Jay Ferguson noted neighbors' counsel had reviewed the plans and supported them at the Board of Adjustment. Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden praised the church's youth outreach, and Council approved the site plan 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 36 (Supplemental): CIP Ordinance Amendment — Riverside on the Eno Failed Development Reimbursement ($74,985)
votes.notes: Uses collected developer securities ($74,985) rather than city tax dollars to complete stormwater facilities.
votes.discussion_detail: Public Works' Robert Joyner presented the supplemental CIP ordinance amendment to allocate $74,985 in remaining developer securities collected between 2009 and 2011 for Riverside on the Eno so a new developer can finish the subdivision's stormwater facilities with zero city taxpayer funds. Council Members Diane Catotti and Don Moffitt thanked staff for moving the item quickly and saving city money. The ordinance amendment passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 10D (Severed): Substitute Motion Option 1 — Repeal $1.80/Month Solid Waste Fee & Adopt Commercial/Yard Waste Fee Schedules
votes.notes: Replaced the $1.80/month solid waste collection fee (~$1.4M) with equivalent property tax revenue while adjusting commercial tipping ($44/ton) and yard waste ($6/month) fees.
votes.discussion_detail: At Mayor Bell's request, Item 10D was severed from the FY 2014-15 budget for an intense policy debate. Council Member Steve Schewel moved Option 1 to repeal the $1.80/month ($21.60/year) solid waste collection fee and replace its ~$1.4 million revenue with property taxes, joined by Diane Catotti and Don Moffitt, who argued the flat fee was regressive (hurting homeowners below ~$370,000 and renters who pay $0 directly under property tax) and would require a 56% hike next year to cover an $800,000 projected shortfall. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Mayor Bill Bell, and Council Member Eugene Brown opposed repeal, arguing the solid waste enterprise fund already received $9.6 million in property tax subsidies, user fees akin to DATA bus fares were sound business practice, low-income residents had not complained, and adding ~0.6 cents to the tax rate risked giving Durham the highest municipal property tax rate in North Carolina. The substitute motion passed 4-3, with Bell, Brown, and Cole-McFadden voting no.

votes.item_title: Item 10 (Remaining Ordinances): Adoption of FY 2014–15 Budget and FY 2015–2020 Capital Improvement Plan
votes.notes: Electronic tally initially showed 7-0 at 02:07:19, but Eugene Brown immediately clarified on the record that he was voting NO on the overall budget because it included the solid waste fee repeal; Cora Cole-McFadden confirmed her Aye vote on the remaining ordinances while preserving her Nay on 10D.
votes.discussion_detail: Before voting on the remaining FY 2014-15 budget ordinances, Council heard public comments from Victoria Peterson (urging alternatives to the $94 million public safety budget), Rafiq Zaidi (demanding accountability on federal JAG informant funds), and Triangle Regional Film Commission's Rob Schoffer (requesting restoration of a $10,000 city grant). City Manager Bonfield offered to review film commission funding after recess, and Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden confirmed she supported the remaining ordinances while keeping her 'no' vote on the solid waste fee repeal. Although the electronic board initially registered 7-0, Council Member Eugene Brown immediately stated on the record that he was voting against the total budget (6-1) because it incorporated the rescission of the solid waste fee.

votes.item_title: Item 11 (Pulled from Consent): Amendment to City Code Section 46-22 and Repeal of Sections 46-23 to 46-27 (Concealed Carry in Parks)
votes.notes: Conforms Durham City Code to N.C. General Assembly preemption on concealed handguns in municipal parks.
votes.discussion_detail: Speaker Victoria Peterson pulled Item 11 to ask City Attorney Patrick Baker whether residents would still be allowed to carry concealed handguns in parks and asked for county jail detention statistics for Durham Police arrests. Baker referred jail counts to the Sheriff's Office and explained that the ordinance update did not originate locally—rather, 2012-2013 state legislation restricted cities from prohibiting concealed weapons in parks outside specific buildings and playground structures, requiring Durham to conform its code to state law. Council approved the amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager's Review Plan and 60-Day Timeline on HRC and CPRB Recommendations
votes.notes: Sets ~60-day review period targeting the August 21 work session for response to all 44 HRC and CPRB recommendations.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield read his memorandum outlining a 60-day team review of the 34 HRC recommendations and 10 CPRB recommendations—consulting DPD, the City Attorney, peer cities, and advocacy groups—with a final report targeted for August 21. Twelve public speakers addressed the item: advocates (including Chris Tiffany, Rafiq Zaidi, Nancy Wilson, David Hall, Victoria Peterson, and Charlie Reese) urged immediate action on written vehicle search consent, complaint handling, and systemic racial disparities, while Hispanic business owners and FOP representative Hilton Cancel defended Chief Jose Lopez against calls for his removal. After Eugene Brown voiced support for the manager's letter, Council voted 7-0 to accept the report.

disagreements.issue: Repeal of the $1.80/Month Solid Waste Collection Fee vs. Property Tax Replacement (Item 10D & Final Budget)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 4-3 on repealing the $1.80/month solid waste collection fee and replacing its $1.4 million revenue with property taxes, leading Eugene Brown to vote no (6-1) on the final overall budget.
disagreements.side_a_position: Repeal the flat $1.80/month ($21.60/year) solid waste fee and fund the $1.4 million through the property tax rate.
side_a_arguments: A flat per-household fee is regressive, charging a $75,000 homeowner or low-income renter the same $21.60/year as a $500,000 homeowner.
Any homeowner below ~$370,000 in assessed value—and single-family/duplex renters who pay $0 directly under property tax—pays less under Option 1.
Keeping the fee would require a 56% fee hike next year to cover a projected $800,000 solid waste shortfall.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain the $1.80/month solid waste user fee to stabilize the solid waste enterprise fund and avoid raising property taxes.
side_b_arguments: The $20 million solid waste fund already receives $9.6 million in general-fund property tax subsidies from all property owners, including businesses and multi-family residents without city pickup.
Like DATA bus fares, a modest $1.80/month user fee for households receiving collection service is not regressive, and DSS assistance covers hardship cases.
Replacing the fee plus county/other increases risks giving Durham the highest municipal property tax rate among North Carolina's largest cities, hurting competitiveness.
disagreements.resolution: Option 1 repeal passed 4-3; the remaining FY 2014-15 budget ordinances then passed 6-1 with Eugene Brown dissenting because the final budget incorporated the fee repeal.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 5, 2014 Durham City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, Council Member Don Moffitt added an item clarifying ordinances governing alcoholic beverage consumption on the grounds of three city park facilities—including the fenced lawn around the Mangum House at West Point on the Eno—and recommended pulling Item 3 (Open Space and Trails Commission appointments) for further advertising. Under suspended rules, Council unanimously approved Item 13 (superseding Employment and Training Grant Project Ordinance #14470) after Office of Economic and Workforce Development staff explained the state-funded competitive business training grants would be contracted by July 10 for a 12-month period. Resident June Forsyth urged enforcement of City Code Section 26-183 to remove invasive bamboo spreading from city right-of-way onto Kent Street, and staff briefed Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden on Item 23, noting the city's benefits broker helped save approximately $32 million over the prior contract cycle by converting to a self-funded insurance program. Council unanimously accepted an additional closed-session litigation item (Developer Surety et al. v. City of Durham) and approved the upcoming regular meeting agenda with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:02 p.m., with Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden and Council Members Eugene Brown, Eddie Davis, and Don Moffitt answering roll call. Moffitt requested adding an ordinance clarification regarding alcoholic beverage consumption in city parks and recommended sending Item 3 (Open Space and Trails Commission appointments) back for further advertising, which Bell supported. Cole-McFadden reported attending a Hispanic construction contractors awards luncheon and presenting a mayoral proclamation.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items: Item 13 (Grant Ordinance #14470) and Closed Session Litigation Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested suspending the rules to vote today on Item 13 (Employment and Training 2013-2015 Grant Project Ordinance superseding Ordinance #14470), which Council deferred briefly to hear staff explanation. The City Attorney requested adding a closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for Developer Surety et al. v. City of Durham, which Council unanimously approved by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Clerk's Agenda Review and Citizen Matter (Item 34: Invasive Bamboo on Kent and Bivins Streets)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk read consent items 1–30, public hearings 31–33, and citizen matter Item 34, while Cole-McFadden flagged Item 23 for discussion. During Item 34 (00:09:49), resident June Forsyth of 1711 Kent Street told Council that Public Works had twice cut down invasive bamboo in the Forest Hills/Lakewood area without removing the roots, allowing regrowth that threatened her property and Kent Street traffic sightlines, and asked the city to enforce City Code Section 26-183.

agenda_items.title: Item 13: Employment and Training Grant Project Ordinance #14470
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Daryl Solomon of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development explained that Item 13 adds competitive state training grant funds awarded for Durham County businesses into the city budget, with contracts to be executed by July 10 for a 12-month training term. Council unanimously voted to suspend the rules and unanimously adopted the grant project ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Item 23: Benefits Consulting and Broker Services Selection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, staff reported that the city's benefits broker saved approximately $32 million over the prior three-to-four-year contract cycle by helping convert the city from a fully funded to a self-funded insurance program. Staff added that a one-year extension had been used to separate the broker's contract cycle from other benefits vendors.

agenda_items.title: Added Item: Alcoholic Beverage Consumption Ordinances in City Parks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Don Moffitt presented an ordinance clarification drafted with the City Attorney's Office and Parks and Recreation covering three park locations where alcohol may be consumed without a special permit, including the fenced lawn around the Mangum House at West Point on the Eno. Moffitt noted the clarification aligns ordinance text with existing practice and asked to place the item on the June 16 business agenda, which staff agreed to prepare.

agenda_items.title: Setting the June 16 Agenda and Transition to Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the consent agenda (Items 2, 4–12, and 14–30), General Business Agenda (Item 33 and new Item 35), and public hearings (Items 31–32), noting Items 13 and 34 were disposed of and Item 3 was referred back. Council then moved to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Add City Attorney Closed Session Item (Developer Surety et al. v. City of Durham)
votes.notes: Roll call at 00:00:16–00:00:24 recorded Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Davis, and Moffitt present; Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel were absent (Catotti had an excused absence approved on May 22).
votes.discussion_detail: Added closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding Developer Surety et al. v. City of Durham.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules for Item 13 (Employment and Training Grant Project Ordinance #14470)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote among the five members present at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended council rules to take immediate action on Item 13 following staff explanation from OEWD.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 13 (City of Durham Employment and Training 2013-2015 Grant Project Ordinance #14470)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote with no opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted superseding grant project ordinance #14470 adding state-awarded competitive business training funds to the city budget.

votes.item_title: Set the Regular Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set consent items 2, 4–12, and 14–30; GBA items 33 and new 35; public hearings 31–32; disposed of 13 and 34; referred Item 3 back.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting June 2, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: With Council Member Diane Catotti absent, the Durham City Council rejected a resolution approving recommendations of the Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS) on a 3-3 tie vote after Steve Schewel objected to proposals such as closing Dillard Street, then voted 6-0 merely to receive the TSS report. Council held its FY 2014-15 budget e-town hall and public hearing—receiving comments on broken sidewalks, Stonehill Estates street paving, and repealing the solid waste fee—and unanimously approved (6-0) the 2013 Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report, two street closings, the consent agenda (including receiving HRC racial profiling recommendations), and a resolution memorializing Dr. Maya Angelou.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions, Excused Absences for July 24 Work Session, and Addition of Dr. Maya Angelou Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eddie Davis honored pioneers Hortense McClinton and Kelly Bryant, Council voted 6-0 to excuse Davis and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden from the July 24 work session, and added supplemental Item 35 (resolution memorializing Dr. Maya Angelou) 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously adopted the consent agenda 6-0, including minutes, street acceptances, Phillips impact fee appeal, dedicated funding and grants audits, Ninth Street infrastructure agreement amendment, East End Connector right-of-way conveyance, FY15 benefits recommendations, four board/commission annual reports, Windmere Ridge reimbursement, telephone system improvement, Lanier Parking amendment, Erwin Rd lighting, water/wastewater contracts, and receiving the HRC recommendations on DPD racial profiling.

agenda_items.title: Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dan Jewell of Durham Area Designers urged Council to ensure TSS scenarios were treated strictly as conceptual and subject to project-specific studies and renewed public engagement. Council Member Steve Schewel opposed accepting the study's recommendations—citing the proposed closing of Dillard Street—and the approval resolution failed on a 3-3 tie before Schewel's motion merely to receive the report passed 6-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approval resolution failed 3-3; Motion to receive report passed 6-0 (Catotti absent)

agenda_items.title: FY 2014–15 Proposed Budget E-Town Hall and Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: WRAL's Ken Smith moderated an interactive e-town hall with Council answering resident questions on sidewalk funding ($100,000 repair budget), potholes/state vs. city streets, bike lanes, public safety, solid waste cuts, the half-cent parks maintenance tax, Long Meadow Pool's electrical safety closure, historic district staffing, the Mayor's poverty initiative, and youth employment. During the public hearing, speakers urged repealing the solid waste fee, paving Stonehill Estates, doubling sidewalk repair funding, and opposing tax hikes before Council closed the hearing and accepted comments 6-0.

agenda_items.title: 2013 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan (A1400002)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Aaron Cain presented the 2013 Comprehensive Plan EAR consisting of 54 edited or new policies and three county parcel future land use technical changes (endorsed 12-0 by the Planning Commission and adopted May 27 by County Commissioners). With no public speakers, Council adopted the EAR 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Street Closings: Unnamed Alley off Alley #12 (SC1400005) and Chaparro Drive (SC1300005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Pat Young presented two street closings: a 50-linear-foot portion of an unnamed alley east of Buchanan Blvd (requested by Julianne Darby, who explained why neighbors' garage access prevented closing the entire alley) and a 1,090-linear-foot portion of Chaparro Drive near Southpoint Mall requested by Hendrick Automotive Group. Both passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Memorializing Dr. Maya Angelou
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously adopted a supplemental resolution honoring the life and achievements of Dr. Maya Angelou, with Mayor Bell noting a memorial program at Wake Forest University.

votes.item_title: Procedural Motion: Excuse Absence of Council Member Eddie Davis from July 24 Work Session
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Following his remarks recognizing Hortense McClinton and Kelly Bryant, Council Member Eddie Davis requested an excused absence for the July 24, 2014 work session. The motion was moved, seconded, and approved 6-0 with Diane Catotti absent.

votes.item_title: Procedural Motion: Excuse Absence of Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden from July 24 Work Session
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting. Cole-McFadden noted she would be attending a national committee meeting in St. Paul, Minnesota on city business.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden requested an excused absence for the July 24, 2014 work session to attend a national committee meeting in St. Paul, Minnesota on city business. Council approved the excused absence 6-0 with Diane Catotti absent.

votes.item_title: Addition of City Clerk's Supplemental Item 35 (Resolution Memorializing Dr. Maya Angelou)
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: City Clerk D. Ann Gray requested adding supplemental Item 35, a resolution memorializing Dr. Maya Angelou, to the June 2 agenda. Council voted 6-0 to add the resolution, and Mayor Bell noted copies were on members' desks and asked staff to check on delivering it for a memorial program at Wake Forest University.

votes.item_title: Item 28: Resolution Approving Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS) Recommendations
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting. Electronic roll call failed on a 3-3 tie; Steve Schewel explicitly spoke and voted Nay while the remaining 5 present members (Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Davis, Moffitt) split 3-2 without individual votes read aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Dan Jewell, president of Durham Area Designers (DAD), addressed Item 28, urging Council to emphasize that the Durham Traffic Separation Study's limited scenarios were conceptual rather than recommended solutions and warning that some proposals could harm city livability unless subjected to immediate project-specific studies and public engagement. Council Member Steve Schewel argued against adopting the resolution—even with caveats—because accepting recommendations such as closing Dillard Street creates public expectations that those closures are settled policy, urging Council to merely receive the report instead. The motion to approve the resolution failed on a 3-3 tie vote with Diane Catotti absent.

votes.item_title: Item 28 (Subsequent Motion): Motion to Receive the Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS) Report
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting. Adopted after the resolution to approve TSS recommendations failed 3-3.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after the resolution approving the Durham Traffic Separation Study recommendations failed on a 3-3 tie, Council Member Steve Schewel moved that the Council simply receive the TSS report without endorsing its specific street closure recommendations. The motion was seconded and passed unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 29: Acceptance of Public Hearing Comments on Proposed FY 2014–15 City Budget
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting. ASR transcript misheard '6-0' as 'six to six' at 01:54:28.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the 60-minute e-town hall moderated by WRAL's Ken Smith, nine residents spoke during the formal budget public hearing: Charlie Reese (Durham People's Alliance) urged repealing the $1.80/month solid waste fee; Stephen Hopkins, Peter Skillern (Reinvestment Partners), former Council Member Larissa Sabol, and Kevin Armstrong called for doubling the $100,000 sidewalk repair budget and prioritizing ADA/redevelopment corridors; Gwen Silver and James O. Williams demanded city paving for Stonehill Estates' failed subdivision streets; Donald Bryson (Americans for Prosperity) opposed property tax increases; and Victoria Peterson advocated paid youth job-training stipends. Council members thanked residents and staff, and Mayor Bell noted the final budget vote was slated for June 16 before Council voted 6-0 to receive the comments.

votes.item_title: Item 30: 2013 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan (A1400002)
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting. ASR misheard '6-0' as 'six is the one' at 01:57:16. Adopts 54 policy updates and 3 county parcel FLUM technical changes.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Aaron Cain presented Case A1400002, the 2013 Evaluation and Assessment Report of the Durham Comprehensive Plan, covering 54 edited or new policy statements and three county parcel future land use map technical updates reflecting acquired agricultural and open-space easements (with zero BOCC FLUM amendments requiring rectification). The Planning Commission recommended approval 12-0 and the Board of County Commissioners adopted the EAR on May 27, 2014. With no public speakers, Council voted 6-0 to approve.

votes.item_title: Item 31: Street Closing — Unnamed Alley Perpendicular to Alley #12 (SC1400005)
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting. Closes 50-linear-foot terminal portion of alley east of Buchanan Blvd and south of Urban Ave.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Pat Young presented SC1400005, a request by Julianne Darby to close a 50-linear-foot terminal segment of an unnamed alley off Alley #12 near Buchanan Boulevard and Urban Avenue, noting no adverse agency impacts. Responding to Council Member Don Moffitt's question about why the entire short alley was not closed, Young and applicant Julianne Darby (705 Watts St.) explained that four neighboring homes south of her had paved and maintained the remaining two-thirds for garage access and closing it would cut off their garages. Moffitt moved approval, seconded, passing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 32: Street Closing — Chaparro Drive (SC1300005)
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting. Closes 1,090 linear feet west of Fayetteville Rd and south of Renaissance Pkwy for Hendrick Automotive Group.
votes.discussion_detail: Planner Pat Young presented SC1300005, an application by Hendrick Automotive Group to close a 1,090-linear-foot portion of Chaparro Drive adjacent to Southpoint Mall to facilitate automotive sales development. City, county, and utility reviewers identified no adverse impacts, and no public speakers appeared. Council closed the public hearing and approved the street closing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 35 (Supplemental): Resolution Memorializing Dr. Maya Angelou
votes.notes: Diane Catotti absent from meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: As the final agenda action, Council took up supplemental Item 35, the resolution memorializing Dr. Maya Angelou. The motion was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously 6-0 with Diane Catotti absent.

disagreements.issue: Acceptance vs. Mere Receipt of the Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS) Recommendations (Item 28)
disagreements.summary: Council tied 3-3 on adopting a resolution accepting the Durham Traffic Separation Study recommendations, then voted 6-0 merely to receive the report without endorsing its conceptual street closures.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the staff-recommended resolution accepting the TSS report with caveats requiring future project-specific studies and public input.
side_a_arguments: The resolution explicitly conditioned any implementation on subsequent project-specific studies, public engagement, and City Council approval.
Accepting the final report concluded the study phase while preserving Council veto power over individual rail crossings.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject the approval resolution and merely receive the report so conceptual closures like Dillard Street are not treated as adopted city policy.
side_b_arguments: Accepting recommendations lacking broad community support creates an expectation that projects like closing Dillard Street are moving forward.
Durham Area Designers noted the limited scenarios evaluated were conceptual at best and potentially damaging to downtown livability.
disagreements.resolution: The resolution accepting the TSS recommendations failed on a 3-3 tie (Diane Catotti absent), and Steve Schewel's motion merely to receive the report passed 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Preliminary FY 2014-2015 Budget Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the May 29, 2014 preliminary FY 2014-2015 budget work session to order, with staff distributing requested schedules on comparative per-capita budgets and property tax categories before departmental presentations. Department of Water Management Director John Grilly presented the proposed FY 2015 budget, requesting four new FTEs (one utility engineer for development review and three plant maintenance positions to support upcoming pump and lift stations), highlighting over 5,400 toilet rebates, methane energy reuse, monthly billing transitions, and a $200,000 customer hardship fund, while City-County Planning Director Steve Medlin reported his department was returning to full staffing without adding positions. Following a middle transcript gap, staff briefed Council on a national performance-data pilot and the biennial employee opinion survey requiring departmental action plans for scores below 70%. Council members and staff concluded by scheduling a brief June 5 budget wrap-up session and listing flagged items for final resolution—including an estimated $200,000 FY 2015 (and $2.9 million FY 2016) privilege license revenue loss from state legislation, $100,000 earmarked in fund balance for Made in Durham, $25,000 for the Golden Belt historic district overlay, Sister Cities funding, and public art funding—with no formal votes taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Requested Budget Schedules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the budget work session to order, and the City Manager acknowledged a prominent recent national loss before reviewing two schedules requested the previous day. Staff noted a comparative budget-to-population calculation had been distributed and explained that the property tax category schedule could not yet break out single-family versus multifamily residential parcels from the tax collector's data.

agenda_items.title: Department of Water Management FY 2014-2015 Proposed Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director John Grilly, assistant directors including Vicki Westbrook, and utility finance manager Martha Ziggler presented Water Management's FY 2015 budget, proposing to shift one wastewater position to customer billing and add four new FTEs—one utility engineer for development review and three plant maintenance staff to service 63 existing lift stations plus 10–15 expected additions. Staff also reviewed conservation metrics (over 5,400 toilet rebates), methane reuse at wastewater sites, keeping tier-one water rates low for fixed- and low-income residents, a $200,000 hardship bill-forgiveness fund, monthly billing expansion, and IVR payment upgrades.

agenda_items.title: City-County Planning Department FY 2014-2015 Proposed Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin and assistant directors Pat Young and Keith Lott opened their FY 2015 budget presentation, reporting no proposed changes to departmental structure or headcount and noting the hiring of a new senior planner in development review restored full staffing before a transcript truncation gap.

agenda_items.title: Performance Pilot, Employee Opinion Survey, and Flagged Budget Wrap-Up Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After the transcript gap, staff briefed Council on joining a national performance-data pilot and administering the biennial employee opinion survey, under which departments scoring below 70% in communication or satisfaction must prepare action plans. Council and staff then agreed to meet briefly at 11:00 a.m. the following Thursday before the work session to resolve flagged items ahead of June 16 adoption, including a projected $200,000 FY 2015 ($2.9 million FY 2016) state privilege license revenue loss, $100,000 fund-balance earmark for Made in Durham, $25,000 for Golden Belt historic district overlay, $7,500 vs. $15,000 for Sister Cities, and public art funding.

meetings.title: City Council Preliminary FY 2014-2015 Budget Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the May 28, 2014 preliminary FY 2014-2015 budget work session to order while Mayor Bill Bell was delayed, turning the session over to the City Manager after roll call. Budget Director Bertha Johnson presented the revenue outlook, citing 2.9% budgeted real property growth, uncertainty from the state's tax-and-tag vehicle tax transition, unpredictable sales tax collections, general fund personal services comprising 75% of appropriations (~$84 million for public safety vs. ~$6 million for governance), and potential immediate FY 2015 impacts from a N.C. Senate proposal barring privilege licenses on out-of-city businesses. Following a middle transcript gap, Transportation staff reviewed the passenger-vehicle-for-hire ordinance and noted City Attorney review with the UNC School of Government regarding unregulated ride-share services Lyft and Uber, proposed 450 new LED streetlights, detailed parking study enforcement and overnight parking-deck security patrols, and outlined bus service expansions (Routes 15 and 16 and commuter routes to the Duke/VA Employment Center) funded by the half-cent sales tax alongside Duke-DATA-TTA integration talks. No formal policy votes were taken during the session before adjourning to the following morning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Schedule Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the special budget work session to order while Mayor Bill Bell was running late, asked the clerk to call roll, and turned the meeting over to the City Manager, who noted Solid Waste had been rescheduled to the next afternoon.

agenda_items.title: FY 2014-2015 Revenue Presentation and Privilege License Legislation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson outlined revenue assumptions including 2.9% real property tax growth, tax-and-tag vehicle collection uncertainty, sales tax volatility, and 75% of general fund appropriations supporting personal services (with ~$84 million in public safety and ~$6 million in governance). Council and staff discussed non-profit/Duke tax-exempt sales tax refunds and an active N.C. Senate bill that would immediately end privilege license taxation of out-of-city businesses.

agenda_items.title: Department of Transportation Budget: For-Hire Vehicles, Streetlights, and Parking
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a transcript truncation gap, Transportation staff discussed expanding vehicle-for-hire permitting to shuttles and limousines and reported that the City Attorney was consulting the UNC School of Government on legal options regarding unregulated Lyft and Uber operations. Staff also reviewed traffic signal workloads, Long-Range Transportation Plan data collection, 450 proposed LED streetlights, paid parking and expanded enforcement on 9th Street and downtown, overnight parking-deck security patrols, and lowering the bus on-time target to a realistic 84–85% en route to 90%.

agenda_items.title: Transit Service Expansions, Duke-DATA-TTA Integration, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined transit expansions funded by the half-cent sales tax and motor vehicle fee, including Route 15 (TW Alexander to Brier Creek), Route 16 (July 1), and Bus and Rail Investment Plan commuter routes from North and South Durham to the Duke/VA Employment Center (target April 1), alongside cost-sharing talks among Duke, DATA, and TTA. A ~$9,355,000 property-tax subsidy / Solid Waste fee item was briefly noted just before the session moved to adjourn until the following morning.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the May 22, 2014 Durham City Council Work Session, during which Council unanimously suspended the rules to approve Item 4 (the 2014 Short Legislative Session Agenda) ahead of the next morning's legislative breakfast and unanimously excused Council Member Diane Catotti's upcoming June 2–5 absences. Council reviewed consent and public hearing items—including the 9th Street infrastructure amendment, Riddle/Buxton intersection project, and proposed FY 2015 budget hearing—and heard public remarks and council questions regarding employee health insurance plan changes and survey deadlines. After a middle transcript gap, Council held an extended review of Item 28, the Human Relations Commission (HRC) recommendations regarding allegations of racial bias and racial profiling by the Durham Police Department, with residents and council members (including Steve Schewel, Eddie Davis, and Mayor Bill Bell, who presided by that point) praising the HRC's work, requesting to see a three-member HRC minority report, criticizing police communication challenges, and directing the City Manager to return by June 16 with an initial plan and cost assessment for a comprehensive 60-to-90-day summer review. Council unanimously set the regular meeting agenda with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Action on Item 4 (2014 Short Legislative Session Agenda)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order, with Cole-McFadden, Diane Catotti, Eddie Davis, Don Moffitt, and Steve Schewel called during roll call. At the City Manager's request ahead of the next morning's legislative delegation breakfast, Council unanimously voted to suspend the rules for Item 4 (2014 Short Legislative Session Agenda).

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request, JCCPC Scheduling, and Approval of Item 4
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved Council Member Diane Catotti's excused absences for the June 2 Council meeting, June 4 JCCPC meeting, and June 5 work session, and discussed JCCPC summer scheduling. Council then unanimously approved Item 4 (2014 Short Legislative Session Agenda) by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Citizen Speakers, and Employee Health Insurance Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk read consent items 1–24, presentations 25–28, and public hearings 29–30, with members holding Item 17 and flagging questions on Items 7, 14/15, 19, and 30. Following citizen speakers—including a Social Security proclamation request and John Tarantino—Council discussed employee health insurance changes, asking whether Blue Cross Blue Shield could reopen a wellness survey window for roughly 600 non-participating employees and noting cost impacts of splitting employee-plus-spouse and employee-plus-child tiers.

agenda_items.title: Item 28: Human Relations Commission Recommendations on Police Racial Bias and Profiling Allegations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a transcript truncation gap, residents including Victoria Peterson spoke on police complaints and HRC recommendations. Council members—including Steve Schewel, Eddie Davis (referenced), and Mayor Bill Bell—commended HRC volunteers (Mr. Hart, Mr. Sabin) and staff, asked to review the three-member HRC minority report alongside the seven majority recommendations, criticized a 'bunker mentality' in police communications, and directed the City Manager to report back by June 16 with a work plan and cost implications for a full 60-to-90-day summer evaluation.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the consent agenda (Items 1–3, 5–19, and 21–24), General Business Agenda (Item 20), and GBA public hearings (Items 29–32), noting Item 4 was disposed of, and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules for Item 4 (2014 Short Legislative Session Agenda)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously; roll call at 00:00:55–00:01:05 confirmed Cole-McFadden, Catotti, Davis, and Schewel answering (Moffitt was called without a recorded verbal response; Bell arrived later in the meeting).
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules at the City Manager's request so Item 4 could be adopted ahead of the next morning's legislative delegation breakfast.

votes.item_title: Approve Excused Absence for Council Member Diane Catotti (June 2–5, 2014)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Granted Diane Catotti's request for excused absences from the June 2 City Council meeting, June 4 JCCPC meeting, and June 5 work session due to travel.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 4 (2014 Short Legislative Session Agenda)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the city's 2014 Short Legislative Session Agenda under suspended rules.

votes.item_title: Set the Regular Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously; Mayor Bill Bell was present and participating by 03:05:02 prior to agenda setting.
votes.discussion_detail: Set consent items 1–3, 5–19, and 21–24; GBA item 20; GBA public hearings 29–32; and noted Item 4 was disposed of.

meetings.title: Proposed Budget for Fiscal Year 2014-2015 for City of Durham, North Carolina
meetings.executive_summary: This video captures City Manager Tom Bonfield's formal presentation of the proposed $386.7 million Fiscal Year 2014-2015 City of Durham budget and FY 2015-2020 Capital Improvement Plan to Mayor Bill Bell and the City Council. The proposal featured a 1.29-cent property tax rate increase to 58.04 cents per $100 of assessed value to cover voter-approved debt service and absorb 16 police officer and 15 firefighter positions from expiring grants, alongside a return to differentiated pay-for-performance raises (averaging 3% for general employees and 3.5% for police and fire), a 7.5% stormwater rate increase, 3% water and sewer rate increases, and $1 million for street repaving. Mayor Bell noted that Council budget workshops would begin on Wednesday, May 28, ahead of a June 2 E-Town Hall.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Fiscal Year 2014-2015 Budget and Fiscal Year 2015-2020 Capital Improvement Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented the proposed FY 2014-2015 total budget of $386.7 million (up 2.7%) and general fund budget of $173.6 million (up 2.3%), recommending a 1.29-cent property tax increase (0.73 cents for voter-approved debt service and 0.56 cents for 31 previously grant-funded police and fire positions) while maintaining a 13.5% general fund balance reserve. The plan proposed returning to differentiated pay-for-performance increases averaging 3% for general staff and 3.5% for public safety, funding $93 million in capital improvement projects, increasing street repaving to $1 million, adding $400,000 for sidewalks, raising water/sewer rates 3% and stormwater rates 7.5%, and presenting a potential additional half-cent tax option for parks maintenance during upcoming workshops. Bonfield also highlighted fiber broadband readiness, Southside revitalization (132 rental units nearing completion and 19 of 48 home lots reserved), a $96,000 HUD fair housing grant, and a $9.6 million general fund subsidy to the solid waste fund.
